title: Managed processor invocations with portable isolation and durable recovery
description:
## Outcome
An application can execute registered native workloads on untrusted inputs through one Runledger-owned invocation path without implementing launch, timeout, cancellation, join, cleanup or retry coordination. Feasibility evidence selects the execution approach; a local-plus-custom-remote adapter pair is not predetermined. The same protected application contract must work in two materially different deployment models under explicit, verified prerequisites. No provider-specific topology is imposed on the application API.

## Scope and authority
This epic is the canonical cross-task decision record. Child Beads own delivery scope, acceptance, priority, status and native blocker edges. Stable T-01 through T-08 identifiers are retained in task titles and external references; there is no parallel Markdown backlog.

The requested work is planning. Implementation tasks remain open and unclaimed. Implementation includes native Runledger contracts/persistence/runtime, only the execution bindings required by the selected deployment models, a generic consumer and conformance evidence. The draft-PR workflow is authorized. Infrastructure provisioning, hosted deployment and publication require their own authorization; this planning epic does not authorize them. Do not modify the motivating application's active migration as part of this epic.

Ordinary handlers keep their existing supported contracts. The new protected processor path must not silently select a weaker backend. Unix-only scope remains; Linux and macOS controllers stay in scope, with unsupported local isolation capabilities explicitly rejected and remote execution available where verified.

## Evidence
Fact: source inspected at 74238a2dffe29aee681440c566d6bcb42e742e30. runledger/runledger-core/src/jobs/{handler,execution,status}.rs provide trusted handlers, live deadlines/progress and retry kinds. runledger/runledger-runtime/src/worker/execution.rs stops polling a handler after deadline or lease loss; it does not establish external-process termination.
Fact: runledger/README.md, Durable execution resources, and runledger/migrations/202607280004_job_execution_resources.up.sql define lease-scoped single-permit reservations released through job transitions/reaping. These cannot bound executions that survive their job lease.
Fact: native settlement lives in runledger/runledger-runtime/src/{settlement,task_group,supervisor}/. runledger/runledger-postgres/src/jobs/queue/{claim,reaper,lifecycle}.rs and associated directories own queue transitions; reuse them rather than adding a second queue.
Fact: an inspected upload-processing consumer's repair history repeatedly addressed disposable-container cleanup, parser/host failure attribution and bounded retries. Its unfinished migration replaced container launch with environment-cleared subprocesses. Source inspection is not executed isolation evidence; no defect-rate or final-consumer claim is made. This anonymized rationale is sufficient; another private checkout is not an implementation prerequisite.
Fact: crates/batter-sqlx/src/atomic/scope.rs exposes PgScopedSql::executor and explicitly permits SQL with irreversible effects such as COMMIT; boundary-loss detection is not rollback. The inspected regression source crates/batter-sqlx/tests/atomic_live/fail_fast_loss.rs exercises committed writes despite scope loss. runledger-postgres/src/atomic.rs reuses that capability, while jobs/queue/lifecycle/success.rs currently owns its own transaction. These sources were inspected, not executed, during this amendment.
Fact: runledger/README.md, Quick start, supports separate producer and worker processes sharing PostgreSQL. Hosting an existing trusted worker beside a proven local executor is a candidate deployment, not proof of processor isolation.
Inference: reusable execution ownership and isolation-binding contracts can remove this repeated application protocol, but backend support, operator burden and deployment assumptions must be demonstrated.
Existing related work: batter-44w, batter-gg8 and batter-0cp are completed foundations, not proof of this capability. batter-7g0 concerns diagnostic correlation and must not become an authority prerequisite.

## Verification and completion
All eight delivery tasks must meet their acceptance. The same representative registered native workload and hostile fixture corpus must execute through the two selected deployment models. A fake adapter, loopback transport or a second identical host alone is insufficient isolation or deployment-diversity evidence. Cover controller/runner death, delayed launch after cancellation, lease takeover, result/commit uncertainty, descendant escape attempts, resource/output exhaustion, credential/filesystem/network denial, current-authority rejection and upgrade/retention compatibility. Include fresh-agent implementation and modification exercises; label them proposed/unexecuted until recorded.

Use focused checks during each task and the repository's applicable complete backend verification before delivery. Record exact revisions, operating systems, backend versions, commands, prerequisites and results in the owning Bead. Update rustdoc/examples, relevant contracts, implemented-status rows, docs/references.md and verification input ownership when implementation lands. Do not present this planning session as runtime, Linux/macOS or hosted-CI verification.

## Rollout and recovery
Use additive migrations and versioned invocation/protocol/profile identifiers. Keep processor dispatch disabled until database guards and every active worker/reaper/admin writer that could claim, reap, replay, cancel or purge processor jobs are compatible or fenced out. Job-type filtering alone does not protect old reapers. Prefer a coordinated cutover when it meets deployment needs; mixed-version operation is not a goal by itself. Preserve legacy job semantics and test actual old/new binaries, including an old session/transaction resumed across activation, against the selected writer-exclusion policy.
Start with synthetic inputs. Stop new processor admission on containment; durably record stop intent, revoke further input access, reconcile outstanding invocations and retain their capacity/tombstones. Plaintext already delivered cannot be recalled. A failed job or expired lease does not prove stopped execution. Never clear an unresolved execution as a normal retry or delete applied schema/history for rollback. Disabling admission must leave a compatible recovery owner running.
Normal bounded shutdown may hand remote recovery to a durable owner only after acknowledged persistence and settlement of local users of dependencies. Report that handoff separately from remote termination; it is not a clean external-execution result.

## Risks and open decisions
T-01 owns the first protected profile, representative processor, deployment selection, failure assumptions, physical execution multiplicity, result-handoff strategy and operational cost. Compare separate native workers with local isolation, an existing managed executor, and a narrow remote runner on equal footing. Limit the comparison to those three topology families and actual mechanism proofs to at most two shortlisted choices; use one representative registered native workload plus hostile fixtures. A new remote service is justified only by a demonstrated trust/deployment need.
T-01 closure must record the chosen models, exact privileges/services/inventories and operating owner, an actionable uncertainty-recovery exercise, and the deployment tests required to establish the intended supported environments. It must revise D-07 and T-05/T-06 scope/edges to its findings before T-02 closes. It can choose a simpler topology without weakening the protected contract or removing deployment-diversity evidence. If no candidate meets the selected required profile, retain the blocker; do not invent a sandbox or silently weaken a guarantee.
T-02 closes only after the SQL capability boundary, result-copy ownership/acknowledgements, backend retry/multiplicity rules and a small compiling consumer are explicit. T-03 owns locking, reservations and writer activation. T-08 rehearses an already designed recovery procedure and records final deployment evidence. Application authorization, application-level result correctness, application content policy, external publication and forensic erasure remain outside library guarantees.
Strict no-overlap and workflow-lineage coverage remain the initial supported policy, with their availability cost recorded in D-05; they are not logical consequences of handling untrusted inputs. Accounted overlapping transformations or a direct-jobs-only scope are alternatives requiring an explicit contract/scope amendment, not implementation shortcuts.
The first safe delivery action is T-01; later implementation is conditional on its closure decisions. After T-02, persistence and the first execution binding can proceed independently when shared interfaces settle. Runtime follows persistence. The second deployment task depends on the first binding only if selected reuse requires it; record that edge before either dependent task starts. Consumer integration and final acceptance follow both deployment proofs.

## Planning validation
The original critical-profile structural check passed with eight tasks, no errors and no warnings. Earlier focused reviews repaired encrypted transport, distributed expiry, atomic application/native completion and workflow-lineage omissions. Two subsequent user-supplied reviews prompted this amendment: correct the trusted SQL boundary, make deployment selection evidence-led, expose executor multiplicity and result-handoff decisions, and bring operational recovery proof forward. Prior review closure is historical, not a claim that later findings were impossible.
The user authorized T-01 to replace the prescribed adapter pair when a simpler deployment approach preserves security and portability. The revised critical-profile structural check passed with eight tasks, zero errors and zero warnings. Tracker readback matched all intended fields: 15 blockers, eight parent links, no active blocking cycles, and only T-01 ready; all 196 unrelated records were unchanged. Shared manifests, Cargo.lock, SQLx foundation seams and generated metadata remain serialized integration surfaces. These are planning/source checks; runtime, isolation and hosted deployment evidence remains unexecuted.
design:
## Decisions and design
D-01 — Accepted planning direction: general managed processor invocations.
The contract owns execution of registered native workloads with bounded opaque inputs and results. Payload schemas, domain interpretation, intake/storage workflows and business authorization belong to downstream applications. Feasibility fixtures exercise execution requirements and do not define library-specific content types or domain processors.
The application supplies an authorized bounded input and interprets the result. Runledger owns registration, durable admission/identity, execution, deadline enforcement, result fencing, settlement and recovery. An adapter owns concrete execution/transport; deployment owns provisioning and enforcing external identity/network/storage configuration. Processors receive no database, key-store or orchestration authority. A trusted broker or native worker is distinct from the untrusted payload processor. A separate Runledger-specific remote service is optional.

D-02 — Accepted: one concrete, fail-closed initial profile; defer a general profile language.
T-01 must define the initial profile before evaluating mechanisms. Assume a fully compromised registered native executable. Name protected secrets, other inputs, broker/worker authority and host resources; allowed channels/files/egress; input/output, CPU, memory, process-count, scratch and duration bounds; and the exact controller/broker/host failure assumptions. Select only the confidentiality/disposal properties required for this first profile. Bind a registered processor/revision to that validated contract, with fresh per-invocation containment; reuse of compromised native processor state is deferred. Required unsupported or unknown properties reject before sensitive input release. An explicit unresolved outcome preserves failure evidence; it never counts as satisfying a requested hard resource or lifetime bound. Distinguish memory-only from encrypted ephemeral scratch, cooperative cancellation from executor-side lifetime enforcement, and process supervision from isolation. Deployment assumptions and evidence have provenance; a Rust witness is not proof of remote configuration. The application chooses a declared profile; adapters cannot weaken it. Processor executable/entrypoint and permitted options are fixed by trusted registration. Untrusted input/result fields cannot select commands, images, mounts, host paths or arbitrary fetch URLs; artifact descriptors are scoped capabilities, not unchecked path/URL strings.

D-03 — Accepted: library-owned phase order.
A canonical processor-job registration supplies trusted preparation and application callbacks around runtime-owned admission -> durable intent -> authorized input transfer -> execution -> candidate-result handoff -> required execution/scratch settlement -> fenced application and native completion -> candidate-result disposal. Preparation may reject without launching; authorize/audit immediately before plaintext transfer, and revalidate authority after any capacity/startup wait. Avoid holding plaintext while awaiting unbounded admission. Work factories are inert before polling/admission. T-01 selects one initial input/result-transfer approach: bounded native streams or explicitly scoped immutable artifact access. Do not build both without a demonstrated need, or persist raw bytes, reusable grants or presigned URLs as queue metadata.
Keep generic contracts free of storage/provider dependencies. Extend native persistence/runtime; keep mechanism-specific SDKs and tooling optional. The Batter adapter only integrates native startup/shutdown and reexports justified native APIs.

D-04 — Accepted: durable invocation identity and independent evidence.
Persist a stable execution identity linked to job/run/attempt, immutable input identity, processor/profile revision, backend binding, absolute durable expiry and bounded sanitized observations before launch. Never serialize a local Instant. Work budgets cannot grow on restart or through transport delay. Specify a trusted time source and conservative conversion to local monotonic clocks, an explicit tolerated skew bound and fail-closed behavior when expiry cannot be established. Name the trusted component that independently arms/enforces expiry and the allowed enforcement delay for each supported failure domain. Prove controller/broker loss while the processor environment remains alive; killing their shared host/container proves a different property. Cover restart/reboot, suspend/resume and clock rollback within the stated fault model. Settlement has its own bounded observation allowance without extending work authority.
Result receipt, accepted result, stop intent, stopped observation and required cleanup are separate facts. NotStarted, returned, rejected, failed and unresolved conditions need exhaustive handling. Returned output cannot authorize application/native success before required execution/scratch settlement and durable ownership of any retained result. Each reservation releases only on evidence for its own obligation; bounded candidate-result disposal may remain durably pending after application/native completion and must not be reported as complete cleanup. The runtime retains those obligations if the caller drops a waiter, ignores the result or returns success.
Backend start/observe/stop/recover operations have stable identity, bounded idempotency/retention and late-launch semantics. Reject conflicting same-identity requests. Cancellation must survive a delayed start, broker restart and identity reuse attempts. Not-found is conclusive only under the backend's absence/fencing guarantee. Retain uncertainty otherwise. Processor self-reported exit is not independent termination evidence.
A backend request/job identity is not assumed to identify exactly one physical execution. Before persistence design, T-01/T-02 must establish executor-internal retry/restart/replacement ownership, physical execution identities and aggregate admission, input grants and elapsed/resource budgets. The initial strict profile requires at most one active physical processor in its lineage; an executor that can launch an uncontrolled duplicate is unsupported even if its API retry count is zero. A bounded execution-group/overlap contract is a separate future decision, not an implicit reinterpretation of one reserved slot. Test replacement initiated by the substrate without another Runledger dispatch.

D-05 — Accepted: capacity and recovery outlive job leases.
Use native durable reservations associated with invocations, reconciled independently of the current job lease. Uncertain launches and possibly live executions remain accounted across retry, cancellation, dead-lettering, reaping and worker death. Define protected no-overlap over a stable native invocation lineage for one logical processor job/workflow step, preserved by direct replay and workflow recovery even when new job/run IDs are allocated. No replacement execution in that lineage while the previous one remains unresolved. Workflow active-key/resource release must consider outstanding processor invocations, not only live canceled leases. New unrelated roots are not globally deduplicated by content hash; applications use explicit resource/idempotency policy when they require cross-root exclusion. Bound outstanding unknown executions and admission waiters across replicas; do not add a general quota engine. Compute, sensitive scratch and retained candidate-result obligations may settle at different times and require separately bounded accounting. Retention/purge cannot cascade away unresolved records, reservations or late-launch tombstones.
Strict no-overlap is an explicit conservative first-release policy: it avoids introducing an overlapping-replay contract while preserving existing workflow resource/exclusion expectations. It can block a lineage indefinitely under uncertainty; T-01 must establish whether that availability cost and containment procedure are acceptable. Side-effect-free duplicates can be valid under another contract with complete aggregate accounting and fenced acceptance; they are not inherently a security defect, but are not enabled here. Workflow coverage is retained; omitting it requires explicit rejection of unsupported processor workflow compositions and a scope amendment.
Use the existing native recovery machinery. A remote runner may use native invocation persistence or its selected executor's durable inventory, but must not grow a second job queue, workflow engine or fleet manager. Recovery control is trusted; the untrusted processor has only the exact input/result channel. Reserve bounded control/reconciliation resources so saturated execution admission cannot prevent recovery. T-01 rehearses full-capacity loss of observability and identifies the responsible operator, real execution-domain identity, supported containment action and evidence permitting reuse. If that evidence is unavailable, expose quarantined/unavailable capacity; deleting rows or operator approval alone is not settlement evidence.
Retries require explicit replay policy, established prior-execution eligibility and finite attempt/elapsed limits. Adapter observations determine infrastructure failures; processor bytes cannot invent them. Indeterminate and deterministic resource-limit failures cannot open an unlimited alternative retry budget.

D-06 — Accepted: untrusted results and fenced application effects.
Bound and validate transport envelopes and output; bind them to invocation, input and processor/profile revision. Require authenticated encryption with peer/endpoint verification for every remote control, input and result hop; authentication alone is insufficient. Any buffered sensitive artifacts obey the selected confidentiality/retention profile. Authenticate narrowly scoped grants; consider replay, wrong audience, expiry, wrong-attempt results and metadata-service/ambient-credential access. Define the authorization linearization point and any online redemption/revocation check or bounded remaining validity of offline grants. Revocation does not recall delivered bytes or necessarily interrupt an already authorized stream.
T-01/T-02 must choose and encode candidate-result handoff semantics. Either retain a bounded recoverable result (or immutable reference) until durable acknowledgement/acceptance permits disposal, or explicitly allow loss and apply finite replay/reauthorization policy only after prior execution is settled. Identify the last recoverable copy and owner at each transfer, including controller death after delivery but before apply, domain rejection, acknowledgement loss and application-commit uncertainty. Processor scratch disposal and candidate-result disposal are different obligations. Apply/retention recovery must reconcile exact acceptance before garbage collection; exceeding retention cannot silently discard an unresolved required copy or create unbounded result storage.
Provide an owned native transaction scope that rechecks current run/attempt/execution authority after locking, then calls application SQL and records application acceptance, native job/attempt completion, events and workflow consequences in the same transaction. There is no acknowledged application commit followed by a separate success write. Expose reusable in-transaction native transitions through the existing owned SQLx foundation; do not call the current independently committing public success entrypoint from the callback or add a parallel transaction abstraction. Current domain authority is application-owned and checked in that same transaction. Duplicate applications must be idempotent or rejected; lost commit acknowledgement is reconciled from that exact invocation/acceptance identity before replay. The runtime must not repeat application SQL after reconciling an identified committed acceptance; the callback can run again after a confirmed rolled-back attempt under explicit retry policy. No owned connection/transaction or separately paired commit token is supplied on the canonical path. PgScopedSql exposes a query executor for trusted SQL; it cannot prevent explicit transaction-control SQL, direct manipulation of ledger tables, or effects through independently captured clients. Those are excluded escapes, not supported compositions or evidence of rollback when detected. T-02 must record this upstream/application trust boundary under ADR-010, demonstrate the explicit-COMMIT negative control, and name any minimal shared SQLx seam needed; do not build a SQL sandbox or weaken ordinary library-owned completion. Runledger performs no non-database execution/transport I/O while holding the application transaction. Arbitrary async callbacks can perform external I/O; those effects remain application-owned and outside the atomicity guarantee. Isolation and result authentication do not establish application-level result correctness, malware absence or arbitrary remote rollback.
Diagnostics use bounded codes and redacted reports; raw input/output/stderr are not automatic logs or durable results.

D-07 — Accepted: evidence-led deployment selection without a mandatory provider or remote service.
T-01 compares (a) an existing trusted Runledger worker next to established local isolation, with the producer elsewhere, (b) an optional binding to an established managed execution service, and (c) a narrow authenticated remote runner where trust/deployment requirements justify it. Provider-specific SDKs may live in optional adapters; the core and application contract remain provider-independent. Moving a worker changes which host holds application/database authority; document that tradeoff rather than treating it as equivalent to a credential-isolated remote broker.
Select two materially different supported deployment models and only the bindings they require. They may share an isolation primitive or adapter; two identical hosts or an RPC wrapper around a local handle do not establish diversity. T-05 implements the selected first binding; T-06 proves the second model and implements another binding/remote protocol only if needed. T-01 updates their concrete scope and reuse edge before downstream execution. A custom runner is limited to bounded start/observe/stop/recover and inventory; no business queue, workflow/retry policy, host placement or fleet lifecycle.
For each candidate, map controller/worker, broker if any, processor, ledger/inventory and sensitive artifact placement, privileges/credentials, enforcement owner and recovery operator. Separately state application portability, executor deployability and operational prerequisites. The evaluation must address a restricted managed-container deployment model without privileged orchestration in the application container, and disclose any independently operated privileged service elsewhere. T-01 names the actual target deployment test required before claiming that operational problem solved; T-08 records its evidence. Local restriction emulation can support only the exercised claims, not substitute for a hosted result. Cloud provisioning needs separate authorization; missing access leaves that target unverified, not falsely complete.
Generic runtime APIs contain no Docker/Kubernetes/cloud resource specification. Native SQLx/PostgreSQL 18 remains authoritative. A warm trusted broker may be reused with fresh processor containment. Additional profiles, warm native-processor reuse, a new weaker supervised mode, extra backend families, generic artifact frameworks and nonessential operator UI are deferred. No universal shell runner, plugin marketplace, antivirus service, application policy engine or arbitrary user-code hosting platform.

## Primary references
Checked during architecture review on 2026-09-26; recheck exact selected upstream releases in T-01 and record them in docs/references.md during implementation.
- TLS 1.3: https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8446#section-1 — confidentiality, integrity and peer authentication are separate transport requirements.
- Docker security: https://docs.docker.com/engine/security/ — daemon authority and runtime isolation depend on configuration.
- Kubernetes Pods: https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/workloads/pods/ — containers in one Pod share networking; grouping alone is not the declared boundary.
- Kubernetes Jobs: https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/workloads/controllers/job/#handling-pod-and-container-failures — parallelism=1 and restartPolicy=Never can still produce duplicate starts; physical execution and replacement semantics need verification. Rechecked 2026-09-26.
- Managed timeout example: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/batch/latest/userguide/job_timeouts.html — best-effort timeout termination and per-attempt countdowns are not an independently proven total lifetime bound. Rechecked 2026-09-26.
- Kubernetes RuntimeClass: https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/containers/runtime-class/ — backend selection is a deployment mechanism.
- AWS Fargate security: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonECS/latest/developerguide/fargate-security-considerations.html and https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonECS/latest/developerguide/fargate-tasks-services.html — task boundaries and unsupported Docker-style controls illustrate why profiles cannot be flag translations.
- Wasmtime security/interruption: https://docs.wasmtime.dev/security.html and https://docs.wasmtime.dev/examples-interrupting-wasm.html — optional capability-based mechanisms; no native-workload compatibility claim.

## Alternatives
Ordinary subprocess + env_clear supplies useful supervision, not the protected isolation boundary. A mandatory container-per-job/cloud-task application API fixes one deployment shape. A provider-neutral trait that leaves lifecycle coordination to applications retains the original problem. Optional bindings to established platforms are live T-01 alternatives under D-07. Building a new sandbox or general orchestration service exceeds this epic.
acceptance_criteria: All eight tasks satisfy their acceptance and actual dependencies after T-01's recorded deployment selection. A generic managed-invocation consumer and the same representative native processor execute under the initial protected profile in two materially different supported deployment models. Application code owns no launch/stop/cleanup protocol or provider SDK. Required isolation, bounded physical execution and artifact accounting, deadline enforcement, result-handoff recovery and supported-path atomic application/native completion have executed evidence within explicit trust/fault limits. Replay/workflow recovery cannot overlap unresolved lineage execution under the initial policy. Ordinary jobs preserve their contracts; incompatible writers are excluded. Operational containment, exact deployment/backend/toolchain evidence, ADR-010 SQL/API boundary assessment and fresh-agent consumer exercises are recorded. No second queue, invented sandbox or unverified portability/security claim is introduced. Required target deployment evidence remains an incomplete acceptance item until executed; optional/unavailable environments are explicitly excluded from support claims.

title: T-01: Prove a deployable isolation approach and its operational recovery
description:
Canonical plan: br show batter-05ci --json (epic description and design).
Task: T-01. Delivery scope and acceptance live in this Bead; native blocker edges own ordering.

## Outcome
Select the first protected profile and simplest feasible execution approach, with reproducible containment/recovery evidence and two materially different deployment models under D-07.

## Context
Resolve D-02/D-04/D-07 before production APIs depend on runtime assumptions. Existing Runledger subprocess ownership does not supply these guarantees.

## Changes
First specify one profile assuming a fully compromised registered workload: protected assets, allowed input/result/filesystem/egress, resource/time limits, plaintext/scratch/result handling and supported enforcement-failure domains. Use one representative registered native workload plus a hostile fixture; keep names/scenarios generic. Inspect versions/licenses, input immutability, native dependencies, subprocesses and scratch requirements. Compare the three D-07 topology families on paper; prove at most two shortlisted mechanisms, not an open-ended runtime survey.
Deliver a deployment/privilege/credential map, explicit operational-cost comparison, observed capability matrix, time/skew/enforcement contract, physical execution identity and backend retry/replacement rules, candidate-result ownership/retention-or-recompute decision, and recovery inventory owner. Separate application portability from executor and operator prerequisites. Identify Linux/macOS controller support and unsupported local profiles; name the actual restricted-hosting target and its required acceptance test without introducing a mandatory cloud dependency.
Rehearse ambiguous execution at full reserved capacity in the bounded spike inventory: who contains/reconciles which infrastructure identity, what permits reuse, what remains quarantined, and what reserved control resources keep recovery possible. Select and record the two deployment models in D-07 and revise T-05/T-06 titles/surfaces and any binding-reuse dependency before downstream work. Keep experiment code separate until adopted; no production abstraction is approved by an unexecuted design. Full native ledger integration belongs to T-03/T-04; this spike must not implement a parallel production queue.

## Recovery
Use disposable synthetic inputs and bounded disposable resources. Stop/fence discovered invocations and retain unresolved evidence; do not broaden host privileges or weaken the profile to make the spike pass. An unsupported requirement becomes a concrete design decision before dependent tasks begin.

## Verification policy
Follow the epic verification and rollout contract and the applicable repository/package guides. Record actual commands, revisions, platform/backend prerequisites and outcomes here. Runtime/security/platform claims require executable evidence; this planned task is unexecuted. New public APIs require rustdoc, examples and the ADR-010 invalid-state assessment.
acceptance_criteria:
Verification: Run the representative processor within the chosen restrictions and independently observe hostile filesystem, network/metadata, credential, descendant and resource/output denial. Kill or stop the controller and broker separately while the processor environment remains alive; partition communication, delay start until after stop, and exercise restart/reboot/clock uncertainty within the declared fault model. A broker timer alone is not independent enforcement. Test backend-initiated replacement without a new dispatch and show it cannot start an unaccounted or overlapping processor under the initial profile. Exercise controller death after candidate delivery but before apply using the chosen recovery policy. Fill outstanding capacity, lose observability and demonstrate verified settlement/containment or an explicit actionable unavailable state.

Done when: The first profile and supported failure assumptions are fixed; the simplest feasible topology is selected from the compared alternatives, with exact reproducible evidence and accepted operator prerequisites/cost. Two materially different deployment models and their actual acceptance tests are named. Required hard bounds are either demonstrated under the declared faults or the candidate is rejected. T-05/T-06 scope and actual dependency edges match the decision; a custom remote service is not mandatory. Missing hosted access leaves the affected proof/claim unverified and cannot be replaced by local-only evidence. If no candidate satisfies the required profile, leave the task open with the concrete unsupported requirement.

title: T-02: Define protected processor contracts and an adversarial executor test harness
description:
Canonical plan: br show batter-05ci --json (epic description and design).
Task: T-02. Delivery scope and acceptance live in this Bead; native blocker edges own ordering.

## Outcome
Expose a small native contract that binds processors to validated isolation requirements and represents execution evidence without conflating results, termination or cleanup.

## Context
D-01 through D-06 and ADR-010. Use T-01's proven semantics; names are implementation choices, while invalid-state prevention is required.

## Changes
Extend runledger-core job/handler contracts and the minimal runledger-runtime catalog seam; identify optional adapter package boundaries. Add only the opaque processor/profile/invocation values, bounded input/output descriptors, redacted exhaustive outcomes and typed observations required by the selected protected path. Keep internal phases inside library-owned execution; do not expose a type per phase to consumers or add a new supervised mode. Define protocol identity/version/expiry and authorized input/result transfer. Build a reusable conformance harness with controllable launch/stop/transport faults and hostile native fixtures; keep owning-suite fixtures out of generic leaf test-support. Define stable invocation lineage across native replay/workflow recovery, distinct from each physical execution identity. Carry T-01 time-source, enforcement-owner, skew and reboot/expiry decisions in the contract. Encode physical execution multiplicity/internal replacement, aggregate accounting and the selected result-handoff acknowledgements, last-copy ownership, retention and loss/recompute policy before T-03 fixes persistence. Distinguish scratch settlement from result disposal.
Use a small compiling generic consumer to exercise preparation, authorization and application before either deployment implementation hardens the API. Close the D-06 SQL capability decision: ordinary transaction ownership/completion stays in the library, while arbitrary transaction-control/direct-ledger SQL and captured external clients are excluded trust-boundary escapes. Inspect PgScopedSql and existing in-transaction native transitions; identify any minimal shared batter-sqlx seam and record the ADR-010 reason local types cannot prove arbitrary SQL/external effects. Do not introduce a SQL sandbox. Confirm T-01 has finalized T-05/T-06 surfaces and reuse edges before closing this task.

## Recovery
Keep new APIs opt-in and old handlers unchanged. Revise a contract that cannot express T-01's actual semantics before persistence/adapters adopt it; do not retain a misleading safe alias for a weaker path.

## Verification policy

title: Host the upstream worker with acknowledged startup and drain
description:
## Outcome and rationale

Runledger already owns claims, leases and durable retries. The process host must preserve that ownership while observing worker startup, failure and shutdown.

## Scope and ownership

Host the selected upstream runtime as one critical component of the reference root, consuming the command job type/payload and typed worker configuration. Use the exact startup witness from docs/reference-compatibility.md, not supervisor build completion as readiness. Lifecycle tests use the isolated fixtures and driven cleanup from batter-kjl. Signal upstream shutdown during process drain and await its owned shutdown/join result with the full documented budget, including abort cleanup. This task owns hosting; provider certainty/reconciliation belongs to batter-8q8.2. Do not supervise or respawn each upstream internal loop.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Startup/schema/registry/witness failure prevents readiness and follows partial-startup cleanup. A controlled initialization witness succeeds through the actual registered handler; acknowledgements state what that witness proves, without claiming every hidden loop initialized.
- Exercise normal drain and returned worker failure using the real upstream runtime and live fixture. Preserve the error returned by upstream; where upstream returns only its first failure and logs later failures, document that visibility limit rather than promise Batter collected hidden errors.
- Request stop-claiming at drain before forced cancellation. An already in-flight upstream claim may finish after the stop request; tests observe/classify it and do not promise a linearized upstream no-claim barrier absent a verified API.
- Outer grace includes the selected shutdown API's abort-cleanup allowance. Dropping its supervisor requests shutdown/detaches in the inspected candidate and is not proof of join. Timeout/panic/forced stop retains uncertain transitive termination and conservative dependency cleanup.
- Each job attempt gets fresh OperationContext budget and trusted dependencies independent of the submitting request token/deadline. Business denial and durable retry/reconcile outcomes remain successful task values rather than fatal process Err.
- Record upstream attempts and handler invocations independently; local replay does not multiply durable attempts. Provider-effect identity/restart proof remains batter-8q8.2.

## Code and evidence entrypoints

- examples/reference-service/ (new unpublished application package)
- docs/integrations.md
- docs/testing.md
- crates/batter/src/lifecycle.rs
- docs/references.md

## Verification and governing constraints

For code/dependency changes, run bash scripts/verify.sh and RUSTUP_TOOLCHAIN=1.94.0 bash scripts/verify.sh. Rebuild cargo build -p batter-axum --example http_service --locked and run python3 scripts/smoke_http.py --binary target/debug/examples/http_service in default, --signal SIGINT, --deadline, --warn-filter, and --warn-filter --deadline profiles. Finish backend work with scripts/jig check test and applicable Jig work gates. These commands do not substitute for this task's real database/provider/contract acceptance. Record exact versions, platform, prerequisites, commands and outcomes in docs/validation.md; missing integration prerequisites fail the explicit target rather than silently passing. Read AGENTS.md, agent-map.md and the nearest package guide. New public APIs need rustdoc and an example; update the relevant contract, implemented-status row and owning Bead. Keep library domain errors concrete, cleanup explicitly awaited, Unix-only scope, and upstream queue/provisioning ownership intact. Do not commit, publish or deploy without an explicit request.

## Design evidence

Re-audited against commit 22848ea on 2026-09-09. Process ownership is now extensively tested; durable job identity and reconciliation remain separate application/upstream contracts. The retrospective sample establishes failure mechanisms, not defect rates or current application bugs. See docs/design-evidence.md for the anonymized rationale and implemented baseline. Delivery authority remains this Bead; historical ExecPlans are not another backlog.


## Dependencies and consumers

Blocked by: batter-5pm — Provide typed root configuration and redacted secret handling; batter-4t6 — Verify compatible SQLx, durable-runtime and database-harness APIs; batter-kpd — Implement the reference command and atomic transactional submission; batter-kjl — Retain all fixture failures through partial acquisition and teardown

Unblocks: batter-8q8.2 — Demonstrate provider outcome certainty and restart reconciliation; batter-8jr — Provide application-root exporter setup and ordered flush; batter-7g0 — Persist versioned correlation and link real worker attempts; batter-fms — Prove atomicity, idempotency and durable lifetime with real PostgreSQL

Parent outcome: batter-8q8. Parent-child grouping is not a prerequisite.

## Implementation handoff: 2026-09-09

Before batter-8q8.2, host an explicit probe-only registry containing the startup/control handler. Its witness may acknowledge the critical component, but the ordinary HTTP root withholds application readiness approval; delivery readiness remains unavailable. Test ordinary pending jobs prepared through the actual command path before this host starts. batter-8q8.2 enables normal application readiness only after registering and witnessing the actual delivery handler. Do not register a successful no-op delivery handler or claim ordinary delivery execution readiness; persisted delivery commands remain pending and unclaimed. Tests prove the witness completes while an ordinary command upstream job stays unclaimed and its domain state is not successful. batter-8q8.2 installs the actual delivery handler through the same host constructor. Recheck the selected Runledger registered-type claim filter; a catalog enabled flag alone is not the registry-omission contract.

Bridge upstream termination certainty explicitly: current Batter treats an ordinary returned Err as joined direct work and does not automatically skip dependent cleanup. Keep an application-owned termination gate with NotStarted, Unproven and CooperativelyStopped states. NotStarted permits ordinary partial-startup cleanup; arm Unproven immediately before an upstream construction step that may spawn work. A verified pre-spawn validation error may restore NotStarted, while a construction panic or uncertain partial spawn may not. Once work may exist, allow dependent resource cleanup only after verified cooperative upstream completion sets CooperativelyStopped. A returned timeout, hidden-loop panic/uncertainty or dropped host never sets that proof. Group dependent resource hooks behind this gate; on uncertainty use an explicit nested CleanupStack::skip(UnsafeTaskExit) report retained in the application shutdown result/cleanup error, rather than pretending the outer report auto-classifies the native error. Preserve the original upstream task error too. Keep the nested stack and resource/lease owners in the separately driven application cleanup owner, outside skipped hook captures as required by batter-kjl. If core skips the grouped hook itself, that owner still produces nested skipped/pending evidence after the process report; capture Drop cannot delete an unquiesced fixture or discard the only nested report path. A real upstream returned-timeout test must show no dependent finalizer invocation and an inspectable skipped/pending result, even though the direct wrapper joined as Err. Do not manufacture a panic/abort or change core TaskOutcome to obtain this behavior.

## Configuration producer handoff: 2026-09-10

Consume the typed JobsConfig constructor from examples/reference-service/src/config.rs delivered by batter-5pm, passing it to the pinned Runledger explicit Supervisor::builder. Preserve deliberate intent-promoter inheritance and avoid builder_from_env or hardcoded replacement settings. Hosted runtime acceptance must distinguish changed worker concurrency with controlled handlers, alongside direct native-option assertions for the other settings. This producer handoff does not establish hosted readiness, drain, transitive joining or retry policy; those remain this task's acceptance. See .agent/plans/batter-5pm.md.


## Implemented constructor seam (batter-5pm, 2026-09-10)

Current worktree exposes `batter_example_reference_service::config::{RootSettings, PoolSettings, WorkerSettings, ConfigMode}`. `RootSettings::from_process(mode, selected_file, overrides)` owns source loading; `request_policy`, `pool_options`, `connect_options_from_process`, `bulkhead`, `supervisor` and `worker().builder` are the concrete native handoff methods. No optional-config/default fallback or native from_env path may bypass them.

The producer currently has passing offline source/constructor/HTTP/admission/credential/startup tests; its added pool/worker/startup live cases await an externally selected endpoint. This is an implementation handoff, not producer closure or this consumer's full-root/runtime acceptance. Existing acceptance and dependency direction remain unchanged. See `.agent/plans/batter-5pm.md` and the reference README for required PG*/passfile policy and the selected graph's unverified TLS negotiation.
acceptance_criteria:
- Startup/schema/registry/witness failure prevents readiness and follows partial-startup cleanup. A controlled initialization witness succeeds through the actual registered handler; acknowledgements state what that witness proves, without claiming every hidden loop initialized.
- Exercise normal drain and returned worker failure using the real upstream runtime and live fixture. Preserve the error returned by upstream; where upstream returns only its first failure and logs later failures, document that visibility limit rather than promise Batter collected hidden errors.
- Request stop-claiming at drain before forced cancellation. An already in-flight upstream claim may finish after the stop request; tests observe/classify it and do not promise a linearized upstream no-claim barrier absent a verified API.
- Outer grace includes the selected shutdown API's abort-cleanup allowance. Dropping its supervisor requests shutdown/detaches in the inspected candidate and is not proof of join. Timeout/panic/forced stop retains uncertain transitive termination and conservative dependency cleanup.
- Each job attempt gets fresh OperationContext budget and trusted dependencies independent of the submitting request token/deadline. Business denial and durable retry/reconcile outcomes remain successful task values rather than fatal process Err.
- Record upstream attempts and handler invocations independently; local replay does not multiply durable attempts. Provider-effect identity/restart proof remains batter-8q8.2.
- The hosted worker consumes batter-5pm native JobsConfig constructors and their selected intent-promoter policy; controlled live handlers distinguish changed configured concurrency from hardcoded defaults. Native-option assertions cover the remaining mapped settings; from_env fallback cannot bypass root validation.
notes:
Implemented and verified at baseline d82f5bf. Added Startup::without_readiness_approval; a probe-only Runledger WorkerHost with exact handler-plus-durable-success witness; fresh per-attempt OperationContext; native stop-before-bounded-join ownership; explicit NotStarted/Unproven/CooperativelyStopped termination gate; and separately driven dependency cleanup retaining UnsafeTaskExit on uncertainty. The production reference root remains unready and omits records.delivery.execute until batter-8q8.2. Live acceptance expanded to 47 cases: both Rust 1.98.1 (68.36s) and 1.94.0 (66.48s) passed with 47/47 against PostgreSQL 18.6. Both scripts/verify.sh matrices, all ten HTTP smokes, and Jig plan_01M27YA6NV07SYD5NGKDWS1WXH passed; api:test receipt receipt_01M2812Q6MYKP25G6WW4ZH35D6. The concurrency audit found and fixed the separate external timeout-trigger requirement and cancellation-dependent cleanup ownership. Runledger's first-error visibility limit remains documented; provider execution/export/publication/deployment remain separate.

title: Let consumers use Runledger and Runlimit through one Batter dependency
description:
## Outcome

A consumer selects Batter, Runledger and Runlimit through the facade and its features at one revision, without separate native package pins, side pins or `[patch]` sections.

## Evidence (read-only two-consumer survey, 2026-09-27; consumers A and B are independently deployed downstream Tokio/Axum/SQLx/PostgreSQL services that pin Batter by Git revision; their identities and file paths are kept outside this tracker)

- Consumer B pins the facade at one revision, `batter-at-rest` at another, and the standalone Runledger repository with a `[patch]` that redirects `batter-sqlx`. It needs native Runledger APIs (supervisor builder, `JobsConfig`, `JobCatalog`, `run_atomic`, `JobEnqueueIntent`, the migrator) that `batter-runledger` does not re-export: `crates/batter-runledger/src/lib.rs:66` re-exports selected `runledger_postgres` items only.
- Consumer A declares eight direct Git dependencies on this workspace (facade, at-rest, three Runledger and three Runlimit packages) at one revision to keep a single source identity.
- `batter-runlimit` already re-exports whole native crates; the two adapters are inconsistent.
- The side pins made consumer B's upgrade harder with every new capability; it is 139 commits behind master as of 2026-09-27.

## Scope

Feature-gated facade re-exports of the native Runledger crates (and any Runlimit crates the facade does not yet expose), a documented single-dependency recipe, and an external consumer that uses only facade paths.

## Acceptance Criteria

- An external consumer implements a Runledger worker with durable intents and migrations plus a Runlimit PostgreSQL limiter using only the batter dependency and its features: no direct native package and no [patch].
- docs/reference-compatibility.md documents the single-dependency recipe, and the publication release order (batter-ddc) stays consistent.
- bash scripts/verify.sh passes.

comments.text:
Implementation complete for batter-0jsf (Claude); review is owned by a separate Codex session.

WHAT CHANGED

Feature-gated facade namespaces now expose every native Runledger and Runlimit
library package as the native package itself, so one `batter` dependency needs no
direct native-package declaration and no [patch] section, and a type reached
through the facade and through a direct dependency are one identity:

- batter::runledger::native::{core, postgres, runtime} under `runledger`.
  batter-runledger declares runledger-core directly (previously dev-only), which
  runledger-postgres and runledger-runtime already resolved.
- batter::runledger::native::test_support under the new `runledger-test-support`,
  documented as test-only.
- batter::runlimit::memory under `runlimit-memory`.
- batter::runlimit::native_transport::{http, axum} under the new
  `runlimit-native-http` and `runlimit-native-axum`.
- runledger-tui is binary-only, so it has no namespace.

Reachability moves no ownership. register_in remains the protected registration
path and runlimit::http the protected quota-before-body assembly; each native
module documents the obligations its callers take on instead. native_transport is
named apart from http for that reason, and neither transport feature selects
axum, batter-axum or that module. The facade default feature set stays empty and
every namespace is absent without its feature.

An earlier draft of this work excluded runlimit-http/runlimit-axum and told
consumers to declare them directly. The user corrected that mid-task on
2026-09-30: coverage of the native transport crates is required, and clear
namespace/feature design is the way to keep native paths distinct from protected
composition. Both are now covered as described above.

EVIDENCE

bash scripts/verify.sh passed (exit 0) on pinned Rust 1.98.1
(48a229cea 2026-09-01), cargo 1.98.1, Linux x86_64, with Docker and PostgreSQL 18
available, on commit e18a278a4e03f686b1e303d970b8c7151f5b5c0f. It ran formatting,
the file-budget check (6 files evaluated, 0 findings), all three Clippy
configurations with warnings denied, all six matrix parts (workspace,
no-default-features, doctests, consumers, runlimit, scripts), rustdoc with
warnings denied, and all five HTTP smoke profiles (each PASS). No MSRV or Jig
gate was run locally. Cargo.lock remains Cargo-generated; the only change is
dependency edges for the new declarations.

Two earlier attempts failed and were repaired rather than relaxed: the runlimit
feature runner rejected the two new adapter features because they had no graph
expectation, and two controls in test_parallel_process.py pinned the old feature
inventory and matrix batch shape. Those guards worked as intended.

New executed acceptance evidence:
- scripts/check_single_facade_consumer.py builds consumers/single_facade_consumer.rs
  from a Git-free source copy, asserts from resolved Cargo metadata that it
  declares only `batter` with default features disabled and no [patch], that
  every required identity resolves once from the copy, and that no external
  source drifts from the root lock. It then requires each of these to run exactly
  once against a disposable PostgreSQL 18 database: both migration histories plus
  Runledger schema verification; a durable enqueue intent and an atomic queue row
  committed in one transaction with an application write; the registered native
  worker executing the promoted intent and the direct enqueue under Batter's
  protected lifecycle from readiness through requested drain and checked
  completion; a native PostgreSQL quota admitted then denied with no work invoked
  on the denial; and that denial's draft-11 response metadata.
- consumers/single_facade_harness.rs owns the disposable database through the
  facade's runledger-test-support feature and is held to the same
  single-dependency assertion. Docker provisioning and teardown remain
  Runledger's; no second database harness was added.
- crates/batter/tests/native_transport_consumer.rs drives one admitted and one
  denied request through the native Axum layer via facade paths and asserts the
  transport types' identity against direct dependencies.
- scripts/check_facade_features.py now covers 20 feature cases including the
  three new features, with graph expectations, reachability imports, identity
  assertions and six new negative cases proving each namespace is absent without
  its feature and that a disabled bridge does not reach its adapter feature
  through another. 38 facade feature/negative/identity cases passed.
- scripts/check_runlimit_features.py now enumerates all 32 subsets of the
  adapter's five features (previously eight of three). It expects the Axum crate
  whenever axum or native-axum is selected but batter-axum only for axum, so the
  native transport layer cannot quietly pull in the Batter Axum adapter, reaches
  each selected namespace, and requires a disabled-native_transport import error.
  All 32 subsets passed.
- scripts/test_single_facade_consumer.py is the new runner control suite: a
  declared native-workspace dependency, a [patch] table, a facade dependency left
  on default features, a missing or duplicated root package, a missing,
  duplicated, remote or sibling identity, a missing or repeated marker, and a
  build output naming no matching executable all fail.

Both parts are wired into complete verification: the single-facade consumer runs
in its own batch of the `consumers` part (it owns a container and a full facade
build), and its controls run in the `scripts` part.

SCOPE AND LIMITS

- The direct-package consumer checks (check_runledger_consumer.py,
  check_runlimit_consumer.py) are unchanged. They legitimately declare native
  dependencies because they prove direct-path and cross-path identity, a
  different contract from the single-facade requirement.
- Only what is listed above executed. The consumer does not drive the native Axum
  layer; that is executed separately by the facade test named above, and the
  consumer's own rustdoc says so rather than implying coverage.
- Selecting runledger-test-support pulls testcontainers' Docker client HTTP stack,
  including the axum crate, into a development graph. That is the native test
  support's own dependency and is recorded in the feature graph expectations.
- "Test-only" for native::test_support is application policy: Cargo cannot gate a
  feature to development graphs, and the facade cannot detect the caller's
  profile. ADR-010 records this along with the rest of the invalid-state review.
- Docs updated: docs/reference-compatibility.md (single-dependency recipe with the
  path/package/feature table, migration order and the executed evidence),
  docs/integrations.md, docs/status.md, docs/testing.md, docs/usage.md,
  docs/architecture.md, ADR-006/010/011/012 amendments, root and crate AGENTS.md,
  agent-map.md, READMEs and CHANGELOG.
- Publication order is unchanged and nothing was published; that remains
  batter-ddc. The native packages still precede the Batter adapters.
- No hosted CI execution is claimed.

Task stays in_progress until the separate Codex review completes.

Reviewed 9cdb53cd301e76d59e7e6a70b42d17fcf9228de3..42a5a659865c8fd0b176fad63399cf42bb6c8fc7. The new consumer has failure-path settlement and build-environment defects; the recorded successful verification matrix was not rerun.

Full review comments:

- [P2] Await worker settlement on every error path — /srv/dev/home/dev/projects/batter-worktrees/single-facade-dependency-0jsf/consumers/single_facade_consumer.rs:244-250
  If readiness fails, submission errors, or a receive wait times out, `?` exits before `running.wait_checked()`. Dropping `RunningSupervisor` only requests shutdown; it does not join it. Consequently, `main` closes the shared pool and can terminate Tokio while native settlement is still running, discarding its report. Always await shutdown before dependency cleanup and retain both application and shutdown failures, as required by [AGENTS.md:231](AGENTS.md#L231).

- [P2] Force SQLx offline mode for the temporary Cargo builds — /srv/dev/home/dev/projects/batter-worktrees/single-facade-dependency-0jsf/scripts/check_single_facade_consumer.py:105-107
  When the invoking shell exports `DATABASE_URL` without `SQLX_OFFLINE=true`, these temporary Cargo roots do not inherit the copied workspace's `.cargo/config.toml`. Runledger's `query!` macros therefore contact the ambient database instead of using committed `.sqlx` metadata, making this check fail against an unrelated or unavailable database. Set `SQLX_OFFLINE=true` for both this build and the harness's `cargo run`, as the existing Runledger consumer runner does; Cargo's `--offline` flag does not control SQLx.

DISPOSITIONS

Both P2 findings confirmed and fixed in new repair commit cca0dd4772941e10f732c1be0a8d0ec597f5ee57. No rejected findings, no standing rejections.

1. The running consumer body now retains its result while awaiting shutdown_checked, preserving both application and shutdown failures. The existing protected Startup API owns pool finalization before database operations, so errors during initialization also retain cleanup and unsuccessful settlement cannot bypass conservative cleanup skipping. The root no longer directly closes the pool after a worker error. Running assertions became returned errors through the same completion boundary. Native runtime and foundation APIs are unchanged.
2. Temporary consumer build, Rust control tests and harness cargo run all explicitly set SQLX_OFFLINE=true. The runtime harness still selects its disposable database. Executed child-process controls verify the override with DATABASE_URL set and SQLX_OFFLINE unset or false.

Failure controls: four Rust cases prove a held worker drain delays return and dependency cleanup, readiness failure preserves application error plus task report, receive failure preserves cleanup failure, and worker panic skips cleanup. Combined formatting is redacted while original causes remain inspectable. Nine Python runner controls pass, including source-copy retention of the new modules. Contracts, consumer guidance, testing docs and implemented-status row updated.

ADR-010: this is the first confirmed lifecycle failure in these review rounds, not a repeated invariant after a lifecycle repair. The earlier failures in comment 420 concern feature/control inventories. Existing protected startup and checked completion APIs support this bounded consumer fix; no public API redesign or architectural escalation was needed. This is executed failure-path evidence, not a fresh-agent usability evaluation.

VALIDATION

Focused source-copy check passed on Linux x86_64 / Rust 1.98.1 with hostile invoking environment SQLX_OFFLINE=false and DATABASE_URL=postgres://unused:unused@127.0.0.1:1/unavailable: all four Rust controls, native PostgreSQL 18 harness, and seven required live acceptance markers passed. Initial focused builds caught and corrected a boxed-error Sized bound and an accidental enum-name replacement. No tests or budgets were relaxed.

Complete bash scripts/verify.sh passed exit 0 on the unchanged repair tree, then committed as cca0dd4772941e10f732c1be0a8d0ec597f5ee57. Rust 1.98.1 (48a229cea 2026-09-01), cargo 1.98.1, Linux x86_64. Formatting, file budgets (8 evaluated, 0 findings), all three Clippy configurations, all six matrix parts, rustdoc with denied warnings and all five HTTP smoke profiles passed. Standalone consumer rustfmt --edition 2024 --check and git diff --check also passed. Cargo.lock unchanged. No local MSRV or hosted CI run; the earlier implementation verification in comment 420 predates these repairs.

Verification environment limitation: the first plain verify run failed the pre-existing reference-service metrics executable test because the concurrent default-feature configuration command replaced target/debug/batter-example-reference-service with a build lacking metrics. Both commands and the shared executable lookup predate this task; this range only adds consumer batches to test_matrix.py. To validate without unrelated repository changes, the successful run used a temporary PATH Cargo launcher that delegates to /srv/dev/home/dev/.cargo/bin/cargo and holds one flock for exactly these two complete commands:
- cargo test --workspace --all-features --all-targets --locked

Every other Cargo invocation is delegated unchanged; flags, test assertions, toolchain and source are unchanged. This serializes only those overlapping executable builds/tests. A consumer that atomically writes application state plus a durable enqueue intent cannot adopt RunledgerTransaction: record_job_enqueue_intent_tx still takes &mut sqlx::Transaction<Postgres>. Minimal external consumer: begin RunledgerTransaction from PgSession, pass &mut tx to record_job_enqueue_intent_tx, then commit. cargo check emits E0308, expected &mut Transaction<Postgres>, found &mut RunledgerTransaction. Direct-job enqueue has capability APIs, but durable-intent recording does not. Runledger owning bead runledger-wtb (closed) was inspected; evidence is also being added there. Do not convert intents to direct enqueue, split atomic writes, expose raw connections, or reinstate a borrow-then-return pool API to enable adoption.

Two additional native boundaries are unexpressible through PgSession: SQLx 0.9 Migrator::run_direct requires &mut C: Migrate, and Runledger ensure_schema_compatible_after_idempotency_cutover_with_connection requires &mut PgConnection. PgSession/PgTransaction expose only Executor. Any supported replacement should retain opaque physical identity, exact native migration/checksum/lock behavior, cancellation retirement and truthful completion evidence. A consumer-local native close-on-drop fallback was considered and rejected because it bypasses the new protected capability boundary; this is an adapter coverage gap, not a request to loosen its invariant.

HttpBoundary also cannot express a custom readiness renderer or route-specific private response headers outside admission; protected assembly owns those positions. Its low-level composition remains explicitly supported, so this is an adoption limitation rather than a demonstrated runtime defect. Any extension should preserve fixed admission/correlation order and validated probe identities.

Acceptance for closing the downstream gap: compile an external consumer that atomically records an intent through an opaque transaction; PostgreSQL 18 tests demonstrate commit/rollback/conflict/isolation semantics; native migration and schema-verification entry points preserve ownership during cancellation. title: Make PostgreSQL verification policies valid before execution
description:
## Outcome

Replace mutable, potentially invalid executable SQLx verification policies with pure compiled policy values and a non-empty verification plan. Structural configuration errors must be returned before an OperationContext or database pool is involved.

## Scope

Implement the systemic authority and migration policy cutover in crates/batter-sqlx. Keep application configuration schemas downstream. Make executable policies opaque and immutable; validate and canonicalize object/privilege compatibility, duplicates, contradictions, and capacity during pure construction. Replace the empty VerificationRequest builder with a non-empty plan. Make the executor accept only compiled inputs, preserve exact-role ownership safeguards, and remove or constrain the ACL-only escape hatch. Migrate repository examples, tests, contracts and known consumer-facing guidance in one coordinated breaking cutover; do not move SQLx into batter core or add a framework.

## Acceptance

- No public type accepted by PostgreSQL verification execution can represent invalid structural policy state or an empty request.
- Object/privilege compatibility is exhaustive across exact objects, discovery defaults, PUBLIC allowances, required privileges, database and parameter policy. Identical duplicates have one documented canonical meaning; contradictory declarations fail pure compilation.
- Policy capacity and migration checksum/version failures occur before operation polling and database acquisition. Runtime VerificationError no longer carries caller policy-construction failures on the canonical path.
- ExactRoleManifest and generic authority construction emit one canonical authority representation; ordinary public APIs cannot discard exact-role safeguards.
- Canonical examples and docs expose one protected path. Existing semantic failure tests, PostgreSQL 18 live contracts, two Rust toolchains, HTTP smokes and Jig gates remain passing with exact executed evidence.
- The open pinned-consumer adoption evidence is explicitly reconciled with this breaking revision before it is claimed as evidence for the new API.

## Governing constraints

Follow AGENTS.md, crates/batter-sqlx/AGENTS.md, ADR-010 and .agent/PLANS.md. Use generic scenarios. Update the relevant contract, status row, testing/validation evidence and this Bead. New public APIs require rustdoc and examples. Do not commit, push, publish or deploy without explicit user authority.

title: Bound adapter future size and type depth on canonical paths
description:
## Outcome

Canonical adapter entry points return futures whose size and type depth let ordinary consumers compose them inside Axum handlers, finite tasks and tests at rustc's default recursion limit and the default test-thread stack, without consumer-local `recursion_limit` attributes, `RUST_MIN_STACK` or bespoke `Box::pin` wrappers.

## Evidence (read-only two-consumer survey, 2026-09-27; consumers A and B are independently deployed downstream Tokio/Axum/SQLx/PostgreSQL services that pin Batter by Git revision; their identities and file paths are kept outside this tracker)

- Original report (consumer A at 95252ad): composing `Quota::run` around SQLx-backed authentication work inside an `OperationContext` and an Axum handler overflowed rustc's trait/query evaluation at the default recursion limit, and the concrete future propagated into downstream integration-test crates. Raising `recursion_limit` in every consumer would leak Batter implementation complexity; consumer A erased its admission future once at the application boundary.
- Consumer A, later pin: awaiting an eight-bind checked `query_scalar!` through `PgQueryHandle::fetch_one` aborted a default-stack Tokio test thread with `SIGABRT` (stack overflow). It passed with `RUST_MIN_STACK=16777216`, with the older `PgLease` path, or after boxing the `fetch_one` future, which is the workaround it keeps. The finding was never filed here because the tracker import failed at the time.
- Both consumers carry `#![recursion_limit = "256"]` in two crates each. Consumer B has 141 `Box::pin` calls, boxed future aliases for authentication workflows and a `send_future` helper, stating that native workflow types exceed the default release layout-query depth.
- Measured 2026-09-27 against master 463d536 (Rust 1.98.1, macOS arm64; unpolled futures; eight-bind `query_scalar`; lazy pool, no database):

| Future | debug | release |
| --- | --- | --- |
| SQLx `QueryScalar::fetch_one(&pool)` | 552 B | 552 B |
| SQLx `PgPool::acquire()` | 2,528 B | 8,608 B |
| `PgLease::acquire` | 3,216 B | 9,296 B |
| `PgQueryHandle::fetch_one` | 23,640 B | 72,280 B |
| `OperationContext::run(fetch_one)` | 24,304 B | 72,944 B |
| `run_atomic_in` (empty body) | 24,592 B | 79,312 B |
| `Box::pin(PgQueryHandle::fetch_one)` | 8 B | 8 B |

SQLx boxes its own pool query future, but `acquire()` is not boxed. Batter's layers (`PgQueryHandle::run`, `retain_with_fallback`, `run_resolved`, the observed operation) pass large futures by value through nested async functions, which multiplies the unboxed acquisition state about eightfold. `OperationContext::run` itself adds about 700 bytes per level.

## Scope

`PgQueryHandle::{fetch_one, fetch_optional, fetch_all, execute}`, the `run_atomic*` family (profiled, fail-fast and policy variants), `PgLease::acquire`, `AttemptRunner::run` and `Quota::run`. Either construct inner futures once without by-value nesting, or erase them once at the adapter boundary (one allocation per database or quota operation, as SQLx already does for its own query future). Keep `operation::run` and core lifecycle paths allocation-free unless measurement shows otherwise. Preserve lazy factory invocation, the same parent deadline, typed failures and consumption evidence, retained outcomes, dispatch through destruction and no work before admission.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Size tests assert upper bounds (for example 4 KiB in debug and release) for every canonical future in scope and fail on regression.
- An external Axum plus SQLx plus quota consumer composes Quota::run, run_atomic_in and PgQueryHandle inside one handler, registers it at rustc's default recursion limit, and runs it on a default-stack test thread, without local recursion_limit, RUST_MIN_STACK or type-erasure wrappers.
- Lazy factories, parent deadlines, typed RunResult failures and consumption evidence, dispatch through destruction and all existing SQLx, quota and attempt tests are preserved; bash scripts/verify.sh passes.
- Any remaining opt-in boxed or direct path documents when to select it.

comments.text:
2026-09-28 implementation and verification record (base 3ea200878585bc84f5ccc2cfe4fd85437cb049c9; commits 128d79e, 4f8c6fc, a6fcbe7).

Delivered: canonical adapter entry points erase their operation once, on first poll. `PgLease::acquire` and the four `PgQueryHandle` helpers erase the bounded operation as `dyn Future + Send`; the helpers dispatch through a private call selector, so no public bound changed, and the generic pooled operation acquires through a crate-private erased `acquire` (SQLx 0.9.0 does not box `Pool::acquire`; its pool executor boxes acquire plus query once). All twelve `run_atomic*` entry points box one private unboxed workflow (`atomic`, `with`, fail-fast `run`) exactly once; stable Rust cannot name `AsyncFnOnce::CallOnceFuture`, so that erasure keeps the concrete type and `Send` stays inferred from the callback. Transaction birth (acquisition, reset, profile, BEGIN, XID) is one separate `dyn Send` erasure, shared with `low_level::PgAtomicTransaction::begin`. `retain`/`retain_with_fallback` now take constructors, removing the ~9x by-value nesting (run_atomic 8,712 B -> run_atomic_in 79,272 B optimized at the base). `Quota::run` erases its native check and its admitted work (new bound `Fut: Send`); the internal HTTP seam keeps its direct work path with the erased check. `AttemptRunner::run` erases native admission and completes through the erased runner. Core `operation::run` is unchanged and allocation-free. Allocations per call: lease acquisition 1, pooled query 2 (operation, acquisition), atomic workflow 2 (workflow, birth), quota 2 (check, work), attempt 3. Verification (macOS arm64, pinned Rust 1.98.1): `bash scripts/verify.sh` passed (fmt, file budget with the pre-existing attempts.rs notice now at 430 lines, three Clippy configurations, all six matrix parts including the new optimized future-size command and the external composed consumer in both profiles, rustdoc, five HTTP smokes). The five new size tests and the external consumer fail against the base. Live PostgreSQL 18.6 disposable cluster: `bash scripts/test_sqlx_live.sh` passed its exact 120-case inventory (atomic 57, migrations 2, disposition 11, pool ownership 14, verification 36) and `attempts_live` passed 14 cases; Runledger's Docker PostgreSQL 18 atomic-runner tests passed inside verify. title: Guard complete protected routers and derive Runlimit feature coverage
description:
## Root cause

The HTTP adapter treated an opaque Axum Router as a route list, although it also carries fallback endpoints. Applying route_layer only to matched routes left nested protected fallbacks outside authentication/quota; merging independent routers before normalizing probe fallback behavior could panic. The isolated feature checker separately hardcoded the manifest feature inventory.

## Acceptance

- Every endpoint supplied in the protected Router, including nested custom fallbacks and method fallbacks, passes lifecycle, authentication and one native atomic quota check before handler/body work.
- Public probes remain explicitly opt-in; their fallback behavior does not become a public endpoint. Business root fallback ownership is explicit and does not silently change.
- Supported Router inputs with custom fallbacks cannot panic during assembly from duplicate fallback ownership; relevant regression tests prove the wire boundary and telemetry.
- Feature-subset validation derives the declared feature set from Cargo metadata and fails on an unmapped addition, with a negative control.
- Update rustdoc, integration contract, status, Bead and validation evidence. Run both supported toolchains, HTTP smoke and Jig gates. Do not claim live PostgreSQL or Linux execution without evidence; do not commit or publish.
