title: Add per-attempt deadlines capped by remaining total budget
description:
## Outcome and rationale

A single slow attempt should be bounded without granting the next attempt a fresh total deadline.

## Scope

Add a source-compatible opt-in per-attempt maximum duration. Preserve existing `execute`/`execute_with_jitter` signatures, default behavior, and the meaning of their currently exhaustively matchable public error enums. Use a new opt-in entrypoint/result boundary for the additional typed attempt-timeout outcome instead of relabeling it as expiration of the original total context. Validate a positive representable attempt duration before any factory work. Immediately before each attempt, after its preceding backoff, derive `attempt_deadline = min(original_context.deadline(), attempt_start + attempt_maximum)` with checked arithmetic and downward cancellation. The input context may already be a shortened work phase; never recover its reserved finalization time or refresh the original total deadline. Reaching an attempt deadline is terminal for this execution, just like cancellation: it does not authorize another attempt or invoke expected-error classification. Preserve the latest earlier application error and the count of factories actually invoked. Keep panic propagation and destruction/cancellation behavior of OperationContext::run. Add a runnable example using distinct total and attempt limits.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Paused-time tests prove the deadline formula for the first and subsequent attempts, including a parent deadline shorter than the requested attempt limit, backoff consuming original total time, and use of a shortened `OperationPhases::work()` context. A later attempt may start with less than its requested maximum remaining; the maximum is a cap, not a minimum useful-work reservation.
- The opt-in result distinguishes an attempt cap expiring while total time remains from the original total deadline expiring. At a tied attempt/total deadline report total deadline; cancellation wins over either deadline, and an expired deadline wins over simultaneously ready work completion, preserving existing boundary precedence.
- Attempt timeout stops the sequence with no classifier call for the interrupted attempt and no next factory. Count only invoked factories: initial interruption reports zero, first-attempt timeout reports one with no prior error, and a later-attempt timeout retains the previous concrete error and actual started count.
- Cancellation during backoff or before the next factory retains the prior error/count without incrementing either attempt or future optional retry-token debit. A started attempt's child scope is cancelled and its owned future destroyed on completion/interruption; parent cancellation remains downward and no arbitrary spawned task is claimed joined.
- Zero/unrepresentable attempt configuration is rejected without starting a factory. No opt-in path catches panics as retryable errors. Existing public entrypoint behavior and exhaustive consumer matches keep compiling, and new public APIs have rustdoc plus an example.

## Code and evidence entrypoints

- crates/batter/src/retry.rs
- crates/batter/src/operation.rs
- crates/batter/tests/retry.rs
- crates/batter/examples/operation_budget.rs

## Dependencies and consumers

## Acceptance Criteria

- The adapter-owned lease/native-pool contract is exercised by the minimal probe consumer and removes duplicated fixture mechanics there. External downstream adoption remains batter-7r3.6; this producer does not depend on its consumer closing.

- Pool maxima plus standalone/administrative connections fit the selected harness connection_limits budget. One-slot pools and acknowledged lock barriers support complete-operation tests without sleep-based lock assumptions.
- Use the explicit ignored reference_live cases and runner from batter-4t6. Missing PostgreSQL 18/external harness prerequisites fail that invocation; ordinary all-feature workspace gates compile but do not execute live cases.
- Normal fixture finish explicitly closes every application pool before consuming the lease for cleanup. Deferred queues are separately drained; external harness shutdown() cannot stand in for drain_deferred_cleanup().
- Tokio paused time controls Tokio timers only. PostgreSQL clocks, transaction ordering and lock ownership use real database observations. Failure/cancelled-waiter ownership is extended by batter-kjl.
- Reusable ownership is public under the optional batter-sqlx test-support feature and consumed by reference tests; the default adapter graph excludes the external harness. Core and generic support remain independent; no Runledger dependency enters fixture support.
- Retained template reuse avoids repeated initialization; changed SQL, bundle order and setup revision change identities. A live changed-input clone proves changed state by independent readback, not only hash inequality. Ordered inputs and initializer ownership follow the readiness handoff below.
- Reject over-budget or overflowing declared connection plans before resource acquisition. Document separately bounded suite observers and harness-owned sessions; use a separately budgeted observer to prove the actual one-slot operation waits on the intended blocker and completes after explicit release.
- Finish closes every owned pool before lease cleanup; independent catalog observation proves database absence. Deferred drain runs after cleanup producers finish. Any retired backend used by the fixture tests is observed terminated before database release; no cancellation-safe teardown claim precedes batter-kjl.
- The exact live runner inventory includes every added fixture case and preserves all four compatibility cases, with runner controls rejecting omissions/skips/zero execution. Record both-toolchain live evidence and preserve the independent SQLx disposition suite.

### Concrete ownership and API boundary

Implement reusable fixture composition in `batter-sqlx` behind an opt-in `test-support` feature and public `test_support` module. Select the already pinned external harness with `default-features = false` as an optional dependency of that feature; the reference package enables it only as a development dependency. Reuse generic `finish` where needed; do not move SQLx or harness ownership into `batter-test-support`. Update package guides and documentation that currently say the harness is selected only directly by reference tests. No Runledger dependency belongs in the fixture module.

Expose a fixture owner retaining the native pools and external database lease, with explicitly awaited normal finish. Keep SQLx `PgLease` (one checked-out connection) distinct from upstream `DatabaseLease` (one disposable database). Accept explicit harness/pool policy and application-owned initialization inputs; no ambient environment parsing in the reusable API. Keep minimal probe SQL and application migration execution in the reference consumer. A reusable helper must be exercised by that consumer, with duplicated lease/pool/finish mechanics removed where replaced.

Use an explicitly owned suite runtime/lifetime for the shared harness and retained template handles. Do not put SQLx pools in a process-static cache shared across independently destroyed Tokio test runtimes. Harness `template` single-flights on cloned handles, but its cache is weak: keep `DatabaseTemplate` handles alive for the reuse being claimed. The suite owner must outlive fixture finish and deferred drain. Choose the concrete suite arrangement in the ExecPlan without changing existing compatibility-probe contracts.

### Template inputs and executable oracles

Use upstream `FingerprintBuilder` and `TemplateSpec`, not another cache/hash engine. Define an ordered input contract with bundle identity, migration identity/type and exact SQL bytes (or the selected upstream checksum), plus an explicit revision for initialization behavior not represented by those inputs. Frame boundaries and order matter; never key by file path, migration version alone, or unordered iteration. The consumer's initializer applies the corresponding declared inputs through its native migration entrypoints, and closes initializer-owned pools on returned success or error before handing control back to the harness. A callback is trusted to match its declared fingerprint; this is not automatically verified by the harness.

Prove unchanged inputs reuse the retained template without rerunning initialization; changed SQL, bundle order and setup revision produce different identities. At least one live changed-input case must produce independently read-back changed clone state, so hash inequality alone cannot pass a broken template selection path. Concurrent leases from one template must have different database identities and independently isolated writes. Require affected-row counts and readback, not merely successful execution. Preserve the existing empty-database and initialized-schema upgrade compatibility cases; neither may be redirected through an already-current template.

### Connection and lock boundaries

Validate declared pool maxima plus standalone blocker/observer/admin connections against `connection_limits().connections_per_database()` before opening those resources, using checked arithmetic. Include observer capacity even when its connection targets the admin database. Document which connections are reserved per lease versus separately bounded suite resources. `max_simultaneous_leases()` is floor division; harness owner/template/lifecycle sessions are additional server usage. Multiple independently started harnesses do not share this local budget. Do not claim a server-wide bound from local permits or SQLx pool maxima; default retirement may leave server sessions alive.

Provide a controlled lock fixture with retained blocker/waiter identities. The blocker acknowledges actual lock acquisition; an independent, separately budgeted observer confirms the intended waiter is blocked by that blocker (for example using `pg_blocking_pids`), then release is explicit. The observer must not acquire from the one-slot pool occupied by the waiter. Prove the real operation stays pending while blocked and completes with independently checked results after release. Bound polling and the whole live invocation independently; elapsed sleeps or a helper-only lock check are not proof. Any interrupted/default-retired session used by these cases needs positive server-side termination observation before database release.

### Finish boundary and follow-up split

Normal finish joins/acknowledges test-owned direct operations, closes every fixture pool, then consumes the database lease for awaited cleanup. Only after all suite producers have finished submitting cleanup may the suite call `drain_deferred_cleanup`; the upstream barrier covers submissions accepted before it begins, not later submissions. External `shutdown()` remains a separate no-op and cannot replace this drain. Assert database absence using an independent observer after cleanup. Keep template caches under upstream ownership; do not delete databases by prefix.

This task delivers normal acquisition/finish and concrete resource ownership, not cancellation-shielded teardown. Do not export a cancel-safe claim or implement `timeout(fixture.finish())` and call dropped ownership retained. Keep errors concrete/redacted and preserve returned body/cleanup failures rather than introducing an early-return loss for the follow-up to fix. `batter-kjl` still owns the resumable cleanup driver, cancelled waiters, partial-acquisition/panic/owner-loss matrix, and systematic detached-session negative controls. Preserve all four existing compatibility cases and the independent SQLx ten-case runner. Keep the independent process watchdog and fail explicit invocation on missing PostgreSQL 18/admin prerequisites, omitted cases, skipped cases or zero executed tests. Run new live cases on both supported toolchains against an explicitly selected disposable server; historical ports are not current prerequisites. Follow existing root verification and Jig requirements. Verify default-versus-test-support dependency graphs, rustdoc/examples, and updated integration/status/validation facts. No production reference router, application row builder, new provisioning engine, upstream modification, or reverse dependency on consumer completion is needed.

title: Specify and test HTTP handler panic behavior
description:
## Outcome and rationale

Operation panic tests and HTTP future-abort tests cannot establish how an unwinding handler affects the HTTP response.

## Scope

Add a dedicated handler-panic regression and an explicit decision about the reference application using an opt-in existing Tower panic boundary. Inspect actual pinned Tower/Axum APIs first. If recovery is selected, compose a sanitized application renderer and test middleware ordering; otherwise test and document propagation. Do not silently add a library-wide catcher.

## Acceptance Criteria

- An unwinding handler panic has an executable, documented outcome.
- If a boundary is adopted, its status/body and metadata are sanitized and its opt-in ordering is tested.
- Aborting panics, default panic-hook output, damaged shared state and body panics after headers remain outside recovery guarantees.
- Panics never become ordinary retryable domain errors.

## Code and evidence entrypoints

- crates/batter-axum/src/lib.rs
- crates/batter-axum/tests/http.rs
- crates/batter-axum/examples/http_service.rs
- docs/guarantees.md
- docs/references.md

## Dependencies and consumers

Blocked by: batter-e6s — Separate core, Axum adapter, and SQLx example packages

Unblocks: batter-jne — Establish reference-service overload and operational evidence

Parent outcome: batter-8ct — Establish lifecycle and real-transport shutdown evidence. Parent-child is grouping, not a prerequisite on finishing the epic first.

## Verification and governing constraints

Work from the repository root. Read AGENTS.md, agent-map.md and the nearest package guide before editing. Native Rust/Tokio remains the foundation; Axum is a separate adapter, SQLx remains native application composition, and generic test support stays a leaf. Preserve downward cancellation, parent deadline clamping, inert factories, explicit replay authorization, report error retention and conservative cleanup after uncertain termination. Never automatically log application error/panic contents. Keep tracing context around polling and full future/span destruction. Do not install library global subscribers or panic hooks, recreate upstream queue/provisioning/storage engines, or infer publication/deployment permission.

Use a task-local ExecPlan under .agent/PLANS.md for sufficiently complex implementation. Its steps/evidence belong to this bead; it must not become a second backlog. Keep acceptance and status in Beads, behavior contracts in docs/guarantees.md and docs/integrations.md, implemented capability facts in docs/status.md, and executed evidence in docs/validation.md. New public APIs need rustdoc and a runnable or doctest example. Add meaningful failure-path tests without weakening existing assertions. Do not overwrite existing migrations or silently break queued/persisted formats.

title: Derive operation contexts from Runledger job executions
description:
## Outcome

Work inside a Runledger job handler runs under an `OperationContext` derived from the job execution, so the execution deadline and the runtime's abandonment of the invocation reach Batter operations without each application re-deriving them.

## Evidence (read-only two-consumer survey, 2026-09-27; consumers A and B are independently deployed downstream Tokio/Axum/SQLx/PostgreSQL services that pin Batter by Git revision; their identities and file paths are kept outside this tracker)

Three copies convert a job execution into a fresh root operation:
- the reference service: `execution.remaining_work_budget(FINAL_STATE_RESERVE)`, then `OperationOwner::new(budget)` and `into_context()` (`examples/reference-service/src/delivery/worker.rs:64-66`);
- consumer A: the execution deadline into `RootDeadline`, plus an `OperationError`-to-`JobFailure` mapping (about 60 lines across worker modules);
- consumer B: a fresh root sized from the remaining work budget.

`JobExecution` exposes a deadline and remaining budget but no cancellation signal (`runledger/runledger-core/src/jobs/execution.rs`). The worker enforces timeout and lease loss by returning from a `select!` and dropping the handler future (`runledger/runledger-runtime/src/worker/execution.rs:315-340`). Awaited nested operations are dropped with it, but a fresh root's cancellation token is never triggered, so work that observes the context rather than being dropped with the handler is not told the invocation was abandoned. Every consumer repeats the deadline and reserve arithmetic.

## Scope

- Runledger exposes a cancellation signal for the current invocation (lease loss, timeout and any runtime-initiated abandonment); its execution services already observe lease loss.
- `batter-runledger` derives an operation owner or context from `JobExecution`: the deadline is the execution deadline minus an explicit final-state reserve, and cancellation is linked to that signal.
- Optionally, a documented `OperationError`-to-Runledger failure classification that preserves concrete application errors.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Tests show lease loss and timeout cancel a derived context observed by spawned work, the derived deadline never exceeds the execution's, and an exhausted budget fails before work starts.
- The reference service delivery worker uses the bridge instead of a fresh root.
- ADR-010 invalid-state review, integration contract, status row and rustdoc are updated; bash scripts/verify.sh passes.

## Scope and ownership

Add narrow, std-based source reading, bounded value parsing, SecretString and value-hiding diagnostic mechanics under batter::settings. Keep setting names, defaults, precedence, unknown-field rules and required-secret decisions in application roots. No framework, DI registry, global subscriber, remote secret store, hot reload, second deployment validator or generic application error hierarchy. Retain concrete causes behind sanitized projections. No new workspace package or adapter dependency in the foundation. Coordinate the new module's public re-export with batter-tmx if its foundation extraction lands first; no artificial ordering dependency is required.

Reference policy and native constructors live in examples/reference-service/src/config.rs, exported through its existing library. The initial set covers HTTP bind/request deadline, separate Bulkhead and finite-process capacities, SQLx pool/connect options and all eight selected Runledger JobsConfig fields. Use native RequestPolicy::new, Bulkhead::new, Supervisor::with_process_capacity, PgPoolOptions, PgConnectOptions and JobsConfig::validate plus Runledger Supervisor::builder. Never route back through JobsConfig::from_env or builder_from_env. Runlimit policy/backend/subject-key settings remain batter-97p after upstream selection; no placeholder constructor here.

## Source and diagnostic contract

Defaults < explicitly selected dotenv file < captured process environment < explicit in-memory overrides. Helpers also accept injected OsString sources. Validate source structure before merging, then parse the winning value; malformed/unknown/duplicate source entries still fail, and invalid winners never fall back. Missing, empty and non-Unicode are distinct. Ignore unrelated environment variables, reject unknown reserved-prefix variables, and reject all unknown keys in dedicated files/overrides. Do not echo unknown keys or raw paths/values in automatic diagnostics.

Read only the selected path, with no ancestor search or environment mutation. No selected file means no file input; a selected missing/unreadable/malformed file is an error. The plan defines a bounded UTF-8 literal dotenv dialect (single-line KEY=VALUE, optional outer quotes, full-line comments, literal dollar/backslash, no interpolation/escape/export/multiline/inline-comment semantics); use one shared reader, not dotenvy's ambient substitution. Application source byte limits and policy are explicit. If another real validator is introduced, run shared accepted/rejected cases through both; do not create a deployment parser solely for testing.

Secret values, whole connection URLs, source maps and settings aggregates redact Debug/Display, including pretty/nested formatting. Keep original typed errors for explicit trusted source inspection, while ordinary stderr/tracing uses static field/category/reason metadata. Native PgConnectOptions Debug, intentional expose_secret/source-chain inspection, upstream runtime logs and the default panic hook are outside that projection; no process-wide secrecy, encryption or zeroization claim follows. Reject unknown connection URL parameters before SQLx can log their values. Use the plan's explicit URL subset and ambient PG* rejection/constructor policy instead of assuming new_without_pgpass is environment-free. Serve/setup required-password differences belong to the reference root; no invented provider/auth secret or generic library rule.

## Producer completion and consumer handoff

This task must deliver actual native constructor consumption now: adopt shared mechanics in the runnable HTTP example without adding a database dependency; pass configured capacity/deadlines through its real router; use reference config in live pool and existing worker-witness probes. Prove constructor mappings and changed runtime behavior with held work, timeouts and independent outcomes. A parser-only struct or a new config-printing executable does not meet acceptance.

Reuse completed Startup and cleanup reservations. Reserve before acquisition, register after success and before the next fallible stage, retain primary plus cleanup failures, and prevent Ready on failure. SQLx Pool::close returns unit; do not fabricate a close error to satisfy a test.

The full production command/root adoption and runtime effect belong to batter-kpd; hosted worker adoption and runtime effect belong to batter-0cp. Their implementation cannot silently replace constructor outputs with hardcoded defaults. Actual authorized pinned downstream migration remains acceptance of batter-7r3.6, not a blocker of this producer. Do not claim examples are deployed adopters or close the later tasks based on this work.

- crates/batter/src/validation.rs, admission.rs, lifecycle/process.rs, startup.rs and cleanup.rs

title: Expose bounded-cardinality operation and shutdown metrics
description:
## Outcome and rationale

Diagnostic metrics need bounded resources and must not add storage/lock requirements to business completion or admission.

## Scope and ownership

Select and version-check an optional existing metrics integration. Define finite operation/attempt/task/admission/cleanup label domains and bounded buffering/flush behavior. Scope noninterference to operational errors, backpressure and saturation of that selected integration. Existing tracing callbacks run synchronously: this does not promise isolation from arbitrary blocking/panicking user subscribers, runtime death or non-yielding destructors. Keep best-effort diagnostics separate from authoritative transactional audit events.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Names, units, aggregation, allowed labels and numerical bounds on retained observation resources are documented and tested; raw IDs/URLs/subjects/keys/errors cannot become labels.
- Slow/unavailable collector, queue saturation and malformed/negative timing inputs follow explicit drop/coalesce/error behavior; bounded resources and business/admission outcomes remain independently observable.
- Rejected-request storms cannot create an unbounded diagnostic write queue or a contended database row/lock prerequisite for business transactions.
- The selected operational failures do not change application results or admission decisions; report observation failures separately without recursive logging or retries that amplify load.
- No metrics backend/global subscriber becomes mandatory for core. Preserve owned-future dispatch/destruction behavior and state the arbitrary-subscriber fault boundary.

## Code and evidence entrypoints

- crates/batter-core/src/telemetry.rs
- crates/batter-axum/src/lib.rs
- crates/batter-core/tests/telemetry.rs
- docs/references.md

## Verification and governing constraints

For code/dependency changes, run bash scripts/verify.sh on the pinned local toolchain. It owns formatting, file budgets, both Clippy configurations, all six test-matrix parts, rustdoc and all HTTP smoke profiles. Do not repeat a successful run without changed source or prerequisites. Routine Rust 1.94.0 MSRV verification belongs only in CI. Current root AGENTS.md supersedes the historical local MSRV and Jig-gate commands. These commands do not substitute for this task's real database/provider/contract acceptance. Record exact versions, platform, prerequisites, commands and outcomes in the owning Bead; missing integration prerequisites fail the explicit target rather than silently passing. Read AGENTS.md, agent-map.md and the nearest package guide. New public APIs need rustdoc and an example; update the relevant contract, implemented-status row and owning Bead. Keep library domain errors concrete, cleanup explicitly awaited, Unix-only scope, and upstream queue/provisioning ownership intact. Do not commit, publish or deploy without an explicit request.

## Design evidence

description:

title: Persist versioned correlation and link real worker attempts
description:
## Outcome and rationale

Committed work outlives its request and may run after deployment; correlation must cross that boundary without becoming authorization or execution lifetime.

## Scope and ownership

Add the missing persisted request correlation and links to real worker attempts
through the existing reference submission and worker paths. DeliveryJobPayload
already has a version, owner, delivery identity and generation; the worker already
decodes it, checks authority/generation against current state and starts a fresh
OperationContext from its native execution budget. Reuse those mechanisms and the
completed provider reconciliation protocol, preserving their failure regressions.

Define a small validated versioned correlation representation with explicit bounds
and compatibility behavior for existing queued payloads without correlation.
Source it from server-generated request metadata, persist it with the original
submission, and link it to distinct native attempt identities after restart.
Correlation remains diagnostic: it grants no authority, replay permission,
deadline extension or ownership. Do not persist cancellation tokens, Tokio Instants,
credentials or arbitrary inbound trace/header values.

Preserve original command/effect identity and canonical provider payload matching.
Same-key replay with a new HTTP request ID must still reconcile the original command;
document which submission correlation is retained and how the replaying request is
observed without rewriting durable identity. Extend the current versioned format
compatibly; no second envelope/worker runtime or destructive migration is needed.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Real database execution through the existing producer and worker preserves bounded submission correlation across enqueue, restart and attempts. Each attempt has a distinct observable identity and its existing fresh native work budget; request completion/cancellation does not cancel committed work.
- Existing payloads without correlation, malformed correlation and unknown correlation versions have explicit compatible or terminal, redacted handling. No CancellationToken, Tokio Instant, credential or unvalidated inbound trace field is persisted.
- Preserve existing authoritative owner/generation checks independently of matching correlation, with negative cases proving correlation cannot authorize stale or wrong-owner work. Reuse existing provider fencing and reconciliation; no duplicate protocol is introduced.
- Same-key/same-payload replay with a different request ID preserves the original command and provider-effect identity and follows a documented correlation-retention policy; diagnostics cannot create payload conflicts or a second effect.
- Queued formats that can coexist have executable compatibility cases and staged/versioned handling. Submission metadata is persisted atomically with the existing command; existing migrations are not overwritten.
- Trace/attempt fields remain separate from authority and execution lifetime, have bounded encoding, and never become unbounded metric labels. Tests exercise actual propagation and redacted failure paths, not just serialization helpers.

## Code and evidence entrypoints

- examples/reference-service/ (existing unpublished application package)
- examples/reference-service/src/http.rs, src/delivery.rs, src/delivery/service.rs and src/delivery/worker.rs
- docs/integrations.md

title: Unify protected quota failure rendering and wire contract
description:
## Assessment

The confirmed interrupted-response inconsistency is an adapter composition gap. `request_admission` owns the caller-selected failure renderer and original request parts, but `HttpQuota::boundary` catches a nested `OperationContext` interruption after Axum has erased typed errors into a `Response`. It emits a fixed quota body before the outer operation is re-polled. A scratch nested-operation experiment reproduced the completion ordering. Repeating string mappings in the quota layer would preserve the same ownership split. The recommended remedy is an opaque request-scoped failure-rendering capability constructed by admission from the original parts and consumed by the inner adapter, with one typed failure classification. A public `RequestPolicy::render_failure` method plus caller-captured parts was considered but makes every adapter repeat the snapshot protocol; a response marker was considered but makes failure ownership implicit in a response extension.

The public-probe writer gap is a router assembly mistake: the root observer must cover every route, but `boundary` only claims the writer on protected routes. Public probe handlers therefore retain the capability. Claim and discard it before those handlers while preserving `NotChecked` telemetry. This needs no new observation authority API.

Quota response codes and HTTP consumption projection are contract and test omissions. Ad hoc string arguments make wire-code drift easy. Use a closed internal rejection kind with one status/code mapping, document its wire vocabulary, and cover live HTTP paths. Test all native backend consumption values through the HTTP projection. These do not justify redesigning native quota storage or policy.

## Acceptance

- A cancelled or expired nested quota operation uses the configured `RequestPolicy` failure renderer with the same sanitized code/status as outer admission; a deterministic protected HTTP test proves the boundary, including retained quota facts.
- Public probe handlers cannot claim or finish the quota observation writer; probes still report `not_checked`, and protected handlers retain their existing guarantee.
- Quota-owned rejections have one typed internal classification, documented status/code values, and HTTP tests asserting reachable JSON codes and no-store behavior. Unknown native denial retains a distinct other-denial code.
- HTTP observation tests cover Consumed, NotConsumed, and PossiblyConsumed backend failure projections without changing native quota ownership.
- Rustdoc, runnable examples, integration/status/validation evidence, and both supported toolchains remain coherent; no live PostgreSQL or Linux claim is introduced.

## Scope limits

Preserve existing quota admission, native atomic batch and public API behavior except correcting interruption rendering. Do not add Windows support, native storage, transaction or PostgreSQL lifecycle code. Do not commit, push, publish or deploy.
acceptance_criteria: Inner interruption uses RequestPolicy renderer; public probes cannot claim writer; quota response codes are typed, documented and tested; all backend consumption projections are tested; supported-toolchain validation passes.
close_reason: Protected quota HTTP boundary, probe capability, wire response, and observation repairs implemented and verified

title: Provide owned dependency-health sampling and fresh read-only observations
description:
## Observed mechanism

A downstream service decouples health measurement from HTTP traffic: one owned monitor performs non-overlapping probes, publishes an atomic result/time observation and invalidates readers on writer loss. Thousands of readiness/status reads start no additional database work. This is operational machinery rather than domain logic.

## Scope and owner

Add a narrow health facility to the batter foundation, with a non-cloneable writer/run owner and cloneable read-only observation handles. Accept an application probe and explicit probe budget, completion-to-next-probe delay, maximum age and scheduling margin. Validate their relationship and duration arithmetic together; do not bake an application's environment names or timing defaults into core. Return enough typed observation/lifecycle information for an adapter to distinguish initial, failed, stale and stopped dependency states without querying the dependency.

Integrate the run future with the existing Supervisor/ShutdownSignal ownership. Probe failure or timeout changes dependency health and permits recovery; it must not accidentally fail the critical component or permanently drain the process. Keep process readiness approval separate from dependency observations.

## Source and integration seams

- crates/batter/src/lib.rs and a new focused health module
- crates/batter/src/lifecycle.rs and existing supervised component examples
- crates/batter-axum/examples/http_service.rs as an adapter consumer
- docs/guarantees.md and docs/usage.md

No registry/service graph, database client, HTTP state, task per reader, per-reader queue or hidden detached task is introduced.

## Delivery requirements

Keep native futures and concrete application errors. The foundation has no SQLx/Axum dependency; generic test support remains a leaf. New public APIs need rustdoc, a runnable example, contract/status updates and failure-path tests. Recheck exact native-library APIs and versions against primary sources during implementation, recording references and actual Linux/macOS evidence without inventing hosted or minimum-version results. Use the repository's required verification and Jig gates. No code commit, publication or deployment is authorized by completing this task.

## Implementation handoff: 2026-09-09

On observed drain, stop admission of probes and drop the directly owned active probe before completing the monitor. Forced cancellation follows the same owned-future destruction rule. Test drain while probing, during delay and immediately before publication; lifecycle drain makes readiness unready regardless of cached success, and late completion cannot revive a stopped writer. This proves owned future destruction only, not detached tasks or remote SQL termination. The owner is an ordinary supervised run future; construction is inert and readers never spawn work.

## Dependencies and consumers

Blocked by: No unfinished prerequisite; activation conditions in this task still apply.

Unblocks: batter-7r3.6 — Prove operational helper adoption and remove duplicated consumer machinery; batter-7r3.4 — Provide opt-in Axum operational defaults with trusted request correlation

Parent outcome: batter-7r3. Parent-child grouping is not a prerequisite.
acceptance_criteria:
- Two thousand concurrent health reads produce zero extra probe attempts; at most one probe is active and delayed scheduling creates no catch-up queue.
- Probe timeout includes the whole application-supplied probe future; cancellation drops active work before monitor completion and dependent cleanup.
- Unknown, failed, expired and writer-stopped observations are unready; a stalled owner cannot extend freshness, and dropping the sole writer invalidates readers immediately.
- Successful observations recover after failures; process drain still overrides health without conflating probe failures with critical component failure.
- Invalid/overflowing timing policies fail before work begins; deterministic clock/barrier tests and a runnable consumer verify the public API.

Fifteen health tests, HTTP health/lifecycle tests, both Rust toolchain matrices (1.98.1 rustdoc corrected and rerun), and ten HTTP process smokes passed. title: Handle session temporary-schema authority explicitly in PostgreSQL verification
description:
Independent final comprehensive review source: Codex. Severity: medium. Blocks the conditional commit of batter-7r3.5.

The public verifier accepts an exact current temporary namespace as an ordinary schema. required.rs:114 uses nspacl/default owner entries and requests.rs:280 uses the generic ACL evaluator. PostgreSQL 18 pg_namespace_aclmask_ext instead gives the connection's own temporary namespace USAGE and derives CREATE from database TEMP authority, without grant options. The snapshot does not retain the session temporary-namespace discriminator. This is a library semantic-coverage gap, not a missing consumer instruction.

A parent-side external public-API probe against dedicated PostgreSQL 18.6 reproduced both errors with a real nonsuperuser login and max_connections(1). After creating a temporary table, native has_schema_privilege returns USAGE=true and CREATE=true. A policy requiring both returns two MissingPrivilege findings. Clearing the requirements and denying both schema privileges returns WithinDeclaredPolicy with zero findings. The normal database CONNECT/TEMP permissions are explicitly allowed. Source and final successful output: /tmp/batter-temp-review-probe/src/main.rs and /tmp/batter-temp-review-probe-final.log. The probe creates and explicitly drops its own table and login; no repository source was changed. Early probe attempts used session authorization on an admin-authenticated connection, then were corrected to a separate real login; an initial cleanup attempt raced server temp cleanup and the final probe explicitly drops the table first.

Primary source: https://github.com/postgres/postgres/blob/REL_18_STABLE/src/backend/catalog/aclchk.c (pg_namespace_aclmask_ext), checked 2026-09-13. Namespace initialization: https://github.com/postgres/postgres/blob/REL_18_STABLE/src/backend/catalog/namespace.c.

Recommended repair: classify session-dependent namespace semantics at capture, then either implement the native rule consistently for current required authority and login-reachable potential authority or return an explicit unsupported/incomplete result for that selected surface. Do not send temporary schemas through generic ACL fallback and do not merely exclude them silently.

Acceptance: native differential live regressions for USAGE/CREATE with and without database TEMP, current-role changes, explicit scope and reused pooled connections; required and excess paths agree with PostgreSQL or explicitly reject unsupported coverage; ordinary schemas remain unchanged; update supported-surface contract and both-toolchain/Jig evidence. No further repair is authorized by this finding; the user requested flagging medium-or-higher final findings.

title: Define PUBLIC relation-deny precedence over column defaults
description:
Independent final comprehensive review source: Claude. Severity: low. Follow-up to batter-7r3.5.

An exact PublicAllowance for Relation(R) with an empty privilege list does not suppress defaults.columns.public_privileges for discovered columns. authority/discovery.rs:273-285 expands each column independently, and authority/privileges/public.rs:97 accepts that default. Thus a PUBLIC column SELECT grant remains allowed when a consumer may expect the exact relation deny to cover its columns. The role-side RelationPolicy suppresses column defaults, while README says exact PublicAllowance entries replace PUBLIC defaults.

The source behavior is confirmed; whether a relation PUBLIC deny is intended to be hierarchical needs an explicit contract decision. No live reproduction was executed for this finding. Keep genuinely exact column exceptions expressible. Do not change policy interpretation silently.

Recommendation and acceptance: define relation/column PUBLIC precedence explicitly, align policy validation and discovery expansion with that rule, and add a regression combining nonempty column PUBLIC defaults, an exact empty relation override, and a native column-only PUBLIC grant. If relation deny covers defaults on columns, suppress those defaults while retaining deliberately explicit column exceptions. If the existing independent-object interpretation is intended, document the difference from role-side relation policy and test it. Revalidate required-privilege acceptance against the same precedence. No repair made during final review.

title: Extract optional SQLx PostgreSQL operation and connection-disposition support
description:
## Observed mechanism

A downstream SQLx 0.9 consumer reproduced pool starvation after dropping a blocked probe and failed setup cleanup during a blocked migration. Ordinary pool return can wait on a health ping behind interrupted SQL. Detaching/dropping an unsuccessful operation's client connection releases its pool slot while the server lock remains held; a successful operation returns its connection for reuse.

## Scope and owner

Introduce a narrowly scoped optional PostgreSQL/SQLx adapter package (batter-sqlx is a proposed name), independently selected by consumers. Inspect the pinned SQLx public API before choosing its operation/lease seam. Share explicit connection acquisition/disposition, a bounded probe composition and pool-close lifecycle registration without hiding PgConnection/Transaction boundaries or introducing repositories, a transaction manager or transaction replay. Decide safe native-failure classification while preserving original causes and operation interruption separately from replay policy.

The same adapter may supply explicit setup-only database creation/existence reconciliation: preserve the original create failure plus a failed existence recheck; never turn timeout into proof that creation failed or automatically perform setup during normal serving.

Verify this focused SQLx/PostgreSQL contract directly; completion of the Runledger/harness compatibility bundle batter-4t6 is not a prerequisite for the operation helper. Reuse its results when available. A real PostgreSQL test may use an explicitly configured external fixture; integrate the existing harness work when available rather than copying provisioning.

## Source and integration seams

- examples/postgres-lifecycle/src/main.rs and its manifest
- a new optional adapter package and nearest AGENTS.md
- crates/batter/src/operation.rs and cleanup/lifecycle registration seams
- docs/integrations.md, docs/references.md and package-boundary documentation

Retirement bounds client ownership, not remote SQL execution. Keep auth locks, commit semantics, migration contents and idempotency application-owned.

## Delivery requirements

Keep native futures and concrete application errors. The foundation has no SQLx/Axum dependency; generic test support remains a leaf. New public APIs need rustdoc, a runnable example, contract/status updates and failure-path tests. Recheck exact native-library APIs and versions against primary sources during implementation, recording references and actual Linux/macOS evidence without inventing hosted or minimum-version results. Use the repository's required verification and Jig gates. No code commit, publication or deployment is authorized by completing this task.

## Implementation handoff: 2026-09-09

Use an explicit separately invoked live test runner whose cases remain ignored during existing --all-features --all-targets checks; absent external PostgreSQL prerequisites fail the live invocation. Keep native SQLx 0.9 source/graph verification independent of the larger compatibility bundle.

Public disposition distinguishes client retirement/pool-capacity release from server-session quiescence. Detach removes connections from pool accounting; neither max_connections nor completed Pool::close bounds or proves termination of detached sessions. Capture each retired backend identity independently in live tests, prove local slot release/close while the blocker remains held, then release the blocker and observe session disappearance before fixture lease cleanup. Repeated interruptions record residual sessions instead of claiming a server-side concurrency bound. Do not expose raw connection internals beyond this explicit optional SQLx adapter contract.

## Dependencies and consumers

Blocked by: No unfinished prerequisite; activation conditions in this task still apply.

Unblocks: batter-4jz — Compose reusable isolated PostgreSQL leases with native pools; batter-kpd — Implement the reference command and atomic transactional submission; batter-7r3.6 — Prove operational helper adoption and remove duplicated consumer machinery; batter-7r3.5 — Provide read-only PostgreSQL schema and runtime-authority verification

Parent outcome: batter-7r3. Parent-child grouping is not a prerequisite.
acceptance_criteria:
- Real PostgreSQL regressions hold a server lock while cancellation/error retires a client connection; a one-slot pool admits independent work and closes within its declared local budget before the lock is released.
- Successful query and acknowledged transaction completion permit reuse; failure, panic and interruption have explicit disposition with no orphaned connection-capacity claim.
- Tests separately observe server-session disappearance after releasing its lock; no remote cancellation acknowledgement or rollback guarantee is inferred from local drop.
- Native errors remain inspectable with safe default diagnostics, and classifications do not automatically authorize retries or flatten uncertain commit into a replayable failure.
- Setup create/failure/recheck paths preserve simultaneous causes if included; normal startup performs no hidden creation/migration.
- Core and generic test support gain no SQLx dependency; existing native SQLx consumers can use the helper without adopting a repository/transaction abstraction.
notes: Completed optional batter-sqlx native lease/probe/cleanup registration and redacted causes. Real PostgreSQL 18.6 tests prove local replacement and close while blocked backends remain, then observe every retired session disappear after unlock; ten cases pass on Rust 1.94.0 and 1.98.1. Both verify matrices, all HTTP/PostgreSQL smokes and five final Jig targets pass. Final api:test receipt_01M23MPBGE3RJ254JFNWQQXKHQ. Optional setup creation is absent; no macOS/hosted/remote rollback claim or commit/publication. See docs/validation.md and plan_01M23KF4J87DZTKKK59Z1TYHK7.

title: Provide owned startup cleanup and reusable Unix service lifecycle composition
description:
## Observed duplication

The SQLx and HTTP examples and an inspected downstream executable each hand-compose successful acquisition, cleanup registration, partial-startup cleanup, readiness approval, Unix signal installation and shutdown-result interpretation. Losing the caller future between these steps must not be disguised as an asynchronous Drop guarantee.

## Scope and owner

Add the smallest startup/composition helpers around existing Supervisor, RunningSupervisor, OperationContext and CleanupStack. Define who owns/drives initialization and cleanup if the caller stops waiting. Keep registered resource ownership explicit; distinguish cancellation inside an acquisition that has not yielded ownership from cleanup of an already registered resource. Do not introduce a DI/service graph, blanket interruption masking or a second runtime.

Preserve a concrete startup error plus its cleanup report with a safe diagnostic projection and application-provided stage/reason metadata. Reuse existing shutdown-report semantics rather than mapping them to unconditional success. Extract reusable Unix signal setup/registration with installation failures reported before readiness. Axum serving remains adapter-owned; this task supplies the lifecycle seam it consumes.

## Source and integration seams

- crates/batter/src/lifecycle.rs and lifecycle/driver.rs
- crates/batter/src/cleanup.rs
- crates/batter/examples/support.rs
- crates/batter-axum/examples/support.rs
- examples/postgres-lifecycle/src/main.rs and src/support.rs

Reuse abandoned-startup and owned-driver regressions. The transitive component proof batter-zu8 is complementary evidence, not a reason to claim arbitrary descendants are owned.

## Delivery requirements

Keep native futures and concrete application errors. The foundation has no SQLx/Axum dependency; generic test support remains a leaf. New public APIs need rustdoc, a runnable example, contract/status updates and failure-path tests. Recheck exact native-library APIs and versions against primary sources during implementation, recording references and actual Linux/macOS evidence without inventing hosted or minimum-version results. Use the repository's required verification and Jig gates. No code commit, publication or deployment is authorized by completing this task.

## Implementation handoff: 2026-09-09

Test the ownership transfers after successful acquisition but rejected finalizer registration, and after initialization but before RunningSupervisor handoff. CleanupStack::push currently consumes the factory before rejecting invalid/duplicate names; reserve/validate registration first or retain explicit ownership that can drive the acquired resource cleanup on rejection. Preserve both registration and cleanup errors. Cancel the waiter at barriers on each side of the transfer and prove exactly one retained owner drives cleanup/reporting. Never-polled construction invokes no factory. Drain during initialization prevents Ready, including the final handoff. Keep these helpers narrow around existing owners rather than introducing a generic asynchronous bracket.

## Dependencies and consumers

- Failure after each acquisition/registration stage drives only acquired finalizers in reverse dependency order and retains the original failure and every cleanup outcome.
- Cancelled waiters, dropped owners, panic and never-polled startup each have an explicit tested owner/report outcome; no async cleanup is falsely reported from synchronous Drop.
- Signal listeners are installed before acknowledging initialization; installation failure follows startup cleanup, and SIGTERM/SIGINT use existing drain/cancel phases.
- Application readiness remains armed only after required initialization; owned-driver waiting/report handling preserves critical errors, forced abort, skipped cleanup and unjoined work.

Offer readiness composition over read-only dependency and lifecycle handles with explicit reason/severity policy. Expected Starting/Draining failures may use INFO; dependency failures while Ready retain WARN. Define Stopped separately rather than silently treating every non-Ready state alike. title: Provide read-only PostgreSQL schema and runtime-authority verification
description:
## Observed mechanism

A downstream serving process checks required SQLx migration versions/checksums without taking the migrator lock and rejects runtime credentials with broader effective authority than its declared policy. The current consumer implementation mixes reusable PostgreSQL catalog inspection with hard-coded schema/table exceptions.

## Scope and owner

Build optional PostgreSQL startup checks alongside the SQLx adapter. Accept the application's required migration bundle and explicit compatibility policy for additional migrations; never run DDL, migrations or permission repair during verification. Separate generic effective-authority inspection from an explicit allowed-capability policy supplied by the application.

Root authority at the actual login (session_user), accounting for inheritance, SET ROLE reachability, ADMIN OPTION, object ownership, table/column/sequence privileges and protected parameter authority in the supported PostgreSQL version. Provide structured findings/unsupported-surface reporting rather than claiming a universal secure-database verdict. Parameterize trusted schema/table/column expectations; copy no application names, grants or domain exceptions into the library.

## Source and integration seams

- optional adapter package from the SQLx operation task
- examples/postgres-lifecycle and future reference root
- docs/integrations.md, docs/references.md and real PostgreSQL tests

Migrations, runtime/setup principal selection, actual grant manifests, domain invariants and deployment changes remain application/operator decisions.

## Delivery requirements

Keep native futures and concrete application errors. The foundation has no SQLx/Axum dependency; generic test support remains a leaf. New public APIs need rustdoc, a runnable example, contract/status updates and failure-path tests. Recheck exact native-library APIs and versions against primary sources during implementation, recording references and actual Linux/macOS evidence without inventing hosted or minimum-version results. Use the repository's required verification and Jig gates. No code commit, publication or deployment is authorized by completing this task.

## Implementation handoff: 2026-09-09

Bound this first checker to the selected PostgreSQL 18 contract and enumerate supported capability surfaces in the public result. Distinguish WithinDeclaredPolicy, Violations and Incomplete/Unsupported; missing catalog access or an unsupported requested surface cannot produce WithinDeclaredPolicy. Run read-only catalog checks on the actual serving login/role connection in one explicitly documented consistent snapshot; the observation makes no guarantee after subsequent grants, role or schema changes. Include role attributes and PUBLIC grants within the declared surface, and state uninspected SECURITY DEFINER/extension behavior explicitly. No universal database-security verdict or automated repair. Recheck PostgreSQL 18 primary catalog/privilege documentation before writing queries.

## Dependencies and consumers

Blocked by: batter-7r3.2 — Extract optional SQLx PostgreSQL operation and connection-disposition support

Unblocks: batter-fms — Prove atomicity, idempotency and durable lifetime with real PostgreSQL; batter-7r3.6 — Prove operational helper adoption and remove duplicated consumer machinery

Parent outcome: batter-7r3. Parent-child grouping is not a prerequisite.
acceptance_criteria:
- Required migration absence, checksum mismatch and unsuccessful ledger entries reject startup; explicitly permitted later migrations coexist, and checks perform no DDL or migrator-lock acquisition.
- Real PostgreSQL cases exercise direct, inherited, SET ROLE and ADMIN OPTION authority plus login-hiding current-role options; the root login cannot conceal excess authority.
- Ownership, table/column writes and grant options, sequence mutation/grant options and protected parameter authority are tested against explicit allowed policies, including negative controls.
- Two different fixture schemas/policies work without source edits to the checker; no application-specific table names or immutable-ID exception is built in.
- Checks are bounded by caller operation policy, return structured safe findings, preserve native causes and state inspection limits; they never silently repair deployed permissions.
- A checker running inside cancellable work either accepts a caller-owned PgConnection or owns PgLease disposition itself; it must not hide acquisition of a raw PoolConnection. Only acknowledged success returns the connection for reuse. A one-slot blocked-query PostgreSQL regression proves local capacity recovery and bounded pool close separately from eventual backend termination.
