title: Render the application's not-found fallback outside boundary admission
description:
## Outcome

An application can render its own not-found body for unmatched paths outside
`HttpBoundary`'s admission, the way it already renders probe bodies outside
admission, so the fallback's status and envelope do not change with the process
lifecycle.

## Evidence (executed two-consumer port, batter-tc9w.9, 2026-09-30)

`HttpBoundary::assemble` installs the default route group's fallback inside that
group's admission: "Unmatched paths, including those under a nested fallback,
reach its fallback inside its admission"
(`crates/batter-axum/src/boundary.rs`). `HttpBoundary` has no counterpart to
`with_rendered_liveness`/`with_rendered_readiness` for the fallback, and
`AssembledHttp` is opaque, so a fallback cannot be added outside the assembled
boundary without abandoning the canonical registration helpers.

Consumer A documents "keep probes and fallback outside request admission" in
its HTTP guide. Its committed tests assert an unknown path's stable JSON
not-found envelope, including its machine-readable code and request id, while
the process is Starting and while it is Draining.

Consumer B's HTTP guide requires probes outside admission; it does not state
the same fallback requirement. Its unknown-route envelope test uses a router
that approves readiness before requests, so it does not establish fallback
behavior during Starting or Draining. B's reproduced port regression is the
missing response header on an unmatched path, described separately below.

Three original, unmodified consumer assertions failed against the ported surface.
In the first consumer:

1. A complete-router observation test asserting that `GET` of an unknown path
   answers 404 at INFO in every lifecycle state. Observed 503.
2. An in-process router integration test named for this contract - "startup and drain keep
   probes and fallback outside the gate" - asserting `GET /missing` answers 404
   with code `not_found` while Starting and while Draining. Observed 503 with
   the admission envelope `{"code":"service_unavailable","message":"The service
   is unavailable","request_id":...}`.

The second consumer failed the same root cause from the response-policy side.
Its surface applies a path-prefix response policy: every response under three
path prefixes carries `cache-control: no-store`, and two of them also carry
`referrer-policy: no-referrer`. The port expressed that policy as three route
groups with their own `BrowserPolicy`, which the boundary applies outside each
group's admission exactly as the original middleware did. Unmatched paths,
however, all reach the one default group's fallback, inside that group's policy,
so a 404 under a prefixed path silently loses the policy. An original,
unmodified assertion that every response in a suite carries
`cache-control: no-store` failed on `POST` of a retired route under a prefixed
path: 404 with `content-type`, `x-request-id` and `content-length` only. Because
only the default group may own a fallback, and it owns the only one, a
per-prefix response policy for unmatched paths is not expressible at all.

Declaring no fallback at all is not a substitute: the boundary then falls
through to Axum's built-in empty 404, which loses the application's code,
message and request id, and both consumers assert those fields.

## Reproducer

Assemble a boundary whose default group declares a fallback, before readiness
approval, and request a path no route matches:

```rust
let (control, approval) = ShutdownHandle::new_with_readiness_approval();
// No approval.approve(): the process is Starting.
let budget = ResponseConstructionBudget::new(Duration::from_secs(10))?;
let policy = RequestPolicy::new(control.operation_admission(), budget);
let assembled = HttpBoundary::new(policy)
    .with_liveness(ProbePath::new("/live")?)?
    .assemble(
        GuardedRouter::new()
            .route("/work", get(|| async { "ok" }))
            .fallback(|| async { (StatusCode::NOT_FOUND, "absent") }),
    )
    .await?;
let response = assembled
    .into_router()
    .oneshot(Request::get("/absent").body(Body::empty())?)
    .await?;
// Observed: 503 from admission. Wanted: the application's 404.
assert_eq!(response.status(), StatusCode::SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE);
let _ = approval;
```

`/live` still answers outside admission in the same state, which is the
behaviour the fallback needs.

## Ownership

Batter, `crates/batter-axum`. This is the canonical composition's own placement
decision, not application policy and not an upstream Axum constraint: the
boundary already merges probe routes outside every group and already reserves
probe paths in the guarded-route checks, so the placement and the renderer hook
both exist for probes.

## Scope

Decide and implement the fallback's placement before `batter-tc9w.2` seals
public composition. A fallback outside admission must not weaken the existing
invariants: it stays inside correlation and the single observer, its path must
keep taking part in the probe and group collision checks, and only the default
group may own one. If the placement is deliberate and must stay, record that
decision and the application obligation it creates instead, so consumers do not
rediscover it per surface.

This Bead blocks `batter-tc9w.2`. The initial `batter-tc9w.9` evaluation was
not authorized to change library code. The user subsequently expanded its
scope to implement this gap while preserving acceptance (comment 448); `.9`
also depends on this repair. The initial evidence above describes the original
pinned revision; implementation and current verification are recorded below.
acceptance_criteria: An unmatched path answers the application's own status, body and headers in every lifecycle state, or the placement is recorded as a deliberate decision with the consumer obligation it creates. A fallback outside admission stays inside correlation and the single observer, keeps taking part in the probe and group collision checks, and remains exclusive to the default group. Executed evidence covers Starting, Ready and Draining.

title: Correlate enqueue intents inside caller transactions for restricted roles
description:
## Outcome

A restricted application login can record a durable enqueue intent in its own transaction and later correlate the retained intent, promoted job and current definition inside a caller-owned transaction, without unscoped access to unrelated payloads, checkpoints or diagnostics.

## Evidence (read-only two-consumer survey, 2026-09-27; consumers A and B are independently deployed downstream Tokio/Axum/SQLx/PostgreSQL services that pin Batter by Git revision; their identities and file paths are kept outside this tracker)

- Migrated from the standalone Runledger tracker, where item "Add restricted caller-transaction intent evidence and recovery boundary" (affected revision d57ec6b) is still open and was never imported. `get_job_enqueue_intent_by_id_with_scope` (`runledger/runledger-postgres/src/jobs/queue/intents.rs`), `get_job_by_id_with_scope` (`jobs/admin/read.rs`) and `get_job_definition_by_type` (`jobs/queue/definitions/crud.rs`) are pool-level and decode full records. Exact idempotency recovery after `record_job_enqueue_intent_tx` needs direct SELECT on the whole intent relation.
- Consumer A correlates intents and jobs by reading Runledger tables from its own SQL (several migrations and a status query), coupling itself to native internals.

## Scope

Caller-transaction read APIs on the opaque transaction owner that return only the correlation fields an application may see, together with the grant fragment they need (see batter-qjxi).

## Acceptance Criteria

- Live tests show a restricted role correlating intent, job and definition inside its own transaction without SELECT on payload or checkpoint columns, including exact idempotent recovery after an unconfirmed commit.
- The standalone tracker item is closed or annotated with a pointer here when this lands.
- bash scripts/verify.sh and the live PostgreSQL suites pass.

title: Own service diagnostic completion and extract the bounded OTLP adapter
description:
Implement protected service completion, shared metric catalog, and optional OTLP adapter.

Evidence: reference runtime/completion.rs duplicates owner/observer/publication; runtime/orchestration.rs reconstructs coverage from native reports; metrics_export.rs::around retains the service result only on its stack through final export, so a diagnostic panic discards it. guard.rs duplicates Batter's catalog. Existing core startup and lifecycle already own cleanup and retain reports.

Design: add a core service boundary that consumes only ScopedStartup, owns startup through checked shutdown and diagnostic settlement, and retains native service outcomes independently before diagnostic finalization. Owner loss requests drain, wait cancellation is neutral, observers survive owner loss. Adapter extension traits are explicitly lower-level; supported diagnostics receive only an opaque settlement witness and expose no public early-flush or arbitrary-future runner. Preserve concrete startup errors and separate diagnostic task failures. Core computes coverage; application exit policy remains local. Centralize catalog schema/validation in core. Extract existing selected OTLP pipeline into opt-in batter-otlp, depending only on core and native SDKs. Keep environment schema, literal loopback policy, identity and timing selection in the reference application. Retain upstream aggregation/encoding and bounded transport behavior.

Execution graph: T1 protected core service lifecycle and panic-retention regressions; T2 core shared catalog validation; T3 optional adapter extraction depends on T1,T2; T4 reference adoption, contracts, verification inventory and Cargo-generated lockfile depends on T3. Work remains uncommitted. Existing public core startup APIs remain compatible; unpublished reference implementation can cut over directly.

Acceptance: protected startup/shutdown/finalization ordering, startup failure cleanup, owner/waiter separation, original service result survives installation/periodic/final diagnostic panics, catalog complete-series acceptance and early rejection, existing collector failure and payload bounds preserved, default graph excludes OTLP, new rustdoc/examples compile, no arbitrary future can serve as protected completion. Run focused failures then one successful pinned bash scripts/verify.sh. Record any unavailable live prerequisites accurately. Independent design review targets ownership and phase misuse; fresh-agent consumer evaluation remains unexecuted unless separately run. No publication/deployment.

Risks: synchronous SDK collection/closure and non-yielding callbacks cannot be preempted by async timeouts; do not strengthen wall-clock claims. Global recorder remains process-wide and explicit. Compatibility with app metrics requires opt-in catalog-only filtering. No runtime-death, remote delivery, or detached-task termination guarantee.

comments.text:
2026-09-27 PR #26 ADR-010 coupled-phase assessment, before dependent repair.

Both independent comprehensive branch reviewers confirmed a new invariant failure introduced by the report-shape repair in commit 6b187cf. In examples/reference-service/src/config/metrics.rs:123-125, the application wraps batter-otlp Prepared::install inside an async block to convert its report. Core service::start calls Diagnostics::install before startup.start, and the direct adapter's Prepared::install installs its recorder synchronously before returning a future. The wrapper delays that call until a spawned task is polled. On a current-thread runtime a competing recorder can take the global slot immediately after runtime::start returns; on a multithreaded runtime startup observations can precede installation. A synchronous installation panic would also be retained as TaskFailed instead of InstallationPanicked. These consequences are source-confirmed by both reviewers; a new runtime reproduction has not yet been executed. The prior 68-case live suite did not test the before-first-yield interval.

Cause classification: implementation mistake in the reference consumer's report conversion. The protected core boundary and the direct adapter already establish the required phase order, while the lower-level Diagnostics trait documents the synchronous-install obligation. The reference application's optional selection and four-case report mapping are its own policy. A generic library map-report/optional-diagnostics combinator could remove this caller obligation, but one local wrapper mistake does not yet justify a new public API or show that the direct adapter path is unsound. Another caller warning alone would not repair this case.

Recommended owner and bounded remedy: move the adapter install call outside the returned async block in the reference wrapper, then await and convert only the returned future; add a child-process regression that attempts a competing global recorder immediately after runtime::start returns, before any await, on both Tokio runtime flavors. Run the focused reference metrics target, complete local verifier and 68-case PostgreSQL live suite. If the same phase defect recurs after this repair, reassess a library-owned report-mapping capability. No separate design Bead is needed on current evidence. title: Define trusted request metadata and explicit propagation
description:
## Outcome and rationale

Existing HTTP span and renderer correlation is implemented; the remaining gap is trusted request metadata and explicit propagation in the reference root.

## Scope and ownership

Define typed correlation separately from OperationContext and application authority. Consume server-generated correlation from batter-7r3.4 through extensions and explicit arguments; validate any separately retained inbound request/trace metadata without allowing it to select server identity. The application owns authentication and trusted peer/proxy configuration. Default to ignoring forwarded identity from untrusted peers; if proxy trust is supported, its configured peer boundary is explicit. Introduce task-local ergonomics only for a real consumer with absence/spawn semantics, not as a prerequisite.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Forged forwarding, trace and request-ID headers cannot select principal, tenant or quota identity; test direct/untrusted input and every trusted-peer mode actually supported.
- Concurrent requests, missing metadata and cancellation do not exchange identity; handlers, failures and nested operations retain the intended correlation.
- Use the existing independent observe_http/request_admission composition and retained first-poll parent/dispatcher behavior; do not duplicate or reopen its closed implementation tasks.
- Any explicit spawned-work helper tests inheritance and absence; arbitrary tokio::spawn remains outside automatic propagation.
- Authorization is exercised through the production reference middleware seam; a correlation identifier is never a capability grant.
- The reference uses the shared request-correlation primitives from batter-7r3.4; generated response/header/body identity agrees while application authority and trusted-peer policy remain separate typed inputs.
- No duplicate server-ID, response-header or infrastructure-rendering implementation remains in reference middleware; application-specific authentication and durable metadata tests remain at their production seams.

## Operational reuse scope (2026-09-09)

batter-7r3.4 owns reusable trusted server request identity, correlation spans/headers, optional safe infrastructure rendering and readiness/serve composition. Consume that adapter API here instead of copying middleware into the reference. This task continues to own production authentication/trusted-peer policy and explicit propagation into application, quota and durable-submission paths. Correlation is diagnostic data; it must never substitute for principal/tenant authority. Keep the existing command prerequisite batter-kpd and add only the shared adapter prerequisite. The basic adapter remains independently deliverable without the durable reference.

## Code and evidence entrypoints

- examples/reference-service/ (new unpublished application package)
- docs/integrations.md
- docs/testing.md
- crates/batter-axum/src/lib.rs

## Verification and governing constraints

For code/dependency changes, run bash scripts/verify.sh and RUSTUP_TOOLCHAIN=1.94.0 bash scripts/verify.sh. Rebuild cargo build -p batter-axum --example http_service --locked and run python3 scripts/smoke_http.py --binary target/debug/examples/http_service in default, --signal SIGINT, --deadline, --warn-filter, and --warn-filter --deadline profiles. Finish backend work with scripts/jig check test and applicable Jig work gates. These commands do not substitute for this task's real database/provider/contract acceptance. Record exact versions, platform, prerequisites, commands and outcomes in docs/validation.md; missing integration prerequisites fail the explicit target rather than silently passing. Read AGENTS.md, agent-map.md and the nearest package guide. New public APIs need rustdoc and an example; update the relevant contract, implemented-status row and owning Bead. Keep library domain errors concrete, cleanup explicitly awaited, Unix-only scope, and upstream queue/provisioning ownership intact. Do not commit, publish or deploy without an explicit request.

## Design evidence

Re-audited against commit 22848ea on 2026-09-09. The HTTP observation series is complete. Historical authority failures came from trusting diagnostic/header values and cross-row identity, not missing spans. The retrospective sample establishes failure mechanisms, not defect rates or current application bugs. See docs/design-evidence.md for the anonymized rationale and implemented baseline. Delivery authority remains this Bead; historical ExecPlans are not another backlog.


## Dependencies and consumers

Blocked by: batter-kpd — Implement the reference command and atomic transactional submission; batter-7r3.4 — Provide opt-in Axum operational defaults with trusted request correlation

Unblocks: batter-kn4 — Prove validated API and generated client contract coherence; batter-7g0 — Persist versioned correlation and link real worker attempts; batter-97p — Compose upstream admission and sanitized observation in the reference API

Parent outcome: batter-faj. Parent-child grouping is not a prerequisite.

## Implementation handoff: 2026-09-09

Consume batter-7r3.4's typed server correlation and observation plumbing. This task owns authenticated application authority, trusted peer/inbound trace policy and propagation into application operations; do not create a second request-ID type/generator. Keep canonical command ownership independent of all correlation fields.

This was not a Batter adapter gap: a generic Router cannot advertise required extensions, and the adapter already provided constrained native peer registration. comments.text: Final ADR-010 assessment: the canonical production composition remained sound. The residual defect was the public test seam returning a servable Router, which left native peer injection as a prose-only caller obligation. Further comparison rejected the provisional feature-gating idea recorded earlier: it would hide the seam in normal builds but would not make misuse impossible when enabled and would complicate live integration builds. title: Retain all fixture failures through partial acquisition and teardown
description:
## Outcome and rationale

Fixture failures must retain their actual causes without deleting a database while native pool shutdown remains unresolved. The inspected harness lease queues database cleanup on Drop, so dropping a skipped finalizer is not retention.

## Scope and ownership

Extend the minimal probe fixtures from batter-4jz with an explicitly driven cleanup owner holding pools and leases. Start/retain that owner before yielding a cancellable waiter; waiter cancellation does not drop the lease or stop cleanup. After a bounded observation timeout, keep ownership in the fixture/suite driver and expose a pending result that can be awaited again. Do not call defer_cleanup or drop a captured lease before all connections close. Ordinary owner loss/runtime death has no cleanup-completion guarantee and must be documented/tested rather than described as safe skipping. Prove these mechanics without depending on a future application router; production composition fidelity belongs to batter-8q8.1, batter-8q8.2 and batter-fms.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Hold a real connection through the close observation deadline. Verify the database/lease is still retained while the cleanup owner remains live, then release the connection and observe Pool::close completion before lease cleanup. Cancelled waiters can resume observation of the same owner/result.
- SQLx 0.9 close returns (); distinguish timeout, cancelled observation and cleanup-owner join failure from a native returned error. Do not fabricate an SQLx close error or claim quiescence from dropped close futures.
- Preserve the original body failure together with actual cleanup failures. Awaited consuming lease cleanup and deferred-queue failure cases use their real separate paths/resources; do not assume the same consumed lease produces both errors. Synthetic boundary errors may test aggregation only when labelled as such.
- Continue independent cleanup after failure while retaining unresolved dependent resources. Explicit upstream defer is used only after connection quiescence; separately await deferred drain, including external mode where harness shutdown is a no-op.
- Assertion error, unwinding panic, cancelled waiter, partial acquisition and cleanup-owner loss have bounded tests naming what remains owned and driven. A pending outcome is not clean reuse; ordinary lease Drop is not a no-op and cannot satisfy skipped deletion.
- For the adapter from batter-7r3.2 (available through batter-4jz), test native SQLx PoolConnection::detach as the negative control. Use a separately budgeted observation connection outside the closing one-slot pool to track retired backend identities. Retain the lease until those sessions are observed quiescent too; Pool::close covers only tracked connections. Failed observation retains an unfinished owner/report instead of releasing the database.
- Reuse existing Script/finish for body and script-verification failures where applicable; shared adapter-owned result/cleanup mechanics are consumed by the minimal probe fixture. External adoption belongs to batter-7r3.6, without a reverse completion dependency.
- Generic batter-test-support gains no harness/foundation dependency. Reference consumers later keep actual config, router and transaction paths with substitutions only at selected external boundaries.

## Operational reuse scope (2026-09-09)

Reuse the existing generic Script and finish semantics for application/body-plus-verification failures instead of adding another assertion-result convention. Keep SQLx/harness-specific ownership and teardown composition in the adapter-owned support established by batter-4jz. ## Scope and ownership

Add a generated specification/client pipeline for the existing reference API,
using selected existing tooling whose source/version is checked at implementation.
Reuse SubmitDelivery validation, DTO/domain conversion, sanitized failure mapping,
DeliveryState and ProviderEffectState. Their implementation is the baseline; this
task supplies the missing generated contract and executable client round trips.

Describe the production wire behavior, including application JSON envelopes, native
extractor/plain-text errors, probes/fallback responses and any admission behavior actually adopted by that application.
The library adapter delivered by batter-97p is not evidence of reference adoption. Preserve the intentional distinction between queue status and provider
outcome, including uncertainty, exhaustion and manual resolution. Define client
polling behavior from those actual projections without inventing a new domain state.

Use the production configuration, authentication, trusted metadata and middleware
order, substituting only declared external boundaries. Any contract mismatch found
must be resolved explicitly against the existing behavior and compatibility policy;
generation must not silently tighten accepted application payloads, add header
requirements or normalize every rejection into one new error envelope.
Keep this first recipe application-owned; no endpoint DSL, universal error type,
bespoke generator or mandatory foundation schema dependency.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Generated request/response contracts match existing validation and safe wire behavior for malformed input, invalid domain combinations and declared enum vocabulary. Preserve intentionally unconstrained application JSON payloads; concrete internal causes cannot serialize into responses.
- Final generated and serialized specification retains required constraints/discriminants, with a negative control that loses a required constraint or producer variant. Generator success or client compilation alone is insufficient.
- Each exposed route/status/body/content-type and required header has a contract case and generated-client handling, including all three business routes, probes/fallbacks, native malformed-JSON/path/body-limit rejections and batter-97p's actual enforced/shadow/backend/capacity outcomes.
- Queue and provider states retain separate projections. Round trips cover pending, reconciliation, definite denial/success, cancellation, exhaustion and manual resolution, with declared terminal behavior that stops automatic polling/replay rather than inferring effect success from queue completion.
- Idempotency fields, same-key conflict, uncertain submission/effect outcomes and Retry-After presence/absence describe the real implementation. No annotation invents a required header or stronger guarantee.
- Tests retain production authentication, metadata, configuration and final admission/middleware order while replacing only selected external boundaries. Shared fixtures cover every producer variant claimed; preserve body/header correlation only where the actual envelope promises it.
- Compatibility checks cover introduced public/persisted formats. Reuse current validators and mappings, keep tooling application-owned and version-pinned, and add no speculative migration framework, comprehensive RFC claim or foundation schema dependency.

## Code and evidence entrypoints

- examples/reference-service/ (existing unpublished application package)
- examples/reference-service/src/http.rs, src/delivery.rs, src/delivery/service.rs and src/delivery/worker.rs
- docs/integrations.md
- docs/testing.md

Keep library domain errors concrete, cleanup explicitly awaited, Unix-only scope, and upstream queue/provisioning ownership intact. Do not commit, publish or deploy without an explicit request.

## Design evidence

Promoted P2 to P1 because recorded successful projections, generated schemas and incomplete shared fixtures contradicted actual domain/runtime behavior. The retrospective sample establishes failure mechanisms, not defect rates or current application bugs. See docs/design-evidence.md for the anonymized rationale and implemented baseline. title: Implement the reference command and atomic transactional submission
description:
## Outcome and rationale

A command is incomplete if it commits its business mutation independently of required durable work, or loses exact resource identity when a retry arrives.

## Scope and ownership

Implement a small generic reference command and query in examples/reference-service. The minimal scenario is delivery of a versioned generic record: a record has an application-owned owner and monotonically changing generation; POST /records/{record_id}/deliveries accepts expected_generation, an idempotency_key and a bounded payload, and GET /deliveries/{delivery_id} projects persisted state. Canonical identity binds the trusted owner, record, generation and payload. The first command creates a stable delivery identifier and upstream submission; exact replay preserves them. Initial records and replacement generations may be prepared by verified fixture/admin operations, not new public product features. The later provider task owns execution states; the command initially exposes accepted/conflict/uncertain outcomes without fabricating execution success. One native SQLx transaction owns the business record and upstream submission. Model a stable command identity, application-owned idempotency key and canonical payload comparison; give the target an explicit generation so stale work can be rejected. Preserve concrete success/conflict/uncertain-commit outcomes. Pass one OperationContext budget through pool acquisition and command execution with an explicit connection/transaction disposition policy. Use the config constructors from batter-5pm. Forward-only application migrations and upstream compatibility checks precede readiness. Do not add a repository abstraction, transaction retry manager or second queue.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The runnable command shares one visible native transaction for the business write and upstream submission; a query exposes durable identity and actual state.
- Request idempotency is scoped to the authenticated owner. Same-key/same-payload replay preserves identity; conflicting payload stays a concrete conflict. Another owner cannot alias that command by reusing its key; replay and status lookup enforce the same ownership as initial submission. Canonical comparison binds owner, target generation and meaningful payload; retention is explicit.
- The command targets the exact record/generation; stale ownership never silently applies to a replacement. Public success projection comes from a closed domain state representation.
- One total budget reaches pool acquisition and database work. Timing out a client future does not prove rollback or connection disposal; uncertain disposition is represented and documented.
- Commit acknowledgement loss remains an uncertain outcome with a query/reconciliation path; no automatic transaction replay is introduced.
- Production router/root uses the configured constructors and application-owned authentication seam; tests may replace a provider/auth boundary, but must not compile production authorization out.
- Focused checks accompany implementation; real transaction/concurrency proof is owned by batter-8q8.1 and combined acceptance by batter-fms.

## Code and evidence entrypoints

- examples/reference-service/ (new unpublished application package)
- docs/integrations.md
- docs/testing.md
- docs/usage.md

## Verification and governing constraints

For code/dependency changes, run bash scripts/verify.sh and RUSTUP_TOOLCHAIN=1.94.0 bash scripts/verify.sh. Read AGENTS.md, agent-map.md and the nearest package guide. New public APIs need rustdoc and an example; update the relevant contract, implemented-status row and owning Bead. Keep library domain errors concrete, cleanup explicitly awaited, Unix-only scope, and upstream queue/provisioning ownership intact. Do not commit, publish or deploy without an explicit request.

## Design evidence

Re-audited against commit 22848ea on 2026-09-09. Historical failures included nested pool acquisition, stale lifecycle targeting, split commit boundaries and false successful projections. The retrospective sample establishes failure mechanisms, not defect rates or current application bugs. See docs/design-evidence.md for the anonymized rationale and implemented baseline. Delivery authority remains this Bead; historical ExecPlans are not another backlog.


## Dependencies and consumers

Blocked by: batter-5pm — Provide typed root configuration and redacted secret handling; batter-4t6 — Verify compatible SQLx, durable-runtime and database-harness APIs; batter-7r3.2 — Extract optional SQLx PostgreSQL operation and connection-disposition support; batter-7r3.3 — Provide owned startup cleanup and reusable Unix service lifecycle composition

Unblocks: batter-8q8.2 — Demonstrate provider outcome certainty and restart reconciliation; batter-8q8.1 — Prove reference command atomicity and concurrent identity; batter-kn4 — Prove validated API and generated client contract coherence; batter-8jr — Provide application-root exporter setup and ordered flush; batter-7g0 — Persist versioned correlation and link real worker attempts; batter-in2 — Define trusted request metadata and explicit propagation; batter-97p — Compose upstream admission and sanitized observation in the reference API; batter-fms — Prove atomicity, idempotency and durable lifetime with real PostgreSQL; batter-0cp — Host the upstream worker with acknowledged startup and drain

Parent outcome: batter-8q8. Parent-child grouping is not a prerequisite.

## Implementation handoff: 2026-09-09

Consume the optional SQLx disposition API from batter-7r3.2 and startup ownership helper from batter-7r3.3 in the command root; do not implement competing connection-retirement or startup-cleanup machinery. Use package batter-example-reference-service and the verified enqueue_job_with_outcome_tx native transaction path at READ COMMITTED. Map the trusted owner explicitly into upstream organization/global idempotency scope and persist immutable canonical enqueue fields so replay cannot change initial scheduling fields. Compose forward-only application and upstream migration entrypoints with the compatibility manifest; repeated startup with both histories is a required case.

Add GET /delivery-commands/{idempotency_key} scoped to the authenticated owner as the public reconciliation path available before POST returns. This path requires no response-generated delivery_id and never dispatches an effect. Bound/validate the key consistently with POST. Return the existing delivery projection when visible, a caller-safe not-observed response when absent, and explain that absence while the original transaction may resolve does not certify rollback. POST exact replay can return the same canonical delivery; mismatched payload remains conflict. Test foreign-owner isolation and resolve the same retained key after lost acknowledgement. An in-process SQL assertion alone is not public reconciliation.

Define the authoritative write set as record/delivery state, canonical command identity and upstream submission. Do not add a separate audit/event subsystem solely for downstream test wording. Worker setup consumes this declared job type/payload; provider execution is added by batter-8q8.2.

## Configuration producer handoff: 2026-09-10

Current worktree exposes `batter_example_reference_service::config::{RootSettings, PoolSettings, WorkerSettings, ConfigMode}`. `RootSettings::from_process(mode, selected_file, overrides)` owns source loading; `request_policy`, `pool_options`, `connect_options_from_process`, `bulkhead`, `supervisor` and `worker().builder` are the concrete native handoff methods. This is an implementation handoff, not producer closure or this consumer's full-root/runtime acceptance. Existing acceptance and dependency direction remain unchanged. See `.agent/plans/batter-5pm.md` and the reference README for required PG*/passfile policy and the selected graph's unverified TLS negotiation.

Final source passes both Rust 1.98.1 and 1.94.0 verify matrices, all ten HTTP smokes, package tests/doctests/Clippy, strict Python controls, and both 42-case PostgreSQL 18.6 live inventories. title: Protect startup ownership for agent-first consumers
description:
## Purpose and observed problem

An agent composing a native Rust/Tokio service should select owned startup,
register components and native dependencies, and await the outcome. It should
not reconstruct Unix signal routing between startup and the running driver,
manually repair a rejected finalizer registration after acquiring a PostgreSQL
pool, or receive ownership-changing methods merely to register a component.

Current baseline is 809d5d5b913d26497232f13682b334e1c4aec806. The reference service
manually installs signal listeners, selects reception against initialization,
requests drain and transfers listeners. The PostgreSQL demonstration installs
signals only after connecting and probing. StartupScope::supervisor exposes
take_cleanup, replacement and start through a mutable Supervisor. SQLx
register_pool_close explicitly leaves rejected-registration cleanup to callers.
Documentation/tracker-only work subsequently advanced HEAD to
39c1b6e3c1c75f808becb5a5e7c33f58001a2ee4. Keep that historical research baseline
separate from each task's actual implementation revision.

These are three related API gaps, not proof all existing behavior is incorrect.
Command already owns callback/finalizer execution; managed Runledger registration
already retains native settlement. Preserve those mechanisms and their tests.
No generic resource graph, ORM, global subscriber, effect DSL, alternate queue,
new provisioning service or second lifecycle driver belongs in this change.

## Selected architecture

1. A concrete borrowed Registration capability contains private access to the
   existing Supervisor registration operations. It offers component registration,
   managed-adapter registration and finalizer reservation, never start,
   run_until, cleanup extraction, replacement or a conversion to Supervisor.
2. A small sealed RegistrationTarget trait exposes only a reborrowed Registration.
   New adapter entrypoints register_http_in and register_in accept it, so protected
   scopes pass directly. Preserve the original adapter signatures; changing them
   to generics breaks existing DerefMut coercion callers. Both names share the
   same registration implementation. Applications need not implement the trait.
3. Introduce additive Startup::scoped and ProtectedStartupScope over the existing
   engine. Preserve existing Startup::new and StartupScope for source compatibility
   as explicitly lower-level paths. The canonical new scope has direct
   reserve_cleanup and registration access, no unrestricted supervisor accessor.
   Its start result uses InitializationError<E> from its first delivery, so later
   signal support does not change the protected path's public error type.
4. An opt-in Unix signal policy belongs to protected startup. Its configuration
   is inert. Starting synchronously validates/reserves the signal name and
   installs SIGTERM/SIGINT before returning the startup owner; the owned engine
   observes reception during initialization and carries sources into running
   supervision without a fallible application handoff.
5. A synchronous SQLx pool constructor consumes an already validated CleanupSlot
   plus native PgPoolOptions/PgConnectOptions, constructs the native pool and
   registers close before returning. Name it batter_sqlx::pool_in. Connectivity
   checks remain explicit native queries or the existing bounded probe. The async
   alternative was tested but is not selected for this delivery.
6. Real example adoption and a fresh public-guidance consumer task complete the
   delivery. Library tests alone do not establish discovery or modification
   usability. No future adapter, publication or production readiness is implied.

## Rationale and rejected directions

Concrete capability: a private borrowed view removes exactly the dangerous
operations while leaving native futures and lifetimes visible. A service locator
or trait hierarchy with resource types would add unrelated design obligations.
Direct scope.reserve_cleanup avoids a temporary-view lifetime trap when a slot
must survive native acquisition across an await.

Sealed adapter target: existing Axum and Runledger functions take &mut Supervisor.
A public trait returning only this view need not violate ownership; sealing fixes
the supported target set and avoids promising arbitrary downstream implementations.
A sealed conversion to a concrete view retains
new call expressions and gives adapters one registration implementation.
A compiled counterexample shows that an application DerefMut wrapper previously
accepted by an &mut Supervisor parameter fails E0277 at a generic target parameter.
Keep old functions/signatures and add register_http_in / register_in using the
sealed capability. Test both function-pointer and coercion compatibility.

Staging: there is recorded downstream adoption even though publishing is disabled.
Removing StartupScope::supervisor immediately would break existing consumers and
conflict with repository public-contract staging guidance. Keeping that method on
the new canonical scope would leave the finding unresolved. A distinct protected
projection over the same engine is the bounded compatibility option. Document
the lower-level old path without presenting equivalent ownership constraints.

Signal installation: an initializer wrapper can receive signals during its
callback but not before the coordinator first polls. A real subprocess negative
control observes SIGTERM terminating that interval without cleanup. Synchronous
installation at the explicit start boundary covers the owner-return interval;
it does not cover earlier application startup before start is called.
Tokio signal installation is process-global and is not restored on listener Drop.
Keep the policy opt-in; do not claim independent/exclusive process signal ownership.

Signal reservation: current install_signals checks a name without reserving it.
The initializer can claim the same name before transfer. Reserve before invoking
the application factory and fulfill internally without another user-visible
registration failure. Do not fake a critical component that has no real owner.

Signal errors: preserve old public error enums and exhaustive matches. Protected
startup uses a new redacted, non-exhaustive InitializationError<E> envelope with
Application(E), Signals(SignalRegistrationError), and SignalPolicyAlreadySelected,
inside existing StartupError/StartupFailure. Freeze this shape in A, even without
signal configuration; B must not change the typed start result or observer APIs.
Repeated selection is its own category, not a misleading duplicate task name.
The original application and IO causes remain inspectable without application
From conversions. A received signal uses existing Draining classification.
Changing existing StartupCause with a new variant is not source-compatible.

Pool creation: SQLx connect_lazy_with can spawn maintenance/min-connection work.
It is not inert. The guarantee is registration in the same synchronous operation
before the returned pool or a later application await, not absence of native work
during construction. Accept native option objects; do not parse URLs, reread PG*
environment, overwrite callbacks/options, or import settings policy into SQLx.

Async pool alternative: acquiring one connection does not reproduce SQLx
connect_with's min_connections behavior, and does not prove SELECT 1 or schema
readiness. A second supplied OperationContext recreates deadline-composition
choices. Prefer the synchronous ownership primitive plus existing probes unless
future separately authorized consumer experiments establish a concrete advantage.
The completed comparison preferred pool_in; no async helper is in this delivery.
## Delivery graph

A = constrained registration plus protected startup projection, with adapter
interoperability and compatibility controls. No blocking prerequisites.
B = startup-owned Unix signal policy and process failure contracts. Depends on A.
C = slot-consuming SQLx pool ownership primitive and native tests. Independent A/B.
D = real application cutover and public-guidance consumer acceptance. Depends A/B/C.

Each task owns its tests, current docs and required verification. D delivers actual
consumer adoption rather than a detached test-only gate. The epic closes only after
all four tasks satisfy acceptance. No planning/review/Beads-conversion tasks exist.
Related coordination: batter-tmx facade relocation, batter-7r3.6 operational adoption,
batter-7r3.8 fixture pool profiles, and completed/concurrent batter-fbd documentation.
Do not make any of them artificial blockers. Resolve current physical paths at
implementation time; public foundation type identity must remain single-copy.
Do not edit or close those independently owned Beads merely to complete this epic.

## Owning delivery graph

Epic batter-lp2 owns this outcome. A=batter-lp2.1, B=batter-lp2.2, C=batter-lp2.3, D=batter-lp2.4.
Blocking edges: B depends on A; D depends on A/B/C. A and C are independently
ready. Parent-child grouping and related coordination are not blocking edges.
Facade relocation batter-tmx, broad adoption batter-7r3.6, fixture pool profiles
batter-7r3.8 and closed documentation convergence batter-fbd are related only.
Resolve current source paths at implementation; preserve one foundation type
identity and do not close or broaden unrelated Beads.

## Historical experiment evidence

Read docs/evidence/agent-startup-apis-2026-09-12/README.md for source-bound
prototype results, first-attempt failures, public consumer trials and limitations.
The archive is evidence, not production implementation or a required dependency.
Three fresh consumer agents each attempted an initial and modification task;
one made a within-agent pool A/C comparison. No reliability rate is established.
Signal name reservation, the final error envelope and combined protected production
composition remain proposed acceptance. Linux/Rust 1.98.1 experiments do not
replace this task's required production verification or macOS evidence.

## Planning review and handoff record

Planning-workflow completed four sequential plan review rounds: two collaborative
review agents, a fresh read-only Codex architecture review, and root integration
review. Fresh standalone checks covered B, C, A and D. The first D check required
more precise acceptance; its expanded task passed a new fresh-context recheck.
No external GPT Pro web session or fourth independent architecture model is claimed.

Round 1 fixed the protected error envelope in A, removed C's hidden A dependency,
and omitted a new parent-cancellable context accessor. Round 2 retained synchronous
preflight failures across owner loss and added opt-out/native-constructor controls.
Round 3 clarified recorded-configuration-error precedence and the reference root's
explicit boxed-error downcast cutover. Round 4 fixed exact predecessor handoffs,
real process versus harness statuses, a named eight-case integration delta, and
bounded source-preserving consumer evaluation. These refinements reached stable
architecture and graph; no meta-planning or review task was created.

DAG and five architectural rationales were checked between rounds. The standalone
Beads include their relevant shared contracts, signatures, failure protocols,
source anchors, verification and completion requirements. Historical source-bound
experiments are in docs/evidence/agent-startup-apis-2026-09-12/README.md. Their
successful prototype checks do not close any implementation acceptance.

Close this epic only after all four child delivery outcomes pass. Commit, push,
publication, deployment and unrelated upstream or tracker changes require their
own authority. Planning created delivery scope, not production Rust changes.
acceptance_criteria: All four concrete delivery tasks satisfy their code, contract, consumer and verification acceptance. Protected startup constrains registration authority, owns opt-in Unix signal handling, and composes slot-owned native SQLx pools in actual consumers. Preserve explicit compatibility and failure-report boundaries; no release or deployment is implied.
notes: Planning-workflow completed four sequential architecture/integration review rounds with fresh standalone checks; the initial D check required acceptance expansion and its amended task passed a fresh recheck. Six delivery-graph passes: (1) searched existing open/closed inventory for duplicate ownership scope; (2) checked each node delivers code/docs/tests rather than planning ceremony; (3) verified exact blocking direction B<-A and D<-A/B/C; (4) verified br ready exposes only A and C among the new children; (5) traced all three requested debts through terminal canonical-consumer adoption D without facade/profile artificial blockers; (6) exact br show readback verified all descriptions, acceptance fields, P1 open metadata, parent-child links and four blocking edges. Active blocking cycle count is zero. Related edges preserve facade, broad adoption, fixture profile and closed docs coordination. Source-bound Linux prototypes and three fresh consumer trials are recorded in docs/evidence/agent-startup-apis-2026-09-12/README.md. No production Rust implementation, commit or publication was performed. Tasks remain open; no execution acceptance was pre-closed by prototype results.

Resolve current source paths at implementation; preserve one foundation type
identity and do not close or broaden unrelated Beads.

## A: Restrict canonical startup to registration authority

Outcome: applications and native adapters register work and finalizers without
receiving the enclosing Supervisor or its cleanup stack. Existing public clients
remain buildable through the explicitly lower-level compatibility path.

Entry points: crates/batter/src/startup.rs and startup/driver.rs; lifecycle.rs;
crates/batter-axum/src/serving.rs; crates/batter-runledger/src/lib.rs; relevant
crate guides; public rustdoc and compile-fail integration tests.

Implement a private-field Registration<'a> borrowing the actual Supervisor.
Forward component and managed registration to current validated ownership logic.
Expose no Deref/DerefMut, AsRef/AsMut, Borrow/BorrowMut, public constructor or
unsealed trait path that recovers Supervisor. Do not return a takeable CleanupStack.
Provide direct scope reserve_cleanup so reservation can cross native awaits.
Publish exact paths batter::registration::{Registration, RegistrationTarget} and
batter::startup::ProtectedStartupScope. Expose stage, reserve_cleanup and
registration, but no new context accessor. Native adapters receive a context
explicitly captured at the composition root as they do today; a new parent-
cancellable OperationContext clone would expand this capability's authority.
Control handles captured by applications before startup remain outside this
capability's prohibition; do not claim the view makes arbitrary code pure.

Add a protected scope and constructor over the same existing owned coordinator.
Do not copy failure cleanup, report publication, handoff or dispatch protection
into a second driver. Keep old signatures and concrete types as legacy entrypoints.
The canonical spelling is Startup::scoped. An isolated compiling prototype shares
the old driver through one callback projection with no visible lifetime parameter
or second coordinator. The implementation task must preserve public compatibility.
Freeze StartingSupervisor<InitializationError<E>> for this new path in A while
leaving legacy Startup::new's E unchanged. Map callback errors at the poll boundary
so the concrete E is retained before destroying the completed inner future;
a naive async await wrapper can lose that E if future destruction panics.

Add register_http_in and batter_runledger::register_in accepting the sealed target;
retain exact existing register_http/register signatures as forwarding compatibility.
Both paths must enter the same native registration logic, not duplicate it.
Cover Axum and Runledger. A may refactor Unix internals privately only to preserve
existing helper behavior; new protected signal policy, reservations and public
signal API belong exclusively to B. SQLx slot construction does not need access
to a Supervisor. CommandScope remains unchanged unless a shared
private helper avoids real duplication without expanding public authority.

Acceptance scenarios:
1. Old minimal consumer, DerefMut-coercing adapter consumers and typed adapter
   function-pointer fixtures still compile. Check in and compile a typed protected
   start/observer consumer now; B must preserve and rerun it unchanged. A does not
   wait for B to establish its own acceptance.
2. New owned startup adds a real channel component and finalizer; actual request
   succeeds, shutdown joins the component, then releases the dependent resource.
3. Native Axum listener/router and prepared Runledger register through the new view.
4. Duplicate/invalid names invoke no application factory and release rejected captures.
5. Extracting cleanup, starting/replacing the process and escaping the view beyond
   initialization all fail compilation for the intended reason.
6. A positive baseline shares dependencies/imports with each compile-fail subject;
   unrelated compiler errors cannot count as protection.
7. Reborrowing registration for successive helpers works, and direct reservations
   cross acquisition awaits without a temporary-value lifetime error.
8. Partial startup error, callback panic, destruction panic and owner/waiter loss
   retain current cleanup/error/redaction behavior.
9. Managed pending settlement and uncertain descendant outcomes still skip cleanup.
10. Exact supported toolchains, docs and required Jig evidence pass.

No closure claim from compile-fail controls alone: runnable native composition is
required. No public new API without rustdoc and a complete example.
## A: Concrete implementation and acceptance appendix

### Source ownership

- `crates/batter/src/startup.rs`: preserve legacy `Startup::new`, `StartupScope`,
  `StartupFuture`, `start` and readiness-selection behavior; add the protected
  projection, direct `stage`/`reserve_cleanup`/`registration`, and the new scoped
  constructor. Publish `InitializationError` through `batter::startup` explicitly
  alongside the named protected scope, and document the entire typed result.
- `crates/batter/src/startup/report.rs`: add the redacted non-exhaustive envelope;
  leave existing public report enums and their variants intact. Preserve
  unbounded formatting implementations for arbitrary concrete E; `Error`
  implementation may remain conditional on E implementing `Error`.
- `crates/batter/src/startup/driver.rs`: retain a single owned coordinator,
  monitor, handoff channel, report publication and cleanup implementation. Map
  `Poll::Ready(Err(E))` into the envelope before the inner future is destroyed.
  The existing explicit poll/catch/drop sequence at lines 213–220 is the relevant
  boundary; an ordinary async `await` mapping is not an equivalent substitute.
- New `crates/batter/src/registration.rs` and its `lib.rs` export: sealed target
  and private borrowed view. Reuse `Supervisor::register`, `register_managed`
  and `reserve_cleanup`, including existing name validation and factory timing.
- `crates/batter-axum/src/serving.rs:57` and
  `crates/batter-runledger/src/lib.rs:80`: retain the exact old functions and put
  the native registration body behind one common implementation per adapter.
  Add new `_in` entrypoints that receive the supported target/view. Do not change
  native Runledger's inert prepared-to-live transfer or report mapping.

### Observable acceptance

1. Add a protected-path counterpart of
   `failed_initialization_preserves_concrete_cause_and_lifo_cleanup_errors` in
   `crates/batter/tests/startup.rs`. Assert the actual nested
   `StartupCause::Failed(InitializationError::Application(Failure))`, stage,
   reverse resource events, both cleanup errors and pointer-identical retained
   observer report. Formatting must exclude the known private cause marker.
2. Extend the custom future used by
   `application_failure_and_future_destruction_panic_both_survive`: protected
   future returns a concrete marker error in `poll` and panics in `Drop`.
   Require both the marker and separately inspected destruction payload, plus
   completed prior-resource cleanup. This catches the tempting async mapping.
3. Reuse the owner/waiter gates from
   `borrowed_waiter_cancellation_leaves_initializer_and_handoff_owned`,
   `owner_drop_during_initialization_drives_registered_cleanup_exactly_once`
   and `owner_drop_before_first_poll_skips_factory_and_drives_existing_cleanup`.
   These require independent counters/events and reports; resolving a waiter
   alone is insufficient.
4. A real channel service owns a resource while it handles a request. Require
   response 42 to input 21, readiness after actual component initialization,
   then component exit before resource finalization, exactly one release, and a
   successful complete shutdown report. Keep the sender alive until shutdown so
   an accidental early critical exit cannot masquerade as ordinary shutdown.
5. Exercise real Axum listener/router registration in
   `crates/batter-axum/tests/operational/serving.rs` or a focused adjacent test.
   Make an actual request, inspect response, then await complete shutdown. For
   Runledger add new-view coverage in `crates/batter-runledger/tests/lifecycle.rs`
   with prepared native ownership. A must execute a protected counterpart of
   `native_local_initialization_requires_no_database_or_durable_witness`: the
   closed lazy pool and native local loops require no database endpoint. Assert
   acknowledged readiness, complete native loop settlement and clean shutdown.
   D owns the combined database-backed reference runtime acceptance.
   Existing foundation managed tests remain relevant regression evidence:
   pending settlement, classifier/destructor panic and uncertain cleanup
   skipping must continue to pass. Merely compiling `PreparedSupervisor` is not
   a substitute for the task's native runtime acceptance.
6. Give rejection tests independent side-effect and capture-drop counters.
   Attempt a duplicate ordinary component and a duplicate managed component
   through the view; assert returned name error, no rejected factory execution,
   and release of inert rejected captures. Invalid names get the same control.
7. Retain dispatch coverage in `crates/batter/tests/scoped_owned_tasks.rs` and
   `scoped_dispatch.rs`: initializer polling and full destruction, including
   nested instrumented spans, must remain in the captured dispatch. Use existing
   shared dispatch construction rather than introducing a global subscriber.

### Compilation controls

Check supported tools against fixtures that actually use the public imports and
dependencies. Preserve old direct calls, old `&mut Supervisor` function-pointer
assignments for both adapters, and calls with a wrapper implementing
`Deref<Target = Supervisor>` plus `DerefMut`. Also preserve legacy exhaustive
matches over existing startup error/cause enums. Add an explicit new type fixture
whose owner and observer are `StartingSupervisor<InitializationError<Concrete>>`
and `StartupObserver<InitializationError<Concrete>>`; B must keep it unchanged.

Positive protected fixtures should cover `&mut ProtectedStartupScope` passed
directly to both new adapter functions, a retained/reborrowed `Registration`,
successive helper calls, and a directly reserved slot held across native await.
Use a concrete Send+Sync error that does not implement `Error` for a compile
fixture to prevent the envelope from strengthening the start method's bounds.

Pair each negative subject with its own working baseline. Reject extraction,
driver start, supervisor replacement, conversion to `Supervisor`, forged target
implementation and registration escape to a `'static` spawned task. Require the
diagnostic to point to that attempted operation and its appropriate method,
type, lifetime or sealed-trait boundary. A missing import, unsupported toolchain
or unrelated fixture error never establishes protection. Do not require a
particular incidental compiler error count.

## Error-envelope contract fixed by this task

Signal errors: preserve old public error enums and exhaustive matches. Protected
startup uses a new redacted, non-exhaustive InitializationError<E> envelope with
Application(E), Signals(SignalRegistrationError), and SignalPolicyAlreadySelected,
inside existing StartupError/StartupFailure. Freeze this shape in A, even without
signal configuration; B must not change the typed start result or observer APIs.
Repeated selection is its own category, not a misleading duplicate task name.
The original application and IO causes remain inspectable without application
From conversions. A received signal uses existing Draining classification.
Changing existing StartupCause with a new variant is not source-compatible.

## Selected architecture

1. A concrete borrowed Registration capability contains private access to the
   existing Supervisor registration operations. It offers component registration,
   managed-adapter registration and finalizer reservation, never start,
   run_until, cleanup extraction, replacement or a conversion to Supervisor.
2. A small sealed RegistrationTarget trait exposes only a reborrowed Registration.
   New adapter entrypoints register_http_in and register_in accept it, so protected
   scopes pass directly. Preserve the original adapter signatures; changing them
   to generics breaks existing DerefMut coercion callers. Both names share the
   same registration implementation. Applications need not implement the trait.
3. Introduce additive Startup::scoped and ProtectedStartupScope over the existing
   engine. Preserve existing Startup::new and StartupScope for source compatibility
   as explicitly lower-level paths. The canonical new scope has direct
   reserve_cleanup and registration access, no unrestricted supervisor accessor.
   Its start result uses InitializationError<E> from its first delivery, so later
   signal support does not change the protected path's public error type.
4. An opt-in Unix signal policy belongs to protected startup. Its configuration
   is inert. Starting synchronously validates/reserves the signal name and
   installs SIGTERM/SIGINT before returning the startup owner; the owned engine
   observes reception during initialization and carries sources into running
   supervision without a fallible application handoff.
5. A synchronous SQLx pool constructor consumes an already validated CleanupSlot
   plus native PgPoolOptions/PgConnectOptions, constructs the native pool and
   registers close before returning. Name it batter_sqlx::pool_in. Connectivity
   checks remain explicit native queries or the existing bounded probe. The async
   alternative was tested but is not selected for this delivery.
6. Real example adoption and a fresh public-guidance consumer task complete the
   delivery. Library tests alone do not establish discovery or modification
   usability. No future adapter, publication or production readiness is implied.
## Common invariants and boundaries

- Native Rust/Tokio remains the execution model; Unix means Linux and macOS.
- Default toolchain 1.98.1; minimum 1.94.0; no Windows branches or CI.
- Foundation never depends on adapters. Generic test support stays a leaf.
- Managed descendant supervision remains in native Runledger.
- Library construction is inert until the explicitly documented start/create call.
- Cancellation travels downward. Finishing work cancels child work before cleanup.
- Readiness requires application approval, running driver and real component ack.
- Signal selection must never manufacture readiness after a drain is observed.
- Preserve first drain cause/timestamp and all returned failures.
- Never log native error or panic contents through automatic diagnostics.
- Retain tracing dispatch during polling and full destruction.
- Registered finalization remains awaited, bounded and LIFO.
- Borrowed waiter cancellation changes no ownership; owner loss requests drain.
- Runtime death, process kill and non-yielding code retain existing limitations.
- Pool close does not certify server-session termination or rollback.
- Types do not stop arbitrary tokio::spawn, leaked handles or remote effects.
- No existing database migrations or durable delivery formats change.
- Preserve application handler absence and intentionally unapproved readiness.
## Verification and evidence rules copied into each Bead

Read root AGENTS.md, agent-map and nearest package guide; preserve existing dirty
changes and append-only .agent state. New code uses generic scenario names.
Use task-local ExecPlans during complex implementation, tied to owning Bead.
Do not create review/planning/Beads-conversion work items.

Run bash scripts/verify.sh and RUSTUP_TOOLCHAIN=1.94.0 bash scripts/verify.sh for
production code/dependency changes. Build the HTTP example and run the five
documented smoke profiles on each exact toolchain. Obtain a final fresh api:test
receipt with scripts/jig work check, verify profile or scripts/jig check test;
inspect evidence/gates before redundant execution. Keep rustdoc/doctests and
failure assertions, and record actual environment/toolchain prerequisites.

Execute affected live SQLx/reference tests against authorized disposable endpoints;
missing prerequisites are incomplete evidence, not silent success. Preserve exact
live inventory and native lock/pins. Keep Cargo.lock generated by Cargo only.
When adding executable source roots, fixtures or scripts, update exhaustive
.jig.toml and .agent/jig-contract.json together. Required fmt/contract/file-budget
checks remain profile siblings, not dependencies of Rust execution.

Update the contract, owning implemented-status row, Bead and validation evidence
for the delivered change. Record upstream semantics against exact resolved source
and primary references. Linux tests are not macOS or hosted CI evidence.
No commits, pushes, publication, deployment, destructive unrelated cleanup or
upstream dependency changes are authorized by completing these tasks.

## Historical experiment evidence

Read docs/evidence/agent-startup-apis-2026-09-12/README.md for source-bound
prototype results, first-attempt failures, public consumer trials and limitations.
The archive is evidence, not production implementation or a required dependency.
Three fresh consumer agents each attempted an initial and modification task;
one made a within-agent pool A/C comparison. No reliability rate is established.
Signal name reservation, the final error envelope and combined protected production
composition remain proposed acceptance. Linux/Rust 1.98.1 experiments do not
replace this task's required production verification or macOS evidence.

Real HTTP and native Runledger local initialization/settlement pass; intended negative authority fixtures reject; returned errors, destruction panic, dispatch and complete cleanup remain preserved. Public docs, both-toolchain verification and final Jig evidence pass.
notes: Implemented Startup::scoped with private-field ProtectedStartupScope and sealed Registration/RegistrationTarget; added shared-driver InitializationError mapping before future destruction; preserved legacy Startup and exact Axum/Runledger signatures while adding register_http_in/register_in. Added protected ownership/failure/rejection/authority controls and real channel, Axum, and prepared Runledger runtime coverage. Linux Rust 1.98.1 and 1.94.0 full verify passed; ten HTTP smokes passed; Jig verify gate passed with api:test receipt receipt_01M2B08EHZ6KBX47RCEJR54KCY. Live PostgreSQL, macOS, and hosted CI were not required/executed.
