title: Own Unix signals from startup start through supervised drain
description:
# Delivery B

Status: planned, not implemented. Own code, tests, docs and evidence together.

## Owning delivery graph

Epic batter-lp2 owns this outcome. A=batter-lp2.1, B=batter-lp2.2, C=batter-lp2.3, D=batter-lp2.4.
Blocking edges: B depends on A; D depends on A/B/C. A and C are independently
ready. Parent-child grouping and related coordination are not blocking edges.
Facade relocation batter-tmx, broad adoption batter-7r3.6, fixture pool profiles
batter-7r3.8 and closed documentation convergence batter-fbd are related only.
Resolve current source paths at implementation; preserve one foundation type
identity and do not close or broaden unrelated Beads.

## B: Own Unix signal reception from startup start through drain

Outcome: a protected service initializer contains application acquisition and
registration only. Selecting an explicit Unix signal policy supplies reception,
drain propagation and running transfer through the library owner.

Depends on A's protected startup scope/entrypoint, not SQLx. Entry points:
crates/batter/src/startup.rs, startup/driver.rs and lifecycle/unix.rs;
foundation Unix subprocess tests and private test-support/process machinery.
Preserve and rerun A's typed owner/observer consumer with and without the policy;
no B change may alter the protected error envelope fixed in A.

Offer opt-in .with_unix_signals(name) -> Self; record configuration inertly and
validate it at start before OS installation or application factory invocation.
Repeated policy selection is a retained configuration failure, not last-wins.
Do not make a fallible consuming builder drop the supervisor's already-registered
finalizers on invalid configuration. Start returns the owned waiter even for
configuration/installation failure, and that owner awaits prior cleanup.
Keep construction/drop-before-start inert. Do not allow a later initializer to
steal the reserved name. Pre-cancelled, expired or already-draining startup skips
OS installation and follows the existing interrupted cleanup path.
An already-recorded configuration failure, including repeated builder selection,
has precedence over subsequently observed initial interruption. Otherwise check
initial interruption before name validation and installation. Both paths skip
the initializer and retain capture-destruction panic separately. Test repeated
selection followed by pre-cancellation explicitly; it must retain the policy error.
At start, synchronously install both native listeners before returning an owner.
Carry installation failure into the separately driven startup failure/cleanup path;
do not return early and drop a Supervisor with pre-registered finalizers.
Retain native partial-installation error even though Tokio may have changed one
process disposition already. Do not promise rollback/restoration of OS handling.
The synchronous start call requires a live signal-enabled Tokio runtime, as the
existing owned start already requires runtime spawning. Document native runtime
precondition panics separately from recoverable listener IO failures; no cleanup
or panic-conversion guarantee is added outside that precondition.
Once synchronous preflight observes an error, store it as an already-completed
initialization result for the coordinator, not only inside a skippable callback.
Later owner loss/cancellation/deadline must not erase that concrete error. Destroy
unused initializer captures under existing dispatch/unwind protection and retain
any destruction panic separately. Pre-callback failures use stage `startup`.

Observe reception concurrently with initializer polling and preserve cancellation
through the callback's destruction and final startup check. Transfer the same
owned signal sources/state to real supervised reception with an infallible internal
completion of the reserved name. No detached application relay task or second
application-owned listener is required. A consumed reception must not require
another OS signal after handoff.

Preserve current real signal-component accounting and signal-only Supervisor
behavior; changing EmptySupervisor policy is outside this work. The signal task
is real supervision, not a dummy warmup used to make a finite command look like
a service. Signals are observed cooperatively: a pending OS notification may be
processed after the initializer is entered. Assert no readiness AFTER observed
drain, not an atomic fence at kernel signal arrival.

Signal policy does not imply automatic readiness, process runtime creation,
default global tracing, force-kill-on-second-signal, or shortened cleanup budgets.
Application readiness withholding remains independent. Existing explicit signal
helpers remain documented lower-level compatibility APIs.

Acceptance scenarios, each in a parent-bounded subprocess for real OS behavior:
1. No signals installed and no callback invoked by an unstarted specification.
2. SIGTERM and SIGINT immediately after start returns but before coordinator polling
   request cleanup instead of default process termination.
3. Each signal during a held post-acquisition initializer produces no Ready state,
   one awaited finalizer and an inspectable drain/failure report.
4. A borrowed startup waiter times out while owner survives; later signal still
   drains and the same final cleanup outcome is observable.
5. Owner loss during startup finalizes acquired dependencies on the live runtime.
6. A controlled final-poll/handoff reception survives transfer without a second signal.
   Use acknowledged phase gates; timer proximity is insufficient evidence.
7. A running native component receives normal drain and joins before cleanup.
8. Invalid, repeated or occupied signal name runs no initializer or rejected side effect.
9. An initializer attempting the reserved name is rejected before that factory runs;
   prior resources still close and the original registration error is retained.
10. Controlled install failure and partial install preserve original IO plus cleanup
    errors without automatically rendering them. Signal failure needs no E conversion.
11. Same-poll application failure/signal or destructor failure does not lose an
    already-observed concrete cause; document existing selection precedence.
12. Repeated signals during cleanup do not reset deadlines or report false completion.
13. A deliberate asynchronous-install-only subject fails case 2; deliberate late
    reservation fails the duplicate test; preserve those controls as evidence.
14. Unix Linux execution and actual macOS execution are labeled separately.
15. In fresh subprocesses, an unstarted configured specification and a started
    unconfigured protected specification retain default TERM/INT termination;
    assert the Unix exit signal. These are intentional opt-out controls.
16. Observe an injected preflight IO error synchronously, then drop the owner
    before coordinator polling: retain IO, zero callback calls, one cleanup and
    the observer report. Repeat with a panicking unused callback capture and
    retain both causes. Pre-cancelled startup must never call the installer.
## B: Concrete implementation and acceptance appendix

### Source ownership and state

Place inert policy storage and its public builder with the protected startup
specification. The selected result type from A remains unchanged. Installation
must occur in the synchronous start path before returning `StartingSupervisor`,
while owned cleanup/report publication continues in the existing coordinator.

Use `crates/batter/src/lifecycle/unix.rs` for native listener creation and
reception behavior. Current `InstalledSignals` already retains `received: bool`
and requests drain during successful registration; preserve that semantic.
Its current `check_component_name` call is not a reservation. Add internal name
reservation that participates in both ordinary and managed collision checks in
`lifecycle.rs`, and consume it exactly once to install the actual signal task.
Do not increment readiness accounting for a placeholder with no real task.
Installation failure must drop owned listeners without claiming to restore
Tokio's process disposition. Keep old public helpers' signatures intact.

The reserved name is a component name, not a cleanup-slot name. Current
`Supervisor` deliberately uses separate component and finalizer namespaces; do
not accidentally make a cleanup slot with the same label a new collision.

### Parent-bounded process fixtures

Use repository-private `test-support/process/` mechanics through a
foundation-owned wrapper. Add suite-specific scenario dispatch, phase markers
and failure assertions with the foundation tests, not to generic process helpers
or `batter-test-support`. Include new source roots in both Jig input contracts.
Bound child startup, semantic checkpoints, and parent termination/reaping;
retain child output and reports before timeout reconciliation can fail.

The key fixture sequences are:

1. **Start-return interval:** child builds a signal-enabled current-thread
   runtime and pre-registers cleanup. Inside runtime entry, call configured
   start, print/flush `start-returned`, then block on a parent gate without
   yielding the runtime. Parent sends TERM or INT and releases the gate. Child
   resumes runtime polling and awaits the observer/owner outcome. Assert native
   signal did not terminate the child, no Ready after observed drain, and prior
   cleanup ran once. A deliberately asynchronous-install subject follows the
   identical phase sequence and must die by the sent signal. This exercises the
   uncovered interval directly without scheduler-delay assumptions.
2. **Held initializer:** callback reserves/registers a resource, publishes
   `resource-registered`, and waits pending. Parent sends one signal after that
   acknowledgement. Require concrete draining startup report, zero component
   readiness, one awaited resource release and no extra signal. In a separate
   variant, cancel only a borrowed waiter before signaling, then observe the
   same owner/report normally.
3. **Owner loss:** after `resource-registered`, drop the sole owner while retaining
   only its observer. Require cleanup/report completion on the live runtime.
   This must not depend on another running owner or retained startup handle.
4. **Handoff:** gate final initializer completion and listener reception
   separately. Assert a consumed reception remains represented in retained
   state and cannot be lost when sources move to running supervision. For exact
   final-poll precedence, a private controllable signal-source seam is acceptable
   beside real OS subprocess tests; distinguish deterministic state-transfer
   evidence from cooperative OS notification timing. An unacknowledged sleep
   near callback completion is not proof of this boundary.
5. **Running component:** permit successful startup, send one actual request to
   a registered channel/native component, then send one OS signal. Require
   component drain/exit before finalizer events and a complete shutdown report.
   Include an intentionally unapproved readiness variant; signal selection must
   not approve it. Preserve a signals-only supervisor test because the listener
   itself is a real critical component under current semantics.
6. **Reservation:** choose a signal name, then inside initialization attempt
   ordinary and managed registration under that name. Independent factory
   counters remain zero, rejected captures drop, the original registration
   error is retained under `Application`, and prior cleanup completes. Include
   invalid/previously occupied name and repeated builder-selection variants
   whose initializer invocation counter remains zero. Assert the intended error
   category, not any generic failure. A deliberately late reservation subject
   must show the collision can occur after the initializer steals the name.
7. **Installation failure:** a private installer seam returns an owned IO marker
   before any listener, and another installs the first native source then fails
   the second. Verify original IO through trusted inspection, cleanup failures
   alongside it, zero callback invocation, and redacted default formatting.
   Retain native disposition caveats. Add R2-1's owner-loss/capture-panic variant.
8. **Selection precedence:** preserve existing biased ordering for already-ready
   drain/cancellation/deadline versus an unpolled callback; do not claim an
   application error that the callback never returned was observed. Conversely,
   a callback whose final poll requests drain and returns a concrete Err must
   retain that observed Err through destruction/final checks. Add a successful
   callback that requests drain in final poll/destruction to prove no readiness
   after that observed request. Keep the selected signal-branch precedence
   explicitly documented and deterministically tested.
9. **Cleanup interval:** finalizer enters and acknowledges a held cleanup stage;
   parent sends repeated signals, then releases it under a fixed budget. Assert
   one invocation, unchanged original drain time/deadlines and the actual final
   complete report. A timeout case must remain incomplete regardless of signal
   count. Do not infer completion from resource-drop events alone.

All process results are Linux evidence unless actually run on macOS. Parent
watchdogs and process-control utilities must retain the Unix-only policy.

## Public error-envelope prerequisite

Signal errors: preserve old public error enums and exhaustive matches. Protected
startup uses a new redacted, non-exhaustive InitializationError<E> envelope with
Application(E), Signals(SignalRegistrationError), and SignalPolicyAlreadySelected,
inside existing StartupError/StartupFailure. Freeze this shape in A, even without
signal configuration; B must not change the typed start result or observer APIs.
Repeated selection is its own category, not a misleading duplicate task name.
The original application and IO causes remain inspectable without application
From conversions. A received signal uses existing Draining classification.
Changing existing StartupCause with a new variant is not source-compatible.

## Selected architecture

1. A concrete borrowed Registration capability contains private access to the
   existing Supervisor registration operations. It offers component registration,
   managed-adapter registration and finalizer reservation, never start,
   run_until, cleanup extraction, replacement or a conversion to Supervisor.
2. A small sealed RegistrationTarget trait exposes only a reborrowed Registration.
   New adapter entrypoints register_http_in and register_in accept it, so protected
   scopes pass directly. Preserve the original adapter signatures; changing them
   to generics breaks existing DerefMut coercion callers. Both names share the
   same registration implementation. Applications need not implement the trait.
3. Introduce additive Startup::scoped and ProtectedStartupScope over the existing
   engine. Preserve existing Startup::new and StartupScope for source compatibility
   as explicitly lower-level paths. The canonical new scope has direct
   reserve_cleanup and registration access, no unrestricted supervisor accessor.
   Its start result uses InitializationError<E> from its first delivery, so later
   signal support does not change the protected path's public error type.
4. An opt-in Unix signal policy belongs to protected startup. Its configuration
   is inert. Starting synchronously validates/reserves the signal name and
   installs SIGTERM/SIGINT before returning the startup owner; the owned engine
   observes reception during initialization and carries sources into running
   supervision without a fallible application handoff.
5. A synchronous SQLx pool constructor consumes an already validated CleanupSlot
   plus native PgPoolOptions/PgConnectOptions, constructs the native pool and
   registers close before returning. Name it batter_sqlx::pool_in. Connectivity
   checks remain explicit native queries or the existing bounded probe. The async
   alternative was tested but is not selected for this delivery.
6. Real example adoption and a fresh public-guidance consumer task complete the
   delivery. Library tests alone do not establish discovery or modification
   usability. No future adapter, publication or production readiness is implied.
## Common invariants and boundaries

- Native Rust/Tokio remains the execution model; Unix means Linux and macOS.
- Default toolchain 1.98.1; minimum 1.94.0; no Windows branches or CI.
- Foundation never depends on adapters. Generic test support stays a leaf.
- Managed descendant supervision remains in native Runledger.
- Library construction is inert until the explicitly documented start/create call.
- Cancellation travels downward. Finishing work cancels child work before cleanup.
- Readiness requires application approval, running driver and real component ack.
- Signal selection must never manufacture readiness after a drain is observed.
- Preserve first drain cause/timestamp and all returned failures.
- Never log native error or panic contents through automatic diagnostics.
- Retain tracing dispatch during polling and full destruction.
- Registered finalization remains awaited, bounded and LIFO.
- Borrowed waiter cancellation changes no ownership; owner loss requests drain.
- Runtime death, process kill and non-yielding code retain existing limitations.
- Pool close does not certify server-session termination or rollback.
- Types do not stop arbitrary tokio::spawn, leaked handles or remote effects.
- No existing database migrations or durable delivery formats change.
- Preserve application handler absence and intentionally unapproved readiness.
## Verification and evidence rules copied into each Bead

Read root AGENTS.md, agent-map and nearest package guide; preserve existing dirty
changes and append-only .agent state. New code uses generic scenario names.
Use task-local ExecPlans during complex implementation, tied to owning Bead.
Do not create review/planning/Beads-conversion work items.

Run bash scripts/verify.sh and RUSTUP_TOOLCHAIN=1.94.0 bash scripts/verify.sh for
production code/dependency changes. Build the HTTP example and run the five
documented smoke profiles on each exact toolchain. Obtain a final fresh api:test
receipt with scripts/jig work check, verify profile or scripts/jig check test;
inspect evidence/gates before redundant execution. Keep rustdoc/doctests and
failure assertions, and record actual environment/toolchain prerequisites.

Execute affected live SQLx/reference tests against authorized disposable endpoints;
missing prerequisites are incomplete evidence, not silent success. Preserve exact
live inventory and native lock/pins. Keep Cargo.lock generated by Cargo only.
When adding executable source roots, fixtures or scripts, update exhaustive
.jig.toml and .agent/jig-contract.json together. Required fmt/contract/file-budget
checks remain profile siblings, not dependencies of Rust execution.

Update the contract, owning implemented-status row, Bead and validation evidence
for the delivered change. Record upstream semantics against exact resolved source
and primary references. Linux tests are not macOS or hosted CI evidence.
No commits, pushes, publication, deployment, destructive unrelated cleanup or
upstream dependency changes are authorized by completing these tasks.

## Historical experiment evidence

Read docs/evidence/agent-startup-apis-2026-09-12/README.md for source-bound
prototype results, first-attempt failures, public consumer trials and limitations.
The archive is evidence, not production implementation or a required dependency.
Three fresh consumer agents each attempted an initial and modification task;
one made a within-agent pool A/C comparison. No reliability rate is established.
Signal name reservation, the final error envelope and combined protected production
composition remain proposed acceptance. Linux/Rust 1.98.1 experiments do not
replace this task's required production verification or macOS evidence.

title: Bind native SQLx pool creation to a reserved cleanup slot
description:
# Delivery C

Status: planned, not implemented. Own code, tests, docs and evidence together.

## Owning delivery graph

Epic batter-lp2 owns this outcome. A=batter-lp2.1, B=batter-lp2.2, C=batter-lp2.3, D=batter-lp2.4.
Blocking edges: B depends on A; D depends on A/B/C. A and C are independently
ready. Parent-child grouping and related coordination are not blocking edges.
Facade relocation batter-tmx, broad adoption batter-7r3.6, fixture pool profiles
batter-7r3.8 and closed documentation convergence batter-fbd are related only.
Resolve current source paths at implementation; preserve one foundation type
identity and do not close or broaden unrelated Beads.

## C: Publish native pool cleanup ownership before initialization can fail

Outcome: creating a native PostgreSQL pool through the supported adapter requires
a validated cleanup slot and registers awaited closure before returning the pool.
It works under both Command and existing service startup without manual close
recovery after failed registration.

No prerequisites: existing CleanupSlot is sufficient. Entry points:
crates/batter-sqlx/src/lib.rs, adapter tests and README; native SQLx remains 0.9.
Keep fixture provisioning and test-support pool profiles outside this default API.
Protected-scope composition is verified in D after A, not a hidden prerequisite
of this independent task. This constructor needs only the existing CleanupSlot.

Add a synchronous slot-consuming function accepting native PgPoolOptions and
PgConnectOptions, returning native PgPool. The owning scope rejects invalid or
duplicate names before this function is called. Inside, construct the native pool,
clone only for closure ownership, synchronously register close and return the pool.
No await, URL parser, ambient configuration reading or fallible post-construction
registration step belongs between pool creation and cleanup publication.
The slot's infallible registration is the ownership primitive; do not expose its
underlying stack or require generic cleanup-target traits.
The exact public spelling is
`batter_sqlx::pool_in(CleanupSlot<'_>, PgPoolOptions, PgConnectOptions) -> PgPool`.
Preserve native runtime/options preconditions and constructor panic behavior.
Successful native construction is followed by synchronous registration; no
rollback guarantee is added when construction itself fails before returning.
Inside owned initialization, prior dependencies retain existing panic cleanup.

Clearly name/document lazy semantics: no connection/authentication/query/schema
readiness is asserted by return. SQLx maintenance may start immediately. Options
and callbacks keep native semantics; no hidden min_connections mutation or retry.
Use existing bounded probe or application-specific first acquisition before
dependent startup. Pools may be cloned; checkouts still require release/join.
Existing register_pool_close remains an explicit lower-level escape for externally
owned pools, with its original rejection obligations and source compatibility.

Acceptance scenarios:
1. Successful actual PostgreSQL query under Command and startup followed by awaited
   close; independently held clones and successful complete cleanup reports
   establish completion. is_closed alone is insufficient: SQLx marks closure
   before waiting for checked-out connections, and the prototype timed out with
   is_closed already true.
2. Duplicate/invalid cleanup name fails before connection/maintenance side effects.
3. Native construction callbacks/options remain preserved, including min_connections
   background behavior; no inertness claim is inferred from synchronous return.
4. First connection authentication error is retained alongside cleanup evidence.
5. Cancellation during acknowledged native acquisition retains the registered pool
   even when no successful connection/pool use was delivered.
6. Later fallible application initialization and its callback panic still close
   each registered pool. Do not imply that the owning report catches arbitrary
   panics in native SQLx maintenance callbacks running on other tasks.
7. Two pools plus a non-pool finalizer establish actual reverse dependency order.
8. Held checkout makes close pending until release or yields documented incomplete
   cleanup within the budget; no false clean report or server-session claim.
9. Failed work and failed/timed-out cleanup coexist in the complete owning report.
10. Native options chosen by the reference settings boundary reach SQLx unchanged.
11. Existing PgLease/probe/disposition, fixture and configuration contracts pass.
12. Adapter/default graph does not gain provisioning, harness or settings dependencies.

Real database tests need disposable external PostgreSQL. A synthetic TCP handshake
is useful cancellation evidence but not a successful SQL/authentication substitute.
Prototype-created clusters are experimental fixtures, not adapter provisioning API.
## C — synchronous pool ownership

### Source anchors and native basis

The implementation belongs beside [`register_pool_close`](/home/aa/Documents/batter/crates/batter-sqlx/src/lib.rs:137).
The existing adapter imports and public error exports begin at `src/lib.rs:26`.
[`CleanupSlot`](/home/aa/Documents/batter/crates/batter/src/cleanup.rs:189) contains the validated name and exclusive stack borrow.
Its consuming [`register`](/home/aa/Documents/batter/crates/batter/src/cleanup.rs:196) returns `()` and performs no name validation.
`CleanupSlot` drop registers nothing; reservation alone does not own an acquired resource.
[`CleanupReport::is_success`](/home/aa/Documents/batter/crates/batter/src/cleanup.rs:130) checks outcomes and skipped hooks.
Its empty-report result is true, so tests must also assert the expected hook identities and count.
[`PgLease::acquire`](/home/aa/Documents/batter/crates/batter-sqlx/src/lib.rs:56) and `probe` at line 110 remain unchanged.
[`SqlxFailure`](/home/aa/Documents/batter/crates/batter-sqlx/src/failure.rs:23) retains the native SQLx error.
The default adapter tests are `crates/batter-sqlx/tests/offline.rs`.
Existing database disposition tests are `crates/batter-sqlx/tests/postgres_live.rs`.
Their explicit runner is `scripts/sqlx_live.py`, invoked by `scripts/test_sqlx_live.sh`.

The inspected SQLx source root is:
`/home/aa/.cargo/registry/src/index.crates.io-1949cf8c6b5b557f/sqlx-core-0.9.0/`.
Within it, `src/pool/options.rs:537`, `connect_with`, performs asynchronous initial acquisition.
`src/pool/options.rs:579`, `connect_lazy_with`, constructs through `PoolInner::new_arc`.
`src/pool/inner.rs`, `new_arc`, invokes `spawn_maintenance_tasks`.
`src/pool/inner.rs:507`, `spawn_maintenance_tasks`, owns native background maintenance.
Read `src/pool/mod.rs`, `Pool::close` and `Pool::is_closed`, before implementing closure assertions.
Record these resolved-source identities in `docs/references.md`; do not substitute unversioned recollection.
Native maintenance may begin during construction, including work for positive `min_connections`.
The promised boundary is synchronous cleanup publication before return, not construction inertness.

### Exact public interface

Add this public function at the adapter crate root:

```rust
pub fn pool_in(
    slot: batter::cleanup::CleanupSlot<'_>,
    pool_options: sqlx::postgres::PgPoolOptions,
    connect_options: sqlx::postgres::PgConnectOptions,
) -> sqlx::PgPool;
```

Its implementation has three ownership steps and one return:

```rust
let pool = pool_options.connect_lazy_with(connect_options);
let closing = pool.clone();
slot.register(move || async move {
    closing.close().await;
    Ok(())
});
pool
```

The function consumes both native option values without rebuilding or overriding them.
It accepts no URL, environment reader, context, supervisor, or separate name.
It returns neither `Result` nor a future because slot validation already occurred.
There must be no additional synchronous application callback invoked by pool_in,
await, or fallible registration between native construction and publication.
Native maintenance callbacks may run concurrently; the constructor does not fence them.
Do not call `register_pool_close` internally; that would reintroduce a rejectable registration path.
Do not detach a closure task; the existing cleanup owner must invoke and await the finalizer.
Preserve the original `register_pool_close(&mut Supervisor, &'static str, &PgPool)` signature.
Its rejected-registration obligations remain documented for externally owned pools.
No public change is required in `CleanupSlot`, `CommandScope`, or legacy `StartupScope`.

Rustdoc must identify the Tokio runtime preconditions inherited from native construction.
Do not promise cleanup after native constructor panic, allocation failure, or process/runtime death.
Return establishes cleanup ownership, not connectivity, authentication, query success, or schema readiness.
SQLx callbacks, connection limits, timeouts, lifetimes, and maintenance retain native semantics.
Callers release checked-out connections and join dependent work before expecting successful close.
An independently retained `PgPool` clone may inspect closure; it does not keep the pool open against `close`.
Detached connections and server sessions remain outside pool-close completion guarantees.

### Complete composition requirements

Publish a compiling `Command` composition using `Command::new`, a concrete error type, and `pool_in`.
The callback reserves `postgres.pool` through `CommandScope::reserve_cleanup`.
It calls `pool_in` immediately after obtaining the slot and the native options.
It then performs an explicit native query or the existing bounded probe.
It awaits the command owner and checks the complete command report.
Demonstrate inspection of work failure together with cleanup failure.
Do not add SQLx to the foundation merely to place this example under `crates/batter/examples`.
An adapter doctest or adapter-owned example is an appropriate location.

C also tests existing service startup, without requiring A's protected projection.
Legacy composition may reserve through `scope.supervisor().reserve_cleanup`.
Keep that spelling confined to the compatibility example or test once D lands.
C's success must not depend on `Startup::scoped`, signal policy, or protected adapter registration.
D supplies the final combined protected-service example.

### Original-native-error retention

`pool_in` creates no SQLx error envelope because it performs no awaited acquisition.
A native error returned by the first explicit operation must survive in its owning report.
For adapter operations, retain `OperationError<SqlxFailure>` without converting it to text.
Use `SqlxFailure::native`, `into_native`, or `Error::source` for trusted native inspection.
For direct native queries, preserve `sqlx::Error` inside a concrete application variant.
Existing application wrappers may retain it in `BoxError`; do not replace it with a static surrogate.
Default wrapper `Display` and `Debug` remain fixed or otherwise explicitly redacted.
Trusted error-chain access and native SQLx logging are separate from those formatting guarantees.

A returned PostgreSQL error must retain database metadata, including a suitable SQLSTATE.
Use a real failing query such as division by zero to verify native `22012` retention.
For authentication failure, require a real server authentication rejection and inspect its native category.
Do not count connection refusal, missing configuration, or a synthetic handshake as authentication evidence.
Do not promise retention of every background-maintenance failure that SQLx itself does not return.
Cancellation may prevent delivery of a native error; record interruption without inventing a cause.
Cleanup errors, timeouts, skipped hooks, and destruction panic remain independent report fields.
A recovery close performed later must not erase the original unsuccessful report.

### Test phases and independent oracles

Each ownership scenario separates acquisition, exercise, teardown, and inspection.
The test retains the owner or observation handle before introducing cancellation.
Setup publishes resource identity only after the relevant native event has occurred.
Exercise failures are retained as values so teardown still executes.
Terminal assertions follow awaited owner completion, except deliberately intermediate pending checks.
An outer watchdog bounds setup, exercise, recovery, and child reaping.
A watchdog timeout is failed evidence, not an alternative successful interruption result.

Use channels or barriers for causal ordering rather than sleeps near expected transitions.
Every acknowledgement states what happened: callback entered, query completed, checkout held, or close observed.
A callback-entry acknowledgement does not establish successful database authentication.
A completed `SELECT 1::integer` with result `1` establishes the successful-query requirement.
An independently held clone plus the expected successful cleanup record establishes observed pool finalization.
Also require zero skipped hooks, the expected record count, `size() == 0`, and `PoolClosed` on later acquire.
`is_closed()` alone is insufficient because native close sets that flag before all checkouts return.
Server absence, when needed by an existing fixture contract, requires a separate administrative observer.
That observer must not borrow capacity from the pool under test.

Before testing the implementation, freeze the oracle expectations and phase protocol.
Retain a negative-control subject that drops the pool-close registration.
It must fail expected-record or surviving-clone assertions, even if native pool drop eventually releases resources.
Retain a premature-success subject that treats `is_closed()` as completion.
A real held checkout must cause that subject to fail the completion oracle.
Run negative controls in isolated subjects; never weaken or mutate the canonical acceptance oracle.
Record source identity, intended violation, observed failure, and whether the failure was the intended one.

### C acceptance case specifications

**C1 — finite success:** create inside `Command`, execute a real query, finish work, await complete cleanup.
Retain a clone outside the callback and verify the named pool record and native closed state.
Inspect the complete command report, including late interruption and destruction-panic fields.
**C2 — service success:** create inside legacy owned startup, register a real acknowledged component, then drain.
Verify component termination precedes successful pool cleanup and inspect the shutdown report.
**C3 — invalid reservation:** reject an empty name before calling `pool_in`.
Use a creation counter and controlled endpoint to prove native construction was never entered.
**C4 — duplicate reservation:** fulfill the first reservation, then reject the second before construction.
Require exactly one pool cleanup record and no second creation acknowledgement.
Do not interpret a dropped unused slot as a permanently occupied cleanup name.

**C5 — options and callbacks:** select distinct native limits and callback behavior before construction.
Observe callback effects with native SQL, such as an application-selected session setting.
Prove positive `min_connections` initiates maintenance without an explicit consumer checkout.
Gate and bound that observation; do not assert instantaneous connection counts at synchronous return.
**C6 — authentication failure:** construct successfully, perform a real failed authentication attempt, then finalize.
Retain the original returned SQLx error and the successful pool cleanup record together.
The fixture must use authentication that rejects the chosen credentials; local trust is not sufficient.
**C7 — acquisition cancellation:** acknowledge a pending native handshake or blocked acquisition, then cancel work.
Require interruption, the already-published pool finalizer, and bounded teardown.
Close the controlled handshake socket explicitly; do not infer backend settlement from local cancellation.

**C8 — later application failure:** complete a native query, then return an independent typed failure.
Require that failure and successful pool cleanup in the same retained report.
**C9 — callback panic:** publish the pool, acknowledge acquisition, then unwind with a typed marker.
Inspect the retained panic payload and finalization without claiming suppression of the process panic hook.
**C10 — two pools and a dependent finalizer:** register pool A, pool B, then the dependent hook.
Gate the dependent hook; verify neither earlier hook is reported complete while it remains held.
After release, assert exact record order: dependent hook, pool B, pool A.
Retain both pool clones and prove each close completed.

**C11 — held checkout, eventual completion:** hold a real connection outside the closing callback.
Observe closure initiation and an unfinished owning report while that checkout remains held.
Release it before the cleanup budget expires, then require successful completion.
**C12 — held checkout, budget exhaustion:** keep the checkout held through the configured cleanup allowance.
Require an unsuccessful complete report or explicitly retained incomplete ownership, as the existing engine specifies.
Never require `Unjoined` when a cooperative close future was successfully aborted and joined.
After inspection, release the checkout and explicitly await native close under a recovery bound.
That repair does not revise the earlier timeout into success.
**C13 — combined failure:** return a native query error and arrange a separate failing or timed-out finalizer.
Assert both original failures and the pool outcome; do not reduce acceptance to process exit status.
**C14 — regression boundary:** retain existing lease, probe, fixture, redaction, and configuration tests.
Ensure the default adapter graph gains no settings, provisioning, or harness dependency.
### Existing SQLx and PostgreSQL example inventory

The SQLx runner currently owns these ten exact ignored names:

```text
blocked_cancellation_releases_capacity
blocked_deadline_releases_capacity
blocked_error_releases_capacity
blocked_panic_releases_capacity
blocked_outer_drop_releases_capacity
repeated_interruptions_leave_independent_residual_sessions
success_and_acknowledged_transactions_reuse
native_database_failure_retires_and_preserves_cause
rejected_commit_preserves_native_cause_and_retires
ordinary_return_control_retains_blocked_capacity
```

The PostgreSQL lifecycle binary currently owns these three live cases:

```text
tests::live::success_closes_the_live_pool_before_exit
tests::live::startup_database_error_retains_failed_cleanup_and_closes_the_pool
tests::live::task_database_error_survives_shutdown_and_pool_close
```

Preserve their behavioral obligations when moving acquisition inside protected startup.
If C adds a separate live target, give it an explicit exact inventory and runner selection.
If C extends `postgres_live`, update `scripts/sqlx_live.py::CASES` and its summary expectations together.
Require each expected new case to execute once; compilation and total counts alone are insufficient.
Retain existing negative controls rather than replacing them with successful pool ownership cases.

## Selected architecture

1. A concrete borrowed Registration capability contains private access to the
   existing Supervisor registration operations. It offers component registration,
   managed-adapter registration and finalizer reservation, never start,
   run_until, cleanup extraction, replacement or a conversion to Supervisor.
2. A small sealed RegistrationTarget trait exposes only a reborrowed Registration.
   New adapter entrypoints register_http_in and register_in accept it, so protected
   scopes pass directly. Preserve the original adapter signatures; changing them
   to generics breaks existing DerefMut coercion callers. Both names share the
   same registration implementation. Applications need not implement the trait.
3. Introduce additive Startup::scoped and ProtectedStartupScope over the existing
   engine. Preserve existing Startup::new and StartupScope for source compatibility
   as explicitly lower-level paths. The canonical new scope has direct
   reserve_cleanup and registration access, no unrestricted supervisor accessor.
   Its start result uses InitializationError<E> from its first delivery, so later
   signal support does not change the protected path's public error type.
4. An opt-in Unix signal policy belongs to protected startup. Its configuration
   is inert. Starting synchronously validates/reserves the signal name and
   installs SIGTERM/SIGINT before returning the startup owner; the owned engine
   observes reception during initialization and carries sources into running
   supervision without a fallible application handoff.
5. A synchronous SQLx pool constructor consumes an already validated CleanupSlot
   plus native PgPoolOptions/PgConnectOptions, constructs the native pool and
   registers close before returning. Name it batter_sqlx::pool_in. Connectivity
   checks remain explicit native queries or the existing bounded probe. The async
   alternative was tested but is not selected for this delivery.
6. Real example adoption and a fresh public-guidance consumer task complete the
   delivery. Library tests alone do not establish discovery or modification
   usability. No future adapter, publication or production readiness is implied.
## Common invariants and boundaries

- Native Rust/Tokio remains the execution model; Unix means Linux and macOS.
- Default toolchain 1.98.1; minimum 1.94.0; no Windows branches or CI.
- Foundation never depends on adapters. Generic test support stays a leaf.

- Registered finalization remains awaited, bounded and LIFO.

- Runtime death, process kill and non-yielding code retain existing limitations.
- Pool close does not certify server-session termination or rollback.
- Types do not stop arbitrary tokio::spawn, leaked handles or remote effects.
- No existing database migrations or durable delivery formats change.
- Preserve application handler absence and intentionally unapproved readiness.

## Historical experiment evidence

title: Adopt protected startup and pool ownership in canonical consumers
description:
# Delivery D

Status: planned, not implemented. Own code, tests, docs and evidence together.

## Owning delivery graph

Epic batter-lp2 owns this outcome. A=batter-lp2.1, B=batter-lp2.2, C=batter-lp2.3, D=batter-lp2.4.
Blocking edges: B depends on A; D depends on A/B/C. A and C are independently
ready. Parent-child grouping and related coordination are not blocking edges.
Facade relocation batter-tmx, broad adoption batter-7r3.6, fixture pool profiles
batter-7r3.8 and closed documentation convergence batter-fbd are related only.
Resolve current source paths at implementation; preserve one foundation type
identity and do not close or broaden unrelated Beads.

## D: Adopt the protected path in runnable consumers

Outcome: the reference root, HTTP example, PostgreSQL lifecycle example and finite
pool consumer use the new APIs; public guidance and independently evaluated agent
implementation agree on the canonical ownership path.

Depends on A, B and C. Entry points: examples/reference-service/src/runtime.rs,
examples/postgres-lifecycle/src/main.rs, crates/batter-axum/examples/http_service.rs,
related package tests; docs/usage, integrations, guarantees, architecture, status,
validation and source references. Preserve current batter-fbd documentation edits.

Replace the reference's manual signal install/select/transfer with builder policy.
Move PostgreSQL demo signal selection before acquisition by library startup policy.
Use slot-consuming native pool creation where code now clones/registers pool close.
Use the protected registration target for Axum and prepared Runledger.
Keep stage metadata, schemas, authentication, settings/PG* validation, native probes,
provider absence and without_readiness_approval semantics application-owned.
Do not remove the deliberate long-running demo component merely to force use of
Command; changing a service demonstration into a finite command changes its purpose.

Update canonical documentation with complete compiling compositions. Show old APIs
only as compatibility/escape paths with precise obligations. Avoid duplicate large
agent guides; contracts live in owning public docs, guide files route to them.
Coordinate paths/imports with facade work if it has landed; do not force that work
to block this delivery or copy historical source files over newer implementations.

Acceptance scenarios:
1. Real reference startup SIGTERM/SIGINT before DB initialization completes follows
   awaited failure cleanup, including stalled initialization and waiter loss.
2. Running HTTP behavior and all five smoke modes preserve prior status/headers,
   readiness/drain, deadlines and sanitized exit diagnostics.
3. Reference keeps readiness unapproved and no production startup witness jobs.
4. Existing live SQLx/reference exact case inventory remains covered, with source
   identities, toolchain and actual platform recorded.
5. New consumer task starts from behavioral requirements/public guidance, no fixed
   ownership signatures, hidden library tests or previous repair transcript.
6. Retain the agent's first source before compiling; record compiler diagnostics,
   repairs, guidance ambiguities and abandoned approaches without inflating success.
7. Independent oracles cover real SIGTERM startup cleanup, native query plus later
   failure, and constrained adapter registration. A subsequent modification adds
   a second dependency and startup stage without rebuilding lifecycle protocols.
8. A separate fresh agent reviews implementability of the standalone delivery task;
   same-agent modification is not another independent sample.
9. Report number of agent tasks and exact conditions, never a general reliability
   percentage. Planning prototypes do not replace final production acceptance.
10. All code/doc/verification requirements below pass before task closure.
## D — actual consumer migration

### Consumer anchors and intended substitutions

[`runtime::run`](/home/aa/Documents/batter/examples/reference-service/src/runtime.rs:90) currently owns manual signal routing.
Its `Startup::new` begins at line 95; manual installation, selection, and transfer occur inside the initializer.
[`register_pool`](/home/aa/Documents/batter/examples/reference-service/src/runtime.rs:147) manually publishes a lazy pool close.
[`register_health`](/home/aa/Documents/batter/examples/reference-service/src/runtime.rs:162) currently requires `&mut Supervisor`.
[`postgres-lifecycle::run`](/home/aa/Documents/batter/examples/postgres-lifecycle/src/main.rs:51) connects before installing signals.
Its [`serve`](/home/aa/Documents/batter/examples/postgres-lifecycle/src/main.rs:92) fixes the initializer's legacy scope type.
[`http_service::run`](/home/aa/Documents/batter/crates/batter-axum/examples/http_service.rs:171) uses the legacy startup projection.
Its dependency helper at line 42 takes `&mut Supervisor`; line 192 obtains a handle through that scope.
[`Session::new`](/home/aa/Documents/batter/examples/reference-service/src/retirement/session.rs:26) is the actual finite pool consumer.
It already runs under `CommandScope` and manually registers a native lazy pool.
Its physical-session replacement guard and fixed one-slot configuration are operational requirements.

### Required A/B interfaces at the D boundary

D consumes `batter::startup::ProtectedStartupScope` through `Startup::scoped`.
The protected start result is `StartingSupervisor<InitializationError<E>>`.
The protected builder supplies `.with_unix_signals(name) -> Self`.
`InitializationError<E>` retains `Application(E)`, `Signals(SignalRegistrationError)`, and repeated-policy failure.
D must use A's delivered non-exhaustive envelope rather than extending existing `StartupCause`.
The scope supplies `stage`, direct `reserve_cleanup`, and `registration`.
It supplies no unrestricted supervisor or newly introduced context accessor.
Adapters expose `batter_axum::register_http_in` and `batter_runledger::register_in`.
They accept the sealed registration target and share implementation with legacy entrypoints.
If an A/B signature differs from this agreed boundary, report to its owning Bead and block D;
do not implement predecessor API repair inside the consumer migration.
Do not compensate by adding scope escape methods or rebuilding signal routing in D.

Use these application-private helper shapes where useful:

```rust
fn register_pool(
    scope: &mut batter::startup::ProtectedStartupScope,
    settings: &RootSettings,
) -> Result<sqlx::PgPool, BoxError>;

fn register_health(
    registration: batter::registration::Registration<'_>,
    pool: sqlx::PgPool,
) -> Result<HealthReader<OperationError<batter_sqlx::SqlxFailure>>, BoxError>;
```

A concrete borrowed registration parameter keeps authority visible without another application trait.
Reborrow successive helpers using the delivered registration method.
Capture readiness handles and native operation contexts at the composition root before moving the supervisor.
Do not manufacture a second parent deadline to work around a scope borrow.

### Migration sequence

1. Confirm A/B/C signatures and their compatibility tests before editing application roots.
2. Migrate the reference pool helper to direct scope reservation plus `batter_sqlx::pool_in`.
3. Preserve `RootSettings::connect_options_from_process` and `pool_options` as the native-option boundary.
4. Replace reference startup with `Startup::scoped(...).with_unix_signals("signals")`.
5. Remove application-owned listener installation, `tokio::select!`, and listener transfer from that initializer.
6. Preserve application stage names for pool acquisition, schema initialization, HTTP bind, and worker registration.
7. Remove or reclassify the old signal-install stage; synchronous policy failures precede application stages.
8. Register health through `Registration`, HTTP through `register_http_in`, and prepared Runledger through `register_in`.
9. Preserve the empty production registry and `.without_readiness_approval()`.
10. Keep schema initialization, authenticated routes, settings validation, and native health sampling unchanged.

11. Migrate the PostgreSQL lifecycle `serve` callback bound to `ProtectedStartupScope`.
12. Select Unix policy on its startup builder before the synchronous `start` boundary.
13. Parse its application-owned `DATABASE_URL` into native `PgConnectOptions` outside `pool_in`.
14. Keep parsing errors before pool construction; do not create a new settings framework for this demo.
15. Replace eager pool construction and manual finalization with reservation and `pool_in`.
16. Retain the explicit bounded probe before registering dependent application work.
17. Document the changed acquisition timing: return from construction is now lazy; the explicit probe establishes connectivity.
18. Preserve the deliberate long-running `application` component and its real startup acknowledgement.
19. Remove only obsolete example-local signal helper calls; retain compatibility helpers still used elsewhere.
20. Migrate actual live-test setup into the new initializer rather than precreating pools outside ownership.

21. Migrate HTTP startup and capture its shutdown/readiness handle before moving the supervisor.
22. Convert its health helper to registration authority and use `register_http_in` for listener ownership.
23. Select the same Unix policy on the builder; preserve router, middleware, configuration, and exit rendering.
24. Migrate retirement `Session::new` by passing its completed `PgPoolOptions` and native options to `pool_in`.
25. Preserve one connection, zero minimum, disabled idle/max lifetime, acquire timeout, and `search_path`.
26. Preserve the entire `after_connect` replacement guard, its atomics, and its fixed diagnostic.
27. Do not change retirement verification, transaction boundaries, cancellation, or separate readback ownership.
28. Run the physical replacement regression through the reference runner after this finite-consumer change.

### Application error and compatibility handling

Reference [`RuntimeStartupFailure::startup`](/home/aa/Documents/batter/examples/reference-service/src/runtime.rs:65) publicly returns the legacy typed error.
Silently changing that return type would violate the staged public-contract policy.
Preserve that type and accessor for legacy clients.
Add the distinct ProtectedRuntimeStartupFailure wrapper for the canonical root's
expanded error envelope. D preserves old type/accessor source compatibility, not
runtime::run's old boxed-error downcast behavior. The intended interface is:

```rust
pub struct ProtectedRuntimeStartupFailure(/* private retained error */);

impl ProtectedRuntimeStartupFailure {
    pub fn startup(
        &self,
    ) -> &batter::startup::StartupError<
        batter::startup::InitializationError<InitializationFailure>
    >;
}
```

Implement fixed `Display` and `Debug`, with `Error::source` retaining the actual protected startup error.
Document that `run` still returns `Result<(), BoxError>` but deliberately changes
its startup-error downcast target to ProtectedRuntimeStartupFailure. This is an
explicit reference-root behavioral cutover, not a claim of unchanged downcasts.
Migrate examples/reference-service/tests/support/startup_process.rs accordingly.
Search downstream examples and tests for old downcasts and migrate those intended to follow the protected root.
Retain a compiled fixture for the original public wrapper accessor.
Do not fabricate an application error for a signal-installation failure to preserve an old downcast.
Protected application failures unwrap through `StartupCause::Failed(InitializationError::Application(...))`.
Retain native SQLx errors, native listener IO errors, cleanup outcomes, and destruction panic independently.
Update PostgreSQL example test helpers that downcast the formerly legacy startup error.
[`check_shutdown`](/home/aa/Documents/batter/examples/reference-service/src/runtime.rs:143) is a report checker, not a report-producing accessor.
Tests needing detailed shutdown assertions retain the actual outcome/report before applying that checker.

## Live inventory and environment ownership

### Existing SQLx and PostgreSQL example inventory

The SQLx runner currently owns these ten exact ignored names:

```text
blocked_cancellation_releases_capacity
blocked_deadline_releases_capacity
blocked_error_releases_capacity
blocked_panic_releases_capacity
blocked_outer_drop_releases_capacity
repeated_interruptions_leave_independent_residual_sessions

native_database_failure_retires_and_preserves_cause
rejected_commit_preserves_native_cause_and_retires
ordinary_return_control_retains_blocked_capacity
```

The PostgreSQL lifecycle binary currently owns these three live cases:

```text
tests::live::success_closes_the_live_pool_before_exit
tests::live::startup_database_error_retains_failed_cleanup_and_closes_the_pool
tests::live::task_database_error_survives_shutdown_and_pool_close
```

Preserve their behavioral obligations when moving acquisition inside protected startup.
If C adds a separate live target, give it an explicit exact inventory and runner selection.
If C extends `postgres_live`, update `scripts/sqlx_live.py::CASES` and its summary expectations together.
Require each expected new case to execute once; compilation and total counts alone are insufficient.
Retain existing negative controls rather than replacing them with successful pool ownership cases.

### Existing reference inventory

`scripts/reference_live.py::CASES` currently contains these 58 entries:

```text
production_root_withholds_readiness_without_control_jobs
retirement_preserves_history_and_disables_old_catalog
retirement_rejects_wrong_identity
retirement_rejects_hidden_sessions
retirement_observes_late_enqueue
retirement_rejects_prepared_enqueue
retirement_retains_commit_error_through_readback_cancellation
retirement_retains_lost_commit_acknowledgement
child_fixture

native_initialization_without_queue_writes
native_in_flight_finishes_after_drain
native_owner_drop_retains_settlement

native_unjoined_callback_blocks_dependency_cleanup
startup_signal_during_schema_initialization
configured_command_root_bounds
configured_pool_capacity_and_acquire_timeout
configured_startup_pool_close_before_lease
configured_worker_concurrency
fixture_abandoned_producer_failure_retained
fixture_assertion_and_script_failures_retained

fixture_close_order_and_resumable_wait

fixture_distinct_deferred_and_consuming_failures

initialized_schema_upgrade

```

The runner classifies these as 56 live probes and two offline signal entries.
It additionally executes `retirement::session::tests::maintenance_session_replacement_is_refused` in the library target.
Preserve that separate target, exact selection, and one-success assertion.
New protected-startup scenarios must update inventory, execution parsing, runner controls, and documented counts together.
Do not count child dispatch entries or compilation as additional independent database experiments.

### Fixture authority and ownership

SQLx and PostgreSQL example live tests use an explicitly supplied disposable `DATABASE_URL`.
The reference runner requires distinct `POSTGRES_TEST_ADMIN_URL` and `POSTGRES_TEST_OBSERVER_URL` clusters.
Its primary PostgreSQL 18 server needs superuser authority and SCRAM host authentication.
It also needs `max_prepared_transactions > 0`, `track_counts`, and autovacuum with naptime at most five seconds.
Both selected administrative endpoints must permit the native cluster-identity preflight.
The observer endpoint must identify a different cluster; aliases of the primary do not qualify.
Keep unrelated workloads and connection producers off the dedicated serial primary.
Application tests do not provision clusters or weaken authentication to make cases pass.

Rust preflight and shared endpoint validation own credentials, native options, and endpoint policy.
Python owns inventory, process scheduling, capture bounds, and watchdogs.
Preserve rejection of ambient PG* state and passfile fallback at the reference boundary.
Use cleared child environments for option-policy tests; never mutate process-global environment in parallel Rust tests.
Keep IPv4, IPv6 loopback, Unix signals, and subprocess prerequisites explicit.
Missing prerequisites fail selected live execution; they are not ignored-test success.
Observer and diagnostic pools remain separately owned from closing application capacity.
Release raw paused SCRAM sockets before awaiting the existing DROP-barrier completion.
Retain existing fixture pending owners and explicit retry paths until resources actually settle.

## D integration and public-consumer acceptance

### Actual-root failure protocols

Exercise both SIGTERM and SIGINT against the migrated executable or the same production root entrypoint.
Gate startup during acknowledged native acquisition and separately during acknowledged schema work.
Emit only static phase identifiers; do not print URLs, credentials, SQL errors, or arbitrary panic payloads.
Send the signal only after the parent receives the phase acknowledgement.
Require observed drain, no subsequent Ready transition, and awaited failure cleanup.
A blocked schema query needs an independently observed lock relationship, not elapsed waiting alone.
Keep the root owner alive while abandoning a borrowed waiter, then signal and inspect its eventual outcome.
Use a separate owner-loss case; waiter cancellation and owner destruction are different contracts.
Retain B's subprocess test for the interval after `start` returns and before coordinator polling.
D must additionally prove combined real-root signal handling and registered pool ownership.
Production `/live` remains available when appropriate; `/ready` remains 503 while approval is withheld.
Verify the native production registry creates no startup witness jobs and cannot claim the absent handler.
Inspect sanitized nonzero startup exits separately from successful running shutdown exits.

### Public agent implementation and modification protocol

Freeze a public task packet before assigning a fresh consumer implementation.
Supply behavioral requirements, public crate documentation, manifests, and authorized fixture access.
Do not prescribe ownership function names, copy internal tests, or include prototype repair transcripts.
Ask for a service that queries PostgreSQL, registers native HTTP work, and closes dependencies on startup signal or failure.
Require concrete inspectable application failures and fixed process diagnostics.
State observable readiness, shutdown, deadline, and dependency-order requirements.
Let the agent discover the canonical path from the public guidance being evaluated.

Retain the first complete submitted source before compiling or giving diagnostic feedback.
Record its content hash, public-guide revision, dependencies, toolchain, and task wording.
Capture every compilation attempt, diagnostic, repair, abandoned approach, and requested clarification.
Classify errors as discovery, type/lifetime, implementation, library gap, or application-protocol complexity.
Do not silently repair the submission before recording its initial result.
An evaluator owns independent runtime oracles and executes them against the retained submission.
Those oracles include real startup SIGTERM, successful native query followed by failure, and constrained adapter registration.
Compile-fail authority checks need a compiling positive baseline and the intended rejection diagnostic.
Runnable HTTP and cleanup assertions remain required even when authority checks pass.

After the initial task, give the same agent a modification request adding a second dependency and startup stage.
Include a failure after the second dependency has been used successfully.
Require reverse dependency teardown and preserved original errors without new application signal-routing machinery.
Retain the modification's first source and all subsequent diagnostics separately.
The modification is a within-agent observation, not another independent sample.
A separate fresh agent reviews whether the standalone delivery task is implementable from its public packet.
Record that review independently from implementation and runtime acceptance.
Report exact task counts and conditions; do not derive a general reliability percentage.
Prototype results from the input are historical experiments, not production acceptance for these changes.
If a repaired example repeats an invariant failure or breaks a coupled lifecycle phase, apply ADR-010's assessment procedure.
Report the design concern before dependent repairs; do not expand the selected architecture without its authorization boundary.

## Documentation, verification, recovery, and completion

### Documentation and compatibility checks

Update adapter rustdoc and README, `docs/usage.md`, integrations, guarantees, architecture, testing, and references.
Update relevant implemented-status rows only when their implementation and evidence exist.
Append exact validation evidence rather than overwriting earlier platform- or revision-specific results.
Update reference compatibility documentation and the affected package guides.
Keep guides as routes to canonical contracts, not duplicate large integration manuals.
Canonical combined service examples in D show pool_in, protected startup, explicit
Unix policy and applicable native adapters. The finite Command example does not
acquire service signals or startup, and the HTTP-only example need not add SQLx.
Label legacy startup, mutable supervisor access, manual signals, and `register_pool_close` as compatibility or escape paths.
Explain native error inspection, complete report inspection, lazy pool behavior, and checked-out connection obligations.
Preserve existing adapter function-pointer and `DerefMut` coercion compatibility fixtures from A.
Check public startup wrapper accessors, downcasts and rustdoc links. Facade-specific checks
are N/A until facade work lands; preserve one foundation type identity in either layout.
Keep existing migrations and lockfile pins unchanged unless a separately justified dependency change is required.

### Required execution evidence

Run `bash scripts/verify.sh` and `RUSTUP_TOOLCHAIN=1.94.0 bash scripts/verify.sh`.
Build `cargo build -p batter-axum --example http_service --locked` on each selected toolchain.
Run `scripts/smoke_http.py` against that toolchain's rebuilt binary in all five documented modes:
default, `--signal SIGINT`, `--deadline`, `--warn-filter`, and `--warn-filter --deadline`.
Execute affected adapter, reference, and PostgreSQL example live inventories with their required external fixtures.
Build the PostgreSQL lifecycle binary and run its default and SIGINT executable smokes.
Include runner-control tests whenever inventory parsing or process protocols change.
Obtain final fresh `api:test` evidence through the required Jig workflow and inspect evidence and gates.
Reuse valid receipts only with unchanged relevant inputs, commands, toolchain, environment, and prerequisites.
Update `.jig.toml` and `.agent/jig-contract.json` together for new executable input roots.
Keep formatting, contract, and file-budget checks as required profile siblings.
Record command, exit result, case inventory, source identity, lockfile, toolchain, platform, and fixture configuration.
Linux evidence does not establish macOS behavior; label unexecuted macOS and hosted runs explicitly.

### Recovery and completion criteria

On test failure, retain the owning report before repairing external resources.
Release acknowledged blockers, held checkouts, and raw sockets through their existing owners.
Await native close and fixture completion under independent recovery bounds.
Do not drop fixture leases or abort dependent supervision merely to obtain a clean exit.
Retain original errors after successful recovery, including recovered observer failures and cleanup timeouts.
For source rollback, revert only task-owned changes; preserve unrelated edits and append-only evidence.
Do not replace newer facade or documentation files with historical copies.

C's completed receipt is a prerequisite; D does not reopen C's delivery checklist.
D completes when all four actual consumers use the selected path and their behavioral contracts remain intact.
D also requires combined signal/pool failures, exact live coverage, public implementation/modification evaluation, and compatibility documentation.
Missing live prerequisites, unresolved native-error loss, false cleanup success, or unexecuted required checks prevent completion.
No commit, push, publication, deployment, unrelated tracker mutation, or upstream architectural change follows from these completion criteria.

## Selected architecture

1. A concrete borrowed Registration capability contains private access to the
   existing Supervisor registration operations. It offers component registration,
   managed-adapter registration and finalizer reservation, never start,
   run_until, cleanup extraction, replacement or a conversion to Supervisor.
2. A small sealed RegistrationTarget trait exposes only a reborrowed Registration.
   New adapter entrypoints register_http_in and register_in accept it, so protected
   scopes pass directly. Preserve the original adapter signatures; changing them
   to generics breaks existing DerefMut coercion callers. Both names share the
   same registration implementation. Applications need not implement the trait.
3. Introduce additive Startup::scoped and ProtectedStartupScope over the existing
   engine. Preserve existing Startup::new and StartupScope for source compatibility
   as explicitly lower-level paths. The canonical new scope has direct
   reserve_cleanup and registration access, no unrestricted supervisor accessor.
   Its start result uses InitializationError<E> from its first delivery, so later
   signal support does not change the protected path's public error type.
4. An opt-in Unix signal policy belongs to protected startup. Its configuration
   is inert. Starting synchronously validates/reserves the signal name and

## Common invariants and boundaries

- Native Rust/Tokio remains the execution model; Unix means Linux and macOS.
- Default toolchain 1.98.1; minimum 1.94.0; no Windows branches or CI.
- Foundation never depends on adapters. Generic test support stays a leaf.
- Managed descendant supervision remains in native Runledger.
- Library construction is inert until the explicitly documented start/create call.
- Cancellation travels downward. Finishing work cancels child work before cleanup.
- Readiness requires application approval, running driver and real component ack.
- Signal selection must never manufacture readiness after a drain is observed.
- Preserve first drain cause/timestamp and all returned failures.
- Never log native error or panic contents through automatic diagnostics.
- Retain tracing dispatch during polling and full destruction.
- Registered finalization remains awaited, bounded and LIFO.
- Borrowed waiter cancellation changes no ownership; owner loss requests drain.
- Runtime death, process kill and non-yielding code retain existing limitations.
- Pool close does not certify server-session termination or rollback.
- Types do not stop arbitrary tokio::spawn, leaked handles or remote effects.
- No existing database migrations or durable delivery formats change.
- Preserve application handler absence and intentionally unapproved readiness.

title: Observe readiness through protected service completion
description:
## Outcome

Applications that adopt `service::start`, which `batter-otlp` requires, can observe readiness and enforce a readiness deadline through the service owner, instead of keeping their own completion glue beside it.

## Evidence (read-only two-consumer survey, 2026-09-27; consumers A and B are independently deployed downstream Tokio/Axum/SQLx/PostgreSQL services that pin Batter by Git revision; their identities and file paths are kept outside this tracker)

- `ServiceOwner` offers `observer`, `wait` and `request_shutdown`; `ServiceObserver` offers `wait` (`crates/batter-core/src/service/driver.rs:36-102`). Neither exposes readiness or startup output.
- Consumer A waits for readiness under its own deadline (a timeout around readiness, then checked shutdown) and logs the listening address only after readiness. It keeps Batter metrics disabled because adopting the OTLP adapter means moving to `service::start` and rebuilding that glue.

## Scope

A read-only readiness observation on `ServiceOwner` and `ServiceObserver` without shutdown or approval authority; an optional readiness deadline whose expiry requests drain and is reported distinctly; and delivery of the typed startup output from batter-syah.

## Acceptance Criteria

- An example adopts service::start with readiness observation, a readiness deadline and typed output, with the OTLP adapter enabled.
- Tests cover readiness before and after the deadline, deadline expiry requesting drain, observer survival after owner loss, and unchanged diagnostic ordering.
- ADR-010 invalid-state review, contracts, status row and rustdoc are updated; bash scripts/verify.sh passes.

title: Avoid repeating relation-owner authority for every column
description:
Verified low-severity residual from the comprehensive review-fix loop; below its medium repair threshold. Claude identified the mechanism; parent static triage confirmed it in the final working files.

crates/batter-sqlx/src/verification/authority/requests.rs::inspect_relation_columns passes the relation owner into inspect_acl_object_parts for every column. privileges.rs::IndexedAcl::actual_for supplies all four column privileges and their grant options for that owner, and inspect_acl_object_parts_collect also adds Ownership. An otherwise denied owner therefore produces nine owner-derived findings per column in addition to relation-level findings. About 1,000 owned ten-column tables can fit the 10,000-column capture bound but exceed the 100,000-finding bound, converting useful ownership diagnostics into EvaluationCapacity. This is diagnostic amplification, not a false pass; capacity errors remain conservative.

Remediation: report owner-implied authority at its owning relation without repeating it for every column. Preserve independently granted column privileges/grant options, explicit column policy exceptions and PUBLIC findings. Acceptance: a multi-column owner fixture retains its relation ownership violation without linear duplicate owner diagnostics, and a near-capacity fixture preserves actionable findings; explicit column-only grants remain detected.

Causal group R3; pinned working-tree HEAD ff507dcf48c688bbc31d99a517cfd5888de5910a. No repair attempt in this loop.

title: Let finite commands own Unix-signal cancellation and return checked owned values
description:
## Outcome

A finite command on the canonical path installs its own Unix signal listeners and returns its checked success value, so operator and CLI roots stop rebuilding signal wiring and stop calling `expect` after a successful check.

## Evidence (read-only two-consumer survey, 2026-09-27; consumers A and B are independently deployed downstream Tokio/Axum/SQLx/PostgreSQL services that pin Batter by Git revision; their identities and file paths are kept outside this tracker)

- Both consumers install SIGTERM and SIGINT listeners by hand around `Command` and cancel the retained owner. Protected startup already offers `with_unix_signals`; `Command::new(context, cleanup, work)` has no equivalent (`crates/batter-core/src/command.rs:69`).
- `check_command` returns `Result<SharedCommandReport<T, E>, CommandFailure<T, E>>` (`crates/batter-core/src/command/report.rs:156-164`). Callers then use `expect` to reach the value: three sites in consumer B and one in consumer A. Consumer B also needs `T: Clone` to copy results out of the shared report.
- Consumer B runs three signal-cancellable stdout publishers so a blocked pipe cannot trap a blocking worker.

## Scope

- Protected command construction that installs Unix signal listeners before work starts and turns a signal into cancellation of the retained owner, keeping cleanup independently driven.
- A checked completion that yields the owned success value with the retained report, so a successful path cannot panic on extraction and needs no `Clone` bound.

## Non-goals

Output publication (stdout, pipes) stays application policy unless a second concrete need appears.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A runnable example performs a finite command with Unix-signal cancellation and checked value extraction, with no expect, no hand-installed listener and no Clone bound.
- Tests cover a signal before work starts, during work and during cleanup; a failed report still exposes retained work and cleanup errors; listeners are removed on completion.
- ADR-010 invalid-state review, usage docs, status row and rustdoc are updated; bash scripts/verify.sh passes.
acceptance_criteria:
- A runnable example performs a finite command with Unix-signal cancellation and checked value extraction, with no expect, no hand-installed listener and no Clone bound.

title: Prevent competing feature builds from replacing the reference test executable
description:
## Outcome
The ordinary pinned bash scripts/verify.sh run cannot race an all-feature reference-service executable against the default-feature hostile-configuration build.

## Executed evidence and audit (2026-09-30)
During batter-0jsf repairs, the plain complete verification run failed the reference-service metrics executable test. scripts/test_matrix.py schedules cargo test --workspace --all-features --all-targets --locked concurrently with cargo test -p batter-example-reference-service --test configuration --locked (the latter through hostile PG environment variables). Both write target/debug/batter-example-reference-service; examples/reference-service/tests/metrics_export/executable.rs spawns CARGO_BIN_EXE_batter-example-reference-service and expects the metrics-enabled binary. A temporary external launcher serializing those two complete commands allowed the unchanged full tree to pass. See batter-0jsf comments 422 and 423 and PR #36. The race predates that task.

Current source confirms the two commands share one parallel workspace batch. No duplicate tracker task found. This task is independently implementable on origin/master; no dependency on unmerged facade changes. Other ready product work remains valuable, but removing this observed source of false validation failures protects subsequent deliveries. No downstream application audit/change needed for repository-owned verification scheduling.

## Scope and constraints
Prevent these incompatible build/test executions from overlapping through the matrix's owned scheduling or equally narrow artifact isolation. Keep every existing command, feature set, hostile environment, semantic assertion, timeout/output bound and failure accounting. Preserve useful unrelated parallelism and all six matrix parts. Prefer a small explicit schedule change over global locks/wrappers. Add executable regression coverage that exercises command scheduling, proves incompatible executions cannot overlap, and checks command inventory/failure handling without simply snapshotting implementation. Integrate controls into normal verification. Update relevant testing contract/status and this Bead. Do not change application/runtime APIs, weaken the metrics test, add a retry, or expand into generic build orchestration.

## Acceptance
- Full command inventory is retained, and incompatible reference-service feature builds cannot overlap within the matrix.
- Regression controls fail against the prior conflicting schedule, demonstrate enforced ordering/isolation, and preserve bounded failure behavior.
