comments.author: claude-implementer
comments.text:
Implementation complete for batter-oq21 (Claude); review is owned by a separate Codex session. Task stays in_progress until that review completes.

WHAT CHANGED

scripts/test_matrix.py now declares, per labelled command, the debug executable it uplifts and the feature selection it uplifts it under, and refuses any plan that puts two selections for one executable in the same batch:

- UPLIFTED_BINARIES declares workspace-tests as the all-features producer of target/debug/batter-example-reference-service and configuration-hostile-environment as the default-feature producer.
- conflicting_binaries(labels) reports executables a batch would build under more than one selection. _scheduled() applies it to every batch of every part and additionally rejects a plan that renames, repeats or drops a declared label, so a later edit cannot silently disable the declaration.
- The workspace part now runs two batches: (workspace-tests, reference-runner-controls) then (configuration-hostile-environment, release-future-sizes).

Cause: Cargo uplifts one debug executable per binary target and builds a package's binaries for its integration tests so they can spawn CARGO_BIN_EXE_*. The build directory lock is released when linking finishes, not when tests end, so the default-feature reference build replaced the metrics-enabled executable while examples/reference-service/tests/metrics_export/executable.rs was still spawning it.

Every command, feature set, hostile environment, semantic assertion, timeout, output bound and failure accounting is unchanged. All six parts and all 24 commands remain. Useful unrelated parallelism is preserved: an unrelated command still runs beside each of the two conflicting builds. No global lock, external launcher, serialization wrapper, blind retry or per-command target directory was introduced; no application or runtime API changed; the metrics test was not weakened; nothing from PR #36 was cherry-picked.

REGRESSION COVERAGE

Six new controls in scripts/test_parallel_process.py, integrated into normal verification through the existing runner-controls command of the scripts part (that suite is now 31 tests, previously 25). They execute the real matrix.main() scheduling with stand-in subprocesses that write, hold and re-read a shared artifact the way the real build and test phases do, and assert against recorded start/finish spans:

- test_scheduled_builds_never_overlap_and_keep_the_uplifted_artifact: the two declared runs never overlap, the artifact survives, and an unrelated command still overlaps each of them.
- test_prior_schedule_still_replaces_the_artifact_under_the_same_control: the same stand-ins under the prior single batch observe the replaced artifact and a failing exit status, so the coverage is sensitive to the defect and not to the current batch shape.

title: Publish before/after migration notes for public API hard cuts
description:
## Outcome

Every public hard cut ships with a before/after migration note, so an agent upgrading a Git-pinned consumer can apply it mechanically instead of rediscovering replacements from compiler errors.

## Evidence (read-only two-consumer survey, 2026-09-27; consumers A and B are independently deployed downstream Tokio/Axum/SQLx/PostgreSQL services that pin Batter by Git revision; their identities and file paths are kept outside this tracker)

- Consumer B is 139 commits behind master as of 2026-09-27, under a no-incidental-upgrade policy. Catching up needs about 60 mechanical edits, 47 of them `OperationContext::new` call sites moving to `OperationOwner`, plus a manifest cut from side pins to the unified workspace.
- Consumer A has re-pinned roughly twenty times; its adoption log records each hard cut found through compiler errors, for example the `OperationContext` constructors, Runlimit denial accessors, `PgLease::connection` and `return_to_pool`, and the Runledger failure-policy change.
- `CHANGELOG.md` labels one entry "Breaking:", and the tree has no `#[deprecated]` items.

## Scope

- A "Breaking:" CHANGELOG entry with before/after code for each hard cut since 0.0.1 (2026-09-22), including the operation-owner split and the Runledger/Runlimit workspace cut.
- A rule in AGENTS.md "Changes must include" that every public hard cut adds such a note.
- `#[deprecated]` shims for one release where a sound compatible form exists, and none where keeping the old form would reintroduce an invalid state.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Backfilled notes cover every removed or renamed public item since 0.0.1, checked against a public-API diff between the 0.0.1 commit and the current head.
- AGENTS.md states the rule, and the next hard cut follows it.

title: Apply typed response policy to probe method rejections without escaping HttpBoundary
description:
## Missing capability

At source revision 717115c61b37293b0c886a816f887f41c74828ad, a consumer cannot
retain a private-response policy on every probe response through the canonical
HttpBoundary -> AssembledHttp -> register path. A GET/HEAD renderer can apply
PrivateResponsePolicy, but unsupported probe methods return Axum's 405 before
that renderer runs. BrowserPolicy applies to guarded route groups, not probes.

Owning layer: batter-axum HTTP assembly. Consumer invariant: all responses on a
private administrative surface, including probe method rejections, carry
cache-control: no-store, x-content-type-options: nosniff and the selected referrer
policy. The scope is response policy, not admission or method-status changes.

## Executed reproduction

Use batter at the revision above with axum enabled, native Axum 0.8.9, Tokio and
Tower ServiceExt. Construct a GroupPolicy::browser with
BrowserPolicy::without_mutation_checks(PrivateResponsePolicy::SameOriginReferrer).
Build HttpBoundary::new(policy), add rendered liveness /live and rendered
readiness /ready, and call PrivateResponsePolicy::apply on the headers inside
both renderer callbacks. Assemble one ordinary /work GET route, then use the
in-process into_router().oneshot API to request the probes.

GET and HEAD /live return 200 with no-store. POST /live returns the expected 405
but cache-control is absent. An executed Rust assertion fails:

```text
assertion `left == right` failed: POST /live: probe method rejection lost the private response policy
  left: None
 right: Some("no-store")
```

Source: crates/batter-axum/src/boundary/probe.rs builds get(...) method routers;
the method fallback does not invoke a renderer. Group middleware is applied in
boundary/assembly.rs before those separate probe routers are merged. This is a
missing canonical capability rather than a claim that a documented group policy
already promises to cover probes.

## Impact and existing scope review

A real consumer port must retain into_router().layer(PrivateResponsePolicy) and
lower-level registration for its private surface. Its public surface can keep
AssembledHttp through registration. The extra layer only applies headers; it does
not replace observation, admission, lifecycle or cleanup.

Open and closed Beads were searched and batter-tc9w.2, batter-tc9w.3,
batter-tc9w.5, batter-http-boundary-fallback-placement-4oxv and batter-lto checked.
The closed fallback issue provides unmatched-path rendering, not probe method
fallback policy. The typed referrer feature selects header values, not placement.
This extension should precede sealing away the escape in batter-tc9w.2.

## Acceptance criteria

- Provide a library-owned typed response-policy selection covering all probe
  methods, including implicit 405 responses, without adding post-assembly layers.
- The supported consumer retains AssembledHttp through registration.
- Test GET/HEAD/POST/OPTIONS on liveness and readiness during starting, ready and
  draining; verify policy headers, unchanged 200/503/405 status, correlation and
  exactly one observation. Probes remain outside application admission.
- Preserve consumers that intentionally select no private probe policy.
- Keep unmatched fallback policy and guarded-group policy contracts explicit.
close_reason: Delivered HttpBoundary::with_probe_response_policy in the batter-tc9w.2 branch at 9451968, so the capability lands with the seal that removes the router escape. Assembly layers the selected PrivateResponsePolicy around the probe routers only; pinned Axum MethodRouter::layer covers the implicit 405 while keeping status and Allow. 48-request matrix plus boundary cases in operational/probe_policy.rs; the filed reproducer passes with no escape. Evidence and limitations in the completion comment.

comments.author: dev
comments.text:
2026-10-05 implemented in the batter-tc9w.2 delivery branch, so the capability
lands with the seal that removes the escape rather than after it.

Cause. A probe is mounted outside every route group, by design, so no admission
gate can reach it; a group's BrowserPolicy is installed around that group's
routes and therefore never reaches a probe. A probe is registered as get(...),
so an unsupported method is answered by that MethodRouter's own fallback, which
runs no renderer. A renderer could apply the policy for GET and HEAD, but not
for the implicit 405, which is exactly what the filed reproduction showed.

Remedy. HttpBoundary::with_probe_response_policy(PrivateResponsePolicy) selects
the policy; assembly layers it around the probe routers before anything is
merged into them, so it reaches exactly the probes. Pinned Axum 0.8.9
MethodRouter::layer maps the layer over every method handler and over fallback,
and carries allow_header through unchanged (method_routing.rs:967-993), which is
why the 405 gains the headers while keeping its status and Allow. route_layer
would skip the fallback and is explicitly rejected in the adapter guide. Nothing
is layered after assembly, so the consumer keeps the sealed AssembledHttp through
registration. Recorded against the primary source in docs/references.md.

Acceptance, per this issue:
- Library-owned typed selection covering all probe methods including the
  implicit 405, with no post-assembly layer: delivered as above.
- The supported consumer retains AssembledHttp through registration: the
  selection is a builder step before assemble(), and registration is unchanged.
- GET/HEAD/POST/OPTIONS on liveness and readiness during starting, ready and
  draining, verifying policy headers, unchanged 200/503/405 status, correlation
  and exactly one observation, probes outside admission:
  crates/batter-axum/tests/operational/probe_policy.rs. One case drives 48
  requests (4 methods x 2 probes x 3 phases x empty-body and rendered probes)
  and requires, per request, the probe's own status, a 36-character generated
  correlation header, the selected no-store/referrer/nosniff values each present
  exactly once, and for every rejection Axum's own Allow: GET,HEAD and empty
  body; the capture requires exactly one completion event per request. A second
  case shows probes answer outside admission: while unapproved, /ready returns
  its own empty-bodied 503 while a guarded route receives the admission
  envelope.
- Consumers that select no private probe policy are preserved: the selection is
  opt-in and a case asserts probe responses carry none of those headers without
  it.
- Unmatched fallback and guarded-group contracts stay explicit: with the
  selection and a group that has no browser policy, a probe method rejection is
  private while /work and an unmatched path are not, so the policy cannot leak
  out of the probe routers. Documented in guarantees, integrations, the adapter
  README and the adapter guide.

Scope held. Response headers only: no admission change, no status change, no
method-semantics change, no readiness-decision change. Selecting twice keeps the
last policy, as with_failure_renderer does. Empty-body and rendered probes are
both covered, and a renderer applying the same policy does not duplicate headers
because apply inserts rather than appends.

Evidence. The reproduction filed in this issue was run verbatim against the new
API with in_process() in place of the removed into_router(), and passes for all
eight method/path combinations with no router escape. bash scripts/verify.sh
passed on the pinned toolchain; the owning delivery record is batter-tc9w.2.

Not executed: the downstream consumer copies were not rebuilt against this
capability, so the consumer's own 48-combination suite and its real-process
lifecycle suites remain its prior evidence at 1e78d46; a fresh-agent usability
evaluation for this API is proposed and unexecuted. ADR-010 carries the
proactive invalid-state assessment.

title: Declare and verify PostgreSQL transaction timeouts in session profiles
description:
Outcome: let a consumer declare idle_in_transaction_session_timeout and transaction_timeout in PgSessionProfile, with library-owned application and verification throughout the existing profiled pool, atomic and snapshot paths. Ownership belongs to batter-sqlx; timeout values remain application policy.

Audit correction (2026-09-22): the originally filed claim that PgConnectOptions startup timeouts become zero after DISCARD ALL is disproved on PostgreSQL 18.6 with SQLx 0.9.0 and the current Batter implementation. Startup options remain the session reset defaults. Values set later by SET/set_config are reset; PgProfiledPool also intentionally replaces supplied pool hooks. A generic fixture using after_connect session policy therefore loses settings that the profile cannot express, whereas the production-style startup-options path retains them. Preserve this distinction in the regression and documentation.

Confirmed gap: profile.rs declares/applies/verifies only statement_timeout and lock_timeout; with_setting rejects both missing built-in GUCs. No declarative profile contract can establish or revalidate the two transaction settings. A profiled atomic callback can SET both to zero and still complete successfully because those values are absent from verification. A connection-options workaround cannot supply that missing verification contract.

Affected source: the downstream pin 70cc6a05be6857aca6ea2f5f127258e75e673d8c and audited HEAD d28a500dd10deeb957e32d478c4f85ca10e2e13d have identical profile.rs. Relevant entrypoints are crates/batter-sqlx/src/profile.rs, profiled_pool.rs, atomic.rs::validate and snapshot.rs::inspect_with_profile.

Limits: idle-in-transaction timeout bounds an idle interval; transaction_timeout bounds transaction duration. These server settings do not cancel an arbitrary Rust callback or release a held local pool lease. Existing OperationContext-owned runners govern cooperative local deadlines. Preserve uncertain commit/rollback outcomes and the distinction between local retirement and observed backend termination. Arbitrary SQL remains an escape hatch; verification is not a sandbox.
design:
Implement as one cohesive adapter task; no prerequisite delivery Bead was identified. Do not add core dependencies, provisioning, migrations, reset callbacks, retries or a replacement transaction owner.

Recommended compatibility path: add a canonical constructor requiring all four timeout selections (a seven-argument constructor is sufficient; no framework or typestate hierarchy is needed). Keep fields private and reuse the exact whole-millisecond 0..=i32::MAX validation. Zero explicitly disables the selected timeout; nonzero selection is application policy. Preserve the existing constructor's source compatibility and inherited reset-default behavior for the two previously undeclared settings. Mark that constructor as the weaker compatibility path in rustdoc, and lead examples with the complete declaration. Internally distinguish undeclared legacy fields from explicit zero: silently defaulting new fields to zero would disable existing connection/role/database budgets. API spelling is an implementation choice; the complete canonical declaration and unchanged legacy behavior are acceptance requirements.

Apply the new declared values in PgSessionProfile::apply after reset and before BEGIN; verify numeric millisecond values through pg_catalog.pg_settings in the shared verify method. Existing after_connect, before_acquire and after_release hooks, atomic validation and snapshot validation must use the same fields. Keep with_setting's prohibition, including mixed-case spellings. Preserve redacted setup errors with retained native causes, failed/cancelled setup retirement, poisoning on detected drift, and existing acknowledged/uncertain disposition.

Version contract: transaction_timeout was introduced in PostgreSQL 17; PostgreSQL 18 is the native verification baseline. A complete declaration requires the parameter to exist, including when explicitly disabled. Missing/unsupported parameters must fail setup before callback access, never silently skip the declared budget. Legacy construction must not acquire a new parameter/version requirement. Use native setup failure or an explicit capability check; do not claim older-version execution without evidence.

ADR-010 assessment: invalid precision/range is locally rejectable; complete canonical timeout selection belongs in construction; reset/apply/verification ordering belongs to the adapter. Timeout selection, including zero and relative values, is application policy, not the core parent/child deadline invariant. PostgreSQL precedence and termination are upstream behavior. SQL mutation between checks, backend disappearance and a pending Rust callback are remote/execution limits, not locally provable permanent guarantees. No repeated repair loop or fresh-agent usability evaluation was executed by this audit.
acceptance_criteria:
1. A canonical declarative profile requires explicit statement, lock, idle-in-transaction and total-transaction timeout selections, validates exact whole milliseconds and PostgreSQL's signed-32-bit range before I/O, and treats zero as explicit disable. Existing constructor callers retain prior behavior; omission must not silently disable inherited settings. Rustdoc and a generic compiling example explain the compatibility boundary.
2. Shared apply/verify enforce both new declared values after reset, before work and at existing atomic/snapshot validation boundaries. All three PgProfiledPool hooks retain ownership. with_setting cannot override them; no caller hook or paired reset step is required. Detected drift cannot yield ordinary successful completion.
3. Offline cases cover each new timeout independently: zero, one millisecond, maximum, overflow and fractional milliseconds; built-in/mixed-case override rejection; redacted formatting. Live PG18 cases distinguish startup options surviving reset from SET/hook values being cleared, then prove explicit profile values override different startup/reset defaults, including explicit zero overriding nonzero defaults and legacy construction preserving existing defaults.
4. Live cases cover initial connection, reused checkout and after_release restoration before try_acquire, plus profiled atomic and snapshot paths. Change each timeout independently during scope SQL to prove revalidation rejects drift and retains the terminal cause/disposition. Exercise setup failure/cancellation retirement with existing controls and preserve retained native errors and redaction.
5. Independently observe server behavior: idle termination while awaiting the client and total-transaction termination despite individually short statements. Use bounded polling/observation and cleanup, not only SHOW or elapsed sleeps. Preserve the documented fact that server termination alone does not cancel Rust work or release a still-held pool slot. Keep deadline/cancellation and ambiguous commit handling conservative; add no automatic retry.
6. Document the PG17 parameter introduction, PG18 executed baseline, explicit-zero semantics, timeout precedence and fail-closed unsupported-parameter behavior. Record primary sources in docs/references.md. Do not advertise unexecuted platform/version coverage.
7. Update the SQLx contract/README, relevant guarantees/integration text, implemented-status row, failure tests and this Bead. Register added live cases in scripts/sqlx_live.py's exact inventory; keep .jig.toml and .agent/jig-contract.json input scopes synchronized if new inputs require changes. Use generic scenarios and external fixture provisioning.
8. Delivery evidence must include adapter offline/live verification, required final fresh api:test/Jig gates, both Rust 1.98.1 and exact 1.94.0 verification matrices/rustdoc and the required built HTTP smokes per AGENTS.md/docs/testing.md, reusing only qualifying receipts. Label fresh-agent evaluations proposed/unexecuted unless actually run. No commit or publication is authorized by this audit.
notes:
Audit 2026-09-22: implementable with the corrected scope/design/acceptance above; implementation remains open. Only this Bead/export is changed by the audit. No production source, dependency or downstream edits were made.

Executed evidence: isolated disposable PostgreSQL 18.6 container on Linux; Rust 1.98.1; SQLx 0.9.0; standalone temporary Rust consumer against local batter-sqlx. PGOPTIONS/psql control showed setting=reset_val=10000/15000 with source=client before and after DISCARD ALL. Rust probe asserted: (a) PgProfiledPool checkout with startup options returns (10s,15s); (b) reset_and_apply clears after_connect SET values to (0,0) on default-zero server; (c) a supplied hook is replaced and omitted profile values remain (0,0); (d) run_atomic_profiled with initial nonzero startup values accepts SET of both omitted fields to zero; (e) an independent pg_stat_activity observer sees a backend disappear under a 250ms idle-in-transaction timeout while the held one-slot pool still has size=1, idle=0, and try_acquire=None. Probe has a 30s outer watchdog and closes all owned connections/pools.

Source evidence for downstream diagnosis: production construction adds PgConnectOptions::options, while fixture pool construction sets values in after_connect then copies those options into PgProfiledPool, which replaces hooks. The fixture assertion expects zeros; a separate server-timeout contract expects nonzero values. These differ and must not be treated as proof that startup options are erased. Consumer source was inspected read-only; its full tests were not run. Private consumer names/paths are intentionally excluded from this upstream task.

Primary sources checked: https://www.postgresql.org/docs/18/sql-reset.html ; https://www.postgresql.org/docs/18/sql-discard.html ; https://www.postgresql.org/docs/18/runtime-config-client.html ; https://www.postgresql.org/docs/17/release-17.html . Local SQLx 0.9.0 source: sqlx-postgres/src/options/mod.rs::options emits startup -c arguments, connection/establish.rs sends them in Startup.

Reproduction artifact for this session: /tmp/batter-qhps-audit-vykcsnv6 (Cargo-generated lockfile and src/main.rs); run cargo run --offline --manifest-path <artifact>/Cargo.toml -- <dedicated-local-PG18-port>. Server must have default-zero transaction settings and a disposable local trust-auth postgres login. This is an audit probe, not a committed regression or full workspace receipt. The implementation must add durable tests described above.

Concurrent unrelated workspace manifest version edits occurred during the audit; Cargo regenerated only the temporary consumer lockfile before the final passing probe. Audited profile/atomic/pool source remained unchanged. No full Rust matrix, HTTP smoke, macOS, PG16/17 runtime or consumer-usability execution is claimed.

title: Export role grant manifests for Runledger and Runlimit relations
description:
## Outcome

Applications compose native Runledger and Runlimit grant requirements into their own ExactRoleManifest, compile once, and use the same compiled value for exact-role verification and inert GRANT rendering. Remove copied native table/column privilege lists without broadening a consumer's selected operations or moving application authorization into Batter.

## Audited evidence (2026-10-03)

Baseline: Batter 454fe462a2773d222bde8dacf8c230b9d23b2280; native Runledger 0.13.0, native Runlimit 0.4.0, SQLx 0.9.0. Two independently maintained downstream services were inspected read-only; deployment is not established. Private consumer names/paths and commits stay outside this tracker. The earlier claim that both were deployed is withdrawn. No live validation or adoption rehearsal was executed in this audit.

- Consumer A has narrow intent-submission column grants, separate full-schema inspection for producer/worker logins, a direct-job worker with scheduler disabled, fixed-window quotas and authentication attempts. Consumer B uses intent submission, direct-job workers with default native loops, GCRA quotas and authentication attempts. Both hand-maintain native grants; B's broad worker CRUD is not an oracle for least authority.
- Consumer policies differ: A permits selected PUBLIC delivery; B denies it, while both retain PostgreSQL row-type USAGE. Fragments must not replace those policies.
- Native intent recording inserts explicit columns and reads selected identity/status/enqueue_request fields with FOR KEY SHARE during duplicate resolution: runledger/runledger-postgres/src/jobs/queue/intents.rs::insert_org_scoped_intent, insert_unscoped_intent, load_existing_intent_with_key_share. UPDATE(id) used for row locking is real mutation authority; A's immutability trigger is application-owned. enqueue_request contains request data; a column-restricted fragment cannot claim payload secrecy or row/tenant isolation.
- Full Runledger schema verification locks _sqlx_migrations, job_queue, workflow_runs, workflow_steps and runledger_migration_history before inspection: runledger/runledger-postgres/src/migrations.rs::ensure_schema_compatible_after_idempotency_cutover. This authority must be an explicit separate selection, never a hidden prerequisite of intent submission.
- Runlimit fixed-window and GCRA paths read/lock capacity shards; GCRA updates observed_at_ms. Capacity row_count mutation belongs to installed trigger execution, not serving grants. Attempt admission performs bounded expiry deletion internally, so DELETE is required even without a separate maintenance caller. Sources: runlimit/runlimit-postgres/src/{admission.rs,cleanup_expired.sql,gcra.rs,attempts.rs,attempt_cleanup.sql} and the three native migration directories.
- ExactRoleManifest currently has individual add_* methods and consuming compile, but no fragment composition (crates/batter-sqlx/src/verification/manifest.rs). The compiler already normalizes duplicate declarations and rejects semantic conflicts (manifest/compile.rs). Reuse it.

## Design and ownership

1. Add the smallest bounded additive grant-fragment abstraction to batter-sqlx::verification. It carries only object declarations; it cannot carry or replace database policy, discovery scope/defaults, role ceilings or the current-database ownership guard. Application code continues to choose those policies. Adding a fragment is one operation: either consume the destination on failure or leave it unchanged. A failed append must not leave an executable partial grant set. Keep aggregate input/expansion limits and one final compiler/renderer; no new ACL evaluator, SQL parser or provisioning engine.
2. Native Runledger grant definitions belong in runledger-postgres alongside its queries/migrations (it already depends on batter-sqlx). Reexport through batter-runledger and the facade. Runlimit's ExactRoleManifest integration belongs in batter-runlimit behind its existing postgres feature. Native runlimit-postgres remains independent of every Batter package (scripts/check_runlimit_workspace.py::validate_graph). Its SQL/migrations are the source of truth, protected by cross-package drift and operation tests; do not add a native ACL DSL or reverse dependency.
3. Expose explicit operation selections, not application role names or a universal administrator preset. Constructors use validated schema identifiers and nonempty selections; callers never enumerate native columns or attach parent relation declarations. Carry explicit PUBLIC delivery and row-type-USAGE choices for the fragment's own objects, compatible with the existing manifest semantics. Do not silently widen to table-level grants, use ALL PRIVILEGES, grant ownership/grant options, or change discovery defaults to avoid conflicts. Contradictory declarations fail before rendering. Names and private layout are implementer choices.
4. Include schema-USAGE requirements through an explicit compatible schema declaration; database CONNECT/TEMP policy remains application-owned. Full-snapshot inspection uses the actual native _sqlx_migrations relation; do not parameterize an alternate ledger unsupported by the native verifier. Runlimit fragments must not select a migration ledger: native Runlimit supports both shared SQLx history and application-vendored migrations. Grant requirements describe this source version's operations, not proof of installed schema, remote effects or application security. Runtime configuration and selected operations remain explicit application policy; document the supported supervisor configurations.

## Bounded capability inventory

Names below describe behavior, not mandated Rust identifiers. Keep overlapping requirements composable and normalized.

- Runledger intent submission: protected required-intent recording/observation, new and same-key duplicate requests, conflicts, global and organization scopes, inside application transactions. Use explicit SELECT/INSERT columns and only the row-lock UPDATE needed; no whole-intent SELECT or unrelated queue authority.
- Runledger full schema snapshot: the existing privileged read-only verification path, separately selected. History-only restricted verification is not this capability.
- Runledger direct-job execution: claiming, release of an unstarted claim after failed RUNNING persistence, heartbeat/progress/checkpoint, success, retry and terminal failure, dead-letter writes, resource claims and reaping. Include incidental workflow-table hooks used by direct jobs. Intent promotion, catalog sync (including exact disable) and scheduled direct-job dispatch are explicit additional groups. Provide/test compositions for scheduler-disabled and default-loop direct-job supervisors against a direct-only workload. Existing workflow-linked rows can reach shared hooks/reaping; these fragments do not establish workflow isolation or mixed-workload support. Required UPDATE/DELETE privileges remain usable by arbitrary SQL: release of an unstarted claim requires DELETE on job_attempts (jobs/queue/release.rs::delete_attempt_row_tx). Do not claim those rows are protected from pruning. Exclude arbitrary workflow execution, replay/recovery administration, arbitrary reader APIs and history-pruning APIs from the supported operation contract.
- Runlimit fixed-window admission and expiry cleanup are independently selectable; GCRA admission and expiry cleanup likewise. Retain column-level shard authority: row_count and counter-key (config_fingerprint/subject_key) mutations are not granted to the serving login. Fixed-window policy_id/scope_id metadata updates remain required; UPDATE(capacity_shard) used for locking is real mutation authority, not an ACL-enforced lock-only capability. The actual SQL decides the required lock column, not copied broad consumer grants.
- Runlimit authentication attempts cover admit, claim/finish in the caller's transaction, and native completion paths, including internal expiry cleanup. Do not invent a separate public attempts cleanup API.
- Routine requirements follow actual direct invocation. Native trigger presence is not by itself a requirement to grant serving EXECUTE on every trigger function. Tests establish runtime behavior with those EXECUTEs revoked. Installed trigger ownership, body safety, owner privileges and application-added trigger dependencies stay explicit prerequisites/application policy.

## Execution sequence

A. Implement and test additive fragment composition in batter-sqlx, including atomic failure and conflicting options. Keep existing ExactRoleManifest callers source-compatible.
B. Build the supported operation-to-object/privilege inventory from current native SQL, map it into the two producers, and add facade reachability without changing default feature graphs. Freeze an independent expected privilege inventory in tests; do not derive the oracle from the exported fragment. Couple review of that inventory to native migration/query changes.
C. Prove the selected operations under real restricted PostgreSQL 18 logins, then demonstrate application composition. Use generic scenarios corresponding to both audited consumer policies, including column-restricted intent + application SQL + one limiter family and the two direct-worker configurations. A source-only consumer rehearsal may use isolated temporary copies; do not modify downstream working trees, dependency pins or deployed roles.
D. Update public rustdoc/example, contracts, status, references and this Bead with actual evidence and limitations. Complete the ADR-010 invalid-state review before declaring the API ready.

## Verification and completion

See the acceptance_criteria field for the falsifiable delivery checks. Required implementation validation: bash scripts/verify.sh once on the pinned Rust 1.98.1 toolchain, plus explicit PostgreSQL 18 live fragment tests. Local MSRV/Jig plan/receipt instructions from historical tasks do not apply. Run native Runledger tests through its existing Docker support. Batter SQLx/Runlimit adapter live fixtures remain externally provisioned; reuse the existing explicit-URL test pattern, with prerequisites failing instead of silently skipping.

Add a discoverable facade integration target for the cross-adapter grant compositions and document its exact ignored-live command; extend a bounded inventory-checked runner to execute every new case. If SQLx live cases are added, update scripts/sqlx_live.py and run bash scripts/test_sqlx_live.sh with its three required endpoints. Ensure scripts/test_matrix.py compiles the new target and executes all offline controls; do not count compiled/ignored cases as live evidence. Keep existing native Runlimit PostgreSQL 16 CI coverage, while new authority claims are scoped to executed PostgreSQL 18 evidence.

Primary PostgreSQL 18 sources checked for this audit (2026-10-03):
- https://www.postgresql.org/docs/18/sql-lock.html — table-level LOCK privilege rules; do not confuse these with a column UPDATE grant for a row-locking SELECT.
- https://www.postgresql.org/docs/18/sql-select.html — locking SELECT requires UPDATE on at least one column in addition to SELECT requirements.
- https://www.postgresql.org/docs/18/ddl-priv.html — direct/PUBLIC/inherited grants, column versus relation scope, default routine/type privileges.
- https://www.postgresql.org/docs/18/sql-createtrigger.html — trigger creation privileges, distinct from executing DML against an installed trigger. The runtime-revocation control above is required before claiming that behavior.
Record implementation-specific semantics and executed server version in docs/references.md; recheck selected upstream versions before implementing.

## Compatibility, exclusions and handoff

Additive library API only; preserve existing native SQL/migrations and manifest semantics. No production/downstream migration rewrite, role creation/ownership transfer, ACL mutation, automated grant application/revocation, installation verifier, arbitrary SQL least-privilege inference, or production rollout is authorized. Disposable test-fixture role/schema provisioning, ACL revocation controls and cleanup are explicitly required and permitted. GRANT rendering cannot remove existing excessive privileges; consumer adoption must separately review/reconcile their provisioned roles and retained PUBLIC policy. An older pin continues to use its existing hand-written manifest until deliberately upgraded.

batter-572p owns payload-restricted full schema verification; batter-hw3k owns new restricted correlation reads; batter-c14a owns definer-owner verification. They are not prerequisites and this task must not claim their outcomes. Leave the existing related edge to batter-hw3k; add no artificial blocker.

Ready for implementation after audit. First action: recheck this Bead/current HEAD, then define the minimal additive fragment and independent expected-grant fixtures from the bounded inventory above. Pure source inspection grounds the plan; every proposed runtime/consumer-adoption result remains unexecuted until recorded. Commit, push, publication and downstream changes require their own authorization.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Additive composition preserves application database/discovery/role/ownership policy; validated schema and nonempty native selections include required parent relations. Duplicate/order-independent composition renders deterministically. Conflicting purposes/PUBLIC/row-type options fail closed, capacity overflow cannot retain a partial fragment, and no compiled policy escapes the existing verification boundary.
2. A non-public mixed-case native schema compiles/renders with correct quoting and executes under the matching session profile. Same-named objects/grants in a shadow schema cannot satisfy verification of the selected schema; no hardcoded public or implicit search-path guarantee. Each exported operation group has a documented source-version contract mapping native entrypoints to exact relation/column/routine needs. Current native migration inventory is independently pinned and changes force a grant-coverage review; representative query/grant mutation controls detect missing privileges. Do not claim automatic least-privilege inference or treat migration-string equality as execution evidence.
3. On disposable PostgreSQL 18, provision non-owner/non-superuser logins without inherited privilege escape routes using the fragment plus explicitly declared application database/schema policy. Execute intent insertion, exact duplicate/conflict and rollback in both scopes; full snapshot only under its selected grants; direct-job success/retry/terminal/unstarted-claim-release/reaper/resource-claim paths, promotion, catalog disable and a due scheduled job; fixed-window/GCRA first insert, update/denial/batch and real expiry deletion; attempt admission/denial, failure settlement with incremented retry delay, success settlement, stale completion and expiry cleanup plus transaction claim/finish. Worker cases cover scheduler-disabled and default-loop compositions and fail on retained native permission/cleanup errors, not merely readiness or empty-loop startup.
4. An independent expected privilege oracle and actual forbidden operations detect overgrant: intent-only cannot claim/promote/synchronize catalog or SELECT the payload column; limited direct-worker composition cannot create workflows or DELETE job_events/job_logs/job_queue when excluded from its reviewed operation inventory; limiter families cannot access unselected stores or update capacity row_count or counter config_fingerprint/subject_key. State that enqueue_request still carries request data and row-lock UPDATE (including capacity_shard) is real mutation authority; fixed-window policy_id/scope_id metadata updates are intentional. Required relation DELETE/UPDATE remains arbitrary SQL authority over those rows, including job_attempts deletion for unstarted-claim release; no generic history protection, row/tenant isolation, immutable identity or payload secrecy claim follows.
5. Remove a required column/relation privilege and require both failed native operation and verifier rejection; add excessive table UPDATE or grant-option authority and require rejection. Runtime tests revoke native trigger-function EXECUTE from serving/PUBLIC, retaining trusted installed triggers; add EXECUTE only for independently demonstrated direct calls. Routine-owner/body and application trigger security remain outside fragment guarantees.
6. Generic consumer-shaped examples compose application relations/columns/routines with both adapters using only a batter dependency. Demonstrate strict PUBLIC-denial and explicitly permitted PUBLIC-delivery policies plus row-type handling without resetting caller defaults. Replace hand-copied native grant declarations in those examples and record source-only rehearsal against both audited shapes; do not change real consumer pins or working trees. Document required setup, selected native operations, omitted operations and grant-only rollout limitations.
7. Preserve native dependency direction, opt-in feature isolation, shared type identity, native SQL/migration digests and generated Cargo.lock. Exported APIs have rustdoc/examples and ADR-010 review; update guarantees/integrations/status and primary PostgreSQL references. Root pinned-toolchain verification and the explicit inventory-checked PostgreSQL 18 fragment suite pass; record exact commands/platform/server version/results here. MSRV runs only in CI; no hosted/adoption/deployment claim without executed evidence.
notes:
2026-10-03 implemented and reviewed. Linux x86-64, pinned Rust 1.98.1.

Delivered API. batter-sqlx gains GrantFragment and FragmentObjectPolicy in crates/batter-sqlx/src/verification/manifest/fragment.rs. A fragment carries only schema/relation/column/routine declarations; FragmentObjectPolicy carries the application's schema privileges, schema and relation ownership allowances, the exact privileges PUBLIC may deliver, and the row-type USAGE choice, and splits every declaration by its individual PUBLIC-delivery choice. ExactRoleManifest::with_fragment consumes the manifest, so a rejected declaration or a declaration-bound overflow leaves no partial grant set. SchemaGrantSpec gained read accessors. Native inventories: runledger_postgres::grants (IntentSubmission, SchemaSnapshot, DirectJobExecution, IntentPromotion, CatalogSync, ScheduledDispatch) and batter_runlimit::grants behind its existing postgres feature (FixedWindowAdmission, FixedWindowExpiryCleanup, GcraAdmission, GcraExpiryCleanup, AuthenticationAttempts). Reachable as batter::runledger::grants and batter::runlimit::grants with no default feature-graph change; native runlimit-postgres gained no Batter dependency.

Executed PostgreSQL 18.6 semantics probes decided three relation-level requirements that column grants cannot express; all are recorded in docs/references.md. LOCK TABLE ... IN ACCESS SHARE MODE needs relation-level SELECT, so the full-schema snapshot is relation-level and stays a separate selection. Reading the ctid system column needs relation-level SELECT, so Runlimit's bounded fixed-window expiry delete reads every counter column including policy_id and scope_id. SHARE ROW EXCLUSIVE and ROW EXCLUSIVE table locks need relation-level UPDATE, DELETE, TRUNCATE or MAINTAIN, and MAINTAIN alone suffices, so catalog synchronization and scheduled dispatch require MAINTAIN on job_definitions and job_schedules rather than table-wide UPDATE. Two further probes shaped the column lists: a locking SELECT (including FOR KEY SHARE and FOR NO KEY UPDATE) needs UPDATE on at least one column, and ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE needs SELECT on the arbiter columns and on every column referenced through EXCLUDED.

Validation. bash scripts/verify.sh passed on the pinned toolchain after each repair round. The explicit PostgreSQL 18.6 grant suite ran through the bounded inventory-checked runner with a complete case inventory: 10 cases passed, 0 ignored (BATTER_SQLX_ADMIN_URL=<redacted superuser URL> cargo test -p batter --features runledger,runlimit-postgres --test grants_live -- --ignored --test-threads=1). The cases provision non-owner, non-superuser NOINHERIT logins from the fragments plus explicitly declared application database, schema and discovery policy, then execute intent recording with exact-duplicate, conflict and rollback handling in global and organization scopes; the separately selected full-schema snapshot and its refusal under intent submission alone; the direct-job lifecycle through claim, RUNNING persistence, heartbeat, ordinary progress, success, handler continuation with re-claim of the advanced run, retry, terminal dead-letter, unstarted prestart claim release, execution resource claim acquisition and trigger-driven release, and lease reaping asserted through reap_expired_leases_with_diagnostics to retain no cleanup error; durable promotion, exact catalog disable and a due scheduled dispatch; scheduler-disabled and default-loop supervisors over a direct-only workload judged by each enabled loop's real effect; fixed-window and GCRA first insert, counter update, denial and real expiry deletion; attempt admission, failure settlement with an increased retry delay, backoff denial, transactional claim/finish and readmission past the quiet period; and one login composing both adapters with its own relation, columns and routine under a permitted PUBLIC-delivery policy beside a second login denying all PUBLIC delivery. Forbidden-operation oracles confirm intent submission cannot read the decoded payload column, promote, claim or write the definition catalog; the worker composition cannot delete job_events, job_queue or job_logs, read job_logs, create workflow runs or read job_queue.enqueue_request; each limiter family cannot reach another store, update a capacity ledger's row_count, or mutate counter-key columns. Revoking one required column privilege fails both the native operation and verification of the same compiled role, and adding table-level UPDATE or a grant option is rejected. The suite revokes all routine privileges from PUBLIC in the native schemas and asserts no serving login or PUBLIC role holds EXECUTE on any routine there while the installed triggers still run. Offline oracles freeze each operation group's rendering as a literal and pin the native migration identities, and run in the ordinary workspace matrix.

Review. Cumulative gpt-6-astra / xhigh / read-only review of 6049b529ffb568de46a34b740a00a6633cf70668..HEAD across three executed rounds. Round 3 found three P2 defects, all confirmed and fixed at their own layer: FragmentObjectPolicy::declare_schema derived one PUBLIC-delivery choice for every schema privilege, so permitting PUBLIC USAGE also accepted PUBLIC CREATE; lease reaping always runs its bounded quiesced workflow-claim cleanup, whose workflow_active_claims and workflow_steps.workflow_run_id requirements were missing and whose failure was discarded as a diagnostic; and the attempt case relied on 5 ms and 10 ms backoffs outlasting database round trips. Round 4 found one further P2 defect, also confirmed and fixed: a handler returning a continuation makes the worker call complete_job_continuation_with_outcome_for_lease, which needed workflow_steps.id/execution_kind/allow_handler_continuation and job_queue.run_number. Both inventory repairs have negative controls: removing the privilege again reproduces the exact refusal. Round 5 found no actionable defects. No finding was rejected or escalated, and no standing rejections were recorded.

Not executed. bash scripts/test_sqlx_live.sh was not run: no BATTER_SQLX_AUTH_ACCEPT_URL fixture was available and this change adds no batter-sqlx live case. scripts/sqlx_live.py now names every grants_live case so that runner executes them wherever its three endpoints exist. MSRV was not run locally; it remains CI's. No hosted CI run, no consumer adoption rehearsal against the real downstream working trees, no publication and no deployment are claimed; the audited consumer shapes are reproduced only as generic compositions in the facade example and the live suite.

Limitations. The requirements describe this source version's statements; they are not evidence that the native schema is installed, that a remote effect occurred, or that an application's authorization model is correct. Adoption is grant-only: rendered statements cannot remove privileges a provisioned role already holds, including privileges reached through PUBLIC, so consumers must reconcile their existing roles separately. enqueue_request still carries submitted request data. Row-locking UPDATE columns, including UPDATE(id), UPDATE(capacity_shard) and UPDATE(updated_at) on workflow_active_claims, are ordinary mutation authority; UPDATE(run_number) is run-identity mutation authority; fixed-window policy_id and scope_id metadata updates are intentional; releasing an unstarted claim requires DELETE on job_attempts; lease reaping requires DELETE on workflow_active_claims; MAINTAIN also permits VACUUM, ANALYZE, REINDEX and CLUSTER. The direct-job requirements support a direct-only workload and establish neither workflow isolation nor mixed-workload support. The ADR-010 public-API invalid-state review is recorded in docs/adr/010-agent-only-consumption.md; fresh agent implementation and modification evaluations for this API remain proposed and unexecuted. Delivered on branch feat/native-grant-fragments-qjxi as PR 39; hosted CI for that branch is not claimed.

2026-10-03 second review pass. A further multi-reviewer pass reported six findings; all six were confirmed and addressed, and a follow-up gpt-6-astra / xhigh / read-only review of 6049b529ffb568de46a34b740a00a6633cf70668..3240d17 found no actionable defects. Three were substantive. The composition example claimed a separate inspection login while selecting SchemaSnapshot beside IntentSubmission, contradicting the audited Consumer A shape; it now renders a snapshot-only schema_inspector beside the two serving roles, and compose scopes discovery to the schemas a role declares objects in. Fixed-window admission required SELECT on the counter table's generated capacity_shard, which only the cleanup statement reads; the requirement is gone and an admission-only login proves admission needs neither it nor the cleanup selection's relation-wide SELECT. The documented fragment guarantee exceeded what GrantFragment enforces, because its raw builders accept an allowed-only ceiling or a permitted grant option; the narrower contract is attributed to FragmentObjectPolicy in docs/guarantees.md and the ADR-010 assessment, with the recorded reason that enforcing it in the fragment type would remove a legitimate library use without removing a caller obligation. Three were coverage obligations. Schedule catalog creation, the conflict-update path and exact deactivation now run under the restricted CatalogSync login rather than the owner. A restricted live control now distinguishes permitted from denied PUBLIC delivery on native objects, which the rendering comparison cannot; it established that a permitted delivery is scoped per declared object, now documented. The five SchemaGrantSpec accessors were leftovers from an abandoned design with no consumer and are removed rather than documented. The live suite is now 11 cases, all passing through the bounded inventory-checked runner, and bash scripts/verify.sh passed again on the pinned toolchain.

2026-10-03 third review pass. Two further supplied findings and two Codex rounds were all confirmed and fixed, after which a gpt-6-astra / xhigh / read-only review of 6049b529ffb568de46a34b740a00a6633cf70668..a5aadde found no actionable defects. A routine declaration could pass through GrantFragment with no test observing it, so removing the transfer compiled; a focused composition test now carries a routine with its exact overload identity and definer allowance into the compiled policy and the rendered plan, and removing the transfer again fails it. The status record's live-case count was stale at ten and now reports eleven with the coverage added since. CatalogSync required SELECT on job_definitions created_at and updated_at, copied from the RETURNING list of update_job_definition, an administrative API outside the supported contract; both are removed, and the restricted login now also runs the single-definition catalog upsert's conflict-update path. DirectJobExecution required UPDATE(release_after) on job_execution_resource_claims, which only the installed release trigger's cancellation branch writes and which the supported lifecycle never reaches; it is removed and cancellation is documented as outside this contract. The quota acceptance cases decided admission against 400 ms windows, so a slow connection could change a correct decision; both families now use hour-long windows and the owner rewrites the stored expiry timestamps, so every decision follows the stored counter while the restricted login's own DELETE authority still removes the row, and the attempt backoffs moved to seconds for the same reason. Six repair rounds total; bash scripts/verify.sh and the eleven-case PostgreSQL 18.6 suite passed after each.

2026-10-03 fourth review pass. One further supplied finding was confirmed and fixed: the composition example's compose helper added the application schema, relation and columns unconditionally, so the snapshot-only schema_inspector received USAGE on the application schema and SELECT/INSERT on delivery_notes while the example's own narrative denied it, and its test checked only the native snapshot grants. Application objects are now an explicit per-role choice; a role selecting none declares none, and its primary schema and discovery scope follow the schemas it actually declares objects in. The inspection test now rejects the application schema, delivery_notes and the routine alongside the quota store. A gpt-6-astra / xhigh / read-only review of 6049b529ffb568de46a34b740a00a6633cf70668..62090b4 then found no actionable defects. Seven repair rounds total. Hosted CI passed on this branch for the first time: both Rust verification shards (1.94.0 and 1.98.1), the native Runlimit PostgreSQL shards, both macOS subprocess-harness shards and the repository-policy workflow are green, which is the first MSRV evidence for this change.

2026-10-03 fifth review pass. Three further supplied findings were confirmed and fixed, after which a gpt-6-astra / xhigh / read-only review of 6049b529ffb568de46a34b740a00a6633cf70668..825934d found no actionable defects. The example's consumer shape B claimed the native supervisor's default loops but omitted ScheduledDispatch, so its rendered role had no job_schedules authority while the default supervisor enables the scheduler loop; the selection is added, disable_scheduler is documented for narrower configurations, and a test asserts the schedule table lock and fire-recording writes appear with the selection and vanish without it. The example also never declared the application routine that this record and acceptance criterion 6 claim it composes, which left the inspection role's exclusion of that routine vacuous; the routine is now declared under the same explicit PUBLIC choice as the columns, with a positive assertion on the serving shapes. Neither FragmentObjectPolicy ownership choice was exercised, so dropping either propagation compiled and would have made verification reject an owner-reachable login the application deliberately permitted; a test now asserts both choices reach the compiled policy independently across all four combinations, and removing either propagation fails it. Eight repair rounds total; bash scripts/verify.sh and the eleven-case PostgreSQL 18.6 suite passed after each, and hosted CI passed on the branch including both MSRV and macOS shards.

2026-10-04 follow-up review loop. Ran codex review (gpt-6-astra, xhigh, read-only) against the same pinned base until it reported no findings, then the comprehensive-review skill with --scope branch twice; three further repair rounds resulted, taking the total to eleven. Round 9: the direct-job case claimed again immediately after a retry settlement, but the native claim excludes future-dated jobs and the retry sets next_run_at to its completion time plus the policy delay, so asserting PENDING established status rather than eligibility; every claim site now goes through one bounded claim_job helper, and a 1,500 ms retry delay keeps the case passing where the unwaited claim failed at once. Round 10: the consumer-shape tests exercised their own operation lists rather than the roles the example renders, so removing ScheduledDispatch from the worker role left the scheduler test green; the three roles are now shared constants that main renders and the tests assert on. In the same round the live consumer shapes were realigned with the audited ones (the snapshot moved to its own login, shape B gained scheduled dispatch) and both composed logins now execute native work rather than only verifying. Round 11: catalog synchronization, promotion and scheduled dispatch had executed under one combined login, and GCRA admission under a role that also held cleanup grants, so a requirement missing from a narrower selection could be masked; each Runledger group now has its own login running only its own operations with per-login refusal probes, and GCRA admission gained an admission-only login. The status record's drift claim was narrowed: the migration pin and frozen inventories cover migration and requirement changes, while a query-only change that alters required privileges is covered solely by the live cases and only on the paths they execute. The final comprehensive branch review of 454fe462..e1aa3b79 reported no actionable findings. Its remaining noted limitations are that multi-item quota admission and stale attempt completion have no dedicated restricted-role case, and that it authenticated no test results itself; its third note, that expiry cleanup lacks a deletion assertion, is inaccurate -- both families assert the counter row count returns to zero after cleanup. Every round reran bash scripts/verify.sh and the eleven-case PostgreSQL 18.6 suite. Both comprehensive passes were single-reviewer results: the Claude reviewer exited non-zero without a report.

2026-10-04 follow-up review loop, second pass. Ran codex review (gpt-6-astra, xhigh, read-only) against the same pinned base 6049b529ffb568de46a34b740a00a6633cf70668 until it reported no findings, with a comprehensive-review --scope branch pass between, taking the total to eighteen repair rounds. Round 12: the restricted-login quota suite exercised only single-item admissions, never reported a stale completion, and inferred the attempts expiry deletion from a later readmission that an update to the retained row also permits; both families now admit a two-item batch through check_all, the GCRA policy admits two requests so the upsert's existing-counter UPDATE branch runs, a completion whose lease the owner expired must report Stale and a claim finished outside its transaction must stage nothing, and the owner plants an already-expired record in the admitted subject's capacity shard which the next admission's bounded cleanup must delete. Three documentation claims were corrected in the same round: capacity row_count is readable by an admitting login rather than ungranted, permitted PUBLIC delivery covers the policy's schema as well as its relations and columns, and the composition example's setup names the REVOKE ALL ON ALL ROUTINES its own fixture performs. Round 13: the attempt case still decided two assertions against short wall-clock windows, because native admission cleans its shard before the subject row lookup and resets the failure count past the quiet period, so a 1.45-second pause failed a correct run; the policy's delays, quiet period and lease are now hours long and the owner rewrites retry_at_ms and last_failure_ms instead, leaving no sleep in the file, and the example's required setup names all three schemas because the native migrations install trigger functions whose default PUBLIC EXECUTE no role declares. Round 14: both quota cleanups ran only under logins that also held admission grants, which read the capacity ledger's row_count while cleanup does not, so a new grants_live/quota_cleanup.rs adds one cleanup-only login per family that deletes an owner-seeded expired counter while refused the admission insert and that row_count. Round 15: the supervisor cases asserted RuntimeSettlement::Clean and SUCCEEDED counts, but runledger-runtime emits the reaper's coordination-cleanup failures through warn! alone, so revoking DELETE on workflow_active_claims left both compositions settling cleanly with every job succeeding; each composition now asserts reap_expired_leases_with_diagnostics under its own login. Rounds 16, 17 and 18 each repaired a regression the preceding round introduced in that same supervisor helper: the cleanup probe was returned to PENDING and inherited by the next phase, so the owner now parks it and the helper asserts that no job is claimable when it returns; the per-minute schedule could fire again across a UTC minute boundary, so the cadence moved beyond the test window; and that fixed annual boundary was itself calendar-dependent, so the cadence now derives from the captured start with no month mapping to itself. Every repair has an executed negative control, and the three that concern masking also show the case passing under the same privilege gap once the new assertion is removed. Every round reran bash scripts/verify.sh on the pinned toolchain and the eleven-case PostgreSQL 18.6 suite through scripts/sqlx_live.py; the last execution was 2026-10-04 at 8fb65d7, which docs/status.md now names. The final codex review of 6049b529..8fb65d7 and the final comprehensive --scope branch pass of 454fe46..8fb65d7 both reported no actionable findings. Both comprehensive passes remain single-reviewer results: the Claude reviewer could not start because its adapter requires writable temporary files and provider network access that the read-only sandbox denies, and neither pass executed any Rust or PostgreSQL test. Hosted CI passed for rounds 12 through 18 at d5a9d1c: both verify shards (1.94.0 and 1.98.1), both native Runlimit PostgreSQL shards, both macOS subprocess-harness shards and the repository-policy workflow are green, which is the MSRV evidence these rounds could not produce locally. The documentation-only commit recording that result is itself not covered by it.

2026-10-04 third review loop, round 19. Four further supplied findings were all confirmed and fixed in d7e2294, after which codex review (gpt-6-astra, xhigh, read-only) of 6049b529..d7e2294 and a comprehensive --scope branch pass of 454fe46..d7e2294 both reported no actionable findings. The fixture discarded the error that started a teardown: Fixture::create returned the cleanup error in place of the provisioning failure and Fixture::run kept the body error but dropped the cleanup error entirely, so both now report the originating failure with any cleanup failure appended, because a leaked role or schema changes how the next run behaves. The missing-privilege controls executed copied SQL rather than the native entrypoint, so a native query change altering the privileges the real path needs would have left them green; they now drive record_required_job_enqueue_intent, requiring insertion to fail after INSERT (enqueue_request) is revoked and duplicate resolution to fail after UPDATE (id) is revoked, with a prior recording under the same key so that path is reached, and skipping either revocation fails the case. The default-supervisor login selected CatalogSync, which the published worker role omits and no supervisor loop calls; removing it leaves the case passing, which is the evidence it was excess authority able to mask a future dispatch requirement. Both operation enums now name the native entrypoints each group covers and the neighbouring ones it does not, which acceptance criterion 2 promised and the behavioural descriptions did not supply; coverage means the requirements were derived from that entrypoint's statements. A first draft of that mapping was wrong and was corrected before commit: it listed enqueue_job under DirectJobExecution, which holds no INSERT on job_queue and therefore cannot submit work, and it claimed two CatalogSync entrypoints whose SQL had not been read. The residual limitation is that the three documentation repairs in this round have no negative control: the frozen rendering oracles pin the privileges, while nothing pins the documented entrypoint names against future drift. Validation reran bash scripts/verify.sh on the pinned toolchain and the full scripts/sqlx_live.py suite. The comprehensive pass was again a single-reviewer result for the same reason as the earlier two, and it executed no Rust or PostgreSQL test.

2026-10-04 fourth review loop, rounds 20 and 21. Eight further supplied and reviewer findings were confirmed and fixed, taking the total to twenty-one rounds, after which codex review of 6049b529..96a5cb9 and a comprehensive --scope branch pass of 454fe46..96a5cb9 both reported no actionable findings, the latter having inspected the entrypoint mappings across all six Runledger and five Runlimit selections against the native SQL. Round 20 closed four: both supervisor compositions returned from startup and observation failures before awaiting shutdown_report, and because dropping a supervisor only requests shutdown, native tasks ran into the fixture teardown and their failures were lost, so each composition now holds its observation result and always awaits settlement; PgAtomicError's Debug delegates to a Display printing one fixed phrase with the real causes reachable only through Error::source, so flattening it destroyed the storage error and its SQLSTATE, and the callbacks now pass typed errors through while the conversion walks the source chain, making a refused recording report permission denied for table job_enqueue_intents rather than the phrase alone; IntentSubmission omitted the atomic-scope entrypoints the tests exercise while the enum documentation declares unlisted ones unsupported, and now names record_required_job_enqueue_intent, observe_job_enqueue_intent and the shared record_job_enqueue_intent_in_transaction with their contracts distinguished; and docs/status.md named a stale revision. Round 21 closed two reviewer findings in round 20's own error paths: the rollback case matched a bare PgAtomicError::Rejected, which the new CaseRejection variant made unsound because a native failure recording the probe also arrives as Rejected while the absence check then passes trivially, so it now matches Rejected(CaseRejection::Application(..)), and the conflict assertion now asserts the native stable code job.intent_idempotency_conflict after a diagnostic run established that a differing request under an existing key arrives as a classified storage error rather than RequiredIntentError::Conflict; and settlement failures were discarded whenever an observation also failed, so both are now combined and a forced double failure reports the observation error followed by the full settlement report including its per-loop records. Every repair has an executed negative control. Three consecutive rounds found defects in the immediately preceding round's work, all in the live suite's error paths or the entrypoint documentation, which are only visible when something else fails and therefore escape the passing-test signal; the privilege inventories themselves have been clean since round 12. The residual limitation is that the documented entrypoint names have no mechanical check: the frozen rendering oracles pin privileges, nothing pins the names against a future native API change. Validation reran bash scripts/verify.sh on the pinned toolchain and the full scripts/sqlx_live.py suite after each round. Hosted CI passed at 49547a0 (run 37221622716, head SHA verified), covering every round through 21: both verify shards 1.94.0 and 1.98.1, both native Runlimit PostgreSQL shards, both macOS subprocess-harness shards and the repository-policy workflow. A twenty-second round then reconciled docs/status.md, which named d7e2294 while rounds 20 and 21 had changed four live-suite files after it; it now names 96a5cb9, the newest commit changing the suite. That reference has gone stale twice, because every repair round touches the suite and nothing mechanical pins the claim; a guard asserting the named revision is the newest commit touching crates/batter/tests/grants_live/ was deliberately not added, since it would fail any future PR changing the suite before its author reran the live tests and that is a repository-policy decision. The comprehensive pass was again a single-reviewer result and executed no Rust or PostgreSQL test.

title: Reject non-finite Unix process watchdog bounds
description:
## Observed behavior

`scripts/scheduling_process.py::run_process` accepts non-finite `timeout` and
`reap_allowance` values. Its validation checks only `<= 0`, so both positive
infinity and NaN reach deadline arithmetic in `_run_owned_process`,
`Capture.observe_until`, and `_settle`.

On 2026-09-09 on Darwin 25.6.0 arm64 with Python 3.14.7, this repository-root
control returned successful `ProcessOutcome` values instead of raising
`ValueError` for all four cases:

```python
run_process(["/usr/bin/true"], timeout=float("inf"), reap_allowance=1, output_limit=1024)
run_process(["/usr/bin/true"], timeout=float("nan"), reap_allowance=1, output_limit=1024)
run_process(["/usr/bin/true"], timeout=1, reap_allowance=float("inf"), output_limit=1024)
run_process(["/usr/bin/true"], timeout=1, reap_allowance=float("nan"), output_limit=1024)
```

The focused `test_scheduling_process.py` suite passed all 24 tests, confirming
that the current test inventory does not reject these values. The sibling
`parallel_process.run_parallel` already requires finite positive bounds and has
an infinity/NaN regression.

## Expected behavior

The bounded Unix process owner should reject every non-finite or non-positive
duration before launching a child. A malformed bound must not be able to turn a
watchdog or termination/reap allowance into an unbounded wait.

## Affected code and likely impact

- `scripts/scheduling_process.py::run_process` validates `timeout` and
  `reap_allowance` incompletely.
- `_run_owned_process` uses `started + timeout`; `Capture.observe_until` cannot
  reach its `remaining <= 0` exit with infinity or NaN.
- `_settle` similarly derives its cleanup deadline from `reap_allowance`.

This is lower-impact because callers are repository-owned test tools with
normally constant values. If a future CLI/configured caller supplies a
non-finite value, however, a hung child can hang local or CI verification
instead of producing bounded failure evidence.

## Verification limitation

The control used `/usr/bin/true` to prove invalid values are accepted without
deliberately launching a permanently hanging child. It therefore did not wait
through the unbounded failure mode. No Linux, hosted CI, or other Python version
was exercised for this finding.
acceptance_criteria: run_process rejects NaN, infinity, zero, and negative timeout/reap allowances before spawning; focused regressions cover both fields and preserve existing bounded success, timeout, interruption, overflow, and reap behavior.

title: Prove compact verification adoption in a pinned real consumer
description:
## Outcome

Prove the high-level PostgreSQL verification path in one authorized real
same-stack consumer, remove its duplicated generic machinery, and record an
immutable pinned adoption without exposing private provenance in Batter.

## Scope

Implement Milestones 4 through 7 of
`.agent/plans/batter-7r3.6-compact-verification-adoption.md`. Exact consumer paths,
commands, revisions, method/error contracts, and LOC inventories are in the
authorized private companion; keep public upstream scenarios generic.

Before upstream API freeze, use an uncommitted local-path prototype for all four
real profiles. Compare compiled policies to independent pre-existing low-level
oracles and new grant effects to old provisioning-script effects. Delete the
translator and scripts recoverably in the prototype and reject an API that does
not reduce the replacement-inclusive responsibility. Then run Batter's bounded
comprehensive low-severity review-fix loop. Pin only an authorized immutable
remote revision, restore all Git dependencies together, and run the consumer's
independent comprehensive loop.

## Acceptance

- All four profiles are readable grouped application data and one compiled
  representation feeds verification, test provisioning, and deterministic
  render-only operator output.
- Independent low-level policy oracles and old-script semantic controls prove
  the new manifest rather than using it as its own sole oracle.
- Schema, role, and queue public methods, startup order, error categories,
  missing/excess behavior, lock-only columns, routines, sequences, PUBLIC,
  inheritance/SET/ADMIN reachability, ownership, and real business operations
  remain covered.
- The render command runs before ordinary application configuration while
  preserving earlier transport dispatch, performs no external I/O except
  buffered stdout, and uses an explicit transactional `psql -X` workflow whose
  tested failures cannot commit a prefix.
- The generic translator, duplicate queue adapter/catalog checks, and four
  hand-maintained grant scripts are removed, with all live references updated.
- The replacement-inclusive consumer responsibility is strictly smaller than its
  recomputed pre-adoption baseline. Historical measurements, Batter growth,
  tests/docs, and generated SQL are reported separately.
- Both repositories' required local gates and independent comprehensive
  low-severity review-fix loops converge on final fingerprints. An immutable
  upstream revision is remotely resolvable and all consumer Batter pins match it.
- Generic adoption evidence is appended without claiming deployment, hosted CI,
  release, or a second adopter that did not occur.
acceptance_criteria: One authorized real consumer pins an immutable reviewed revision, removes its generic translator/catalog checks and duplicate grant scripts, preserves independently characterized behavior, passes both comprehensive low-severity review-fix loops and all required gates, and demonstrates replacement-inclusive downstream code reduction.
